He previously served as an assistant coach for the [[New York Jets]], [[Buffalo Bills]], and [[Cleveland Browns]], as well as the defensive coordinator for the [[Houston Texans]] and the [[Miami Dolphins]]. Weaver was a [[college football]] [[defensive end]] at [[Notre Dame Fighting Irish football|Notre Dame]] and was drafted by the Ravens in the second round of the [[2002 NFL draft]]. He also previously played for the Texans. ==Early life== Weaver was born in [[Abilene, Texas]] on July 28, 1980. '''Antonio Bryant''' (born March 9, 1981) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[wide receiver]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Pittsburgh Panthers football|Pittsburgh Panthers]], earning consensus [[College Football All-America Team|All-American]] honors and winning the [[Fred Biletnikoff Award]]. Bryant was selected by the [[Dallas Cowboys]] in the second round of the [[2002 NFL draft]], and also played professionally for the [[Cleveland Browns]], [[San Francisco 49ers]], and [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]] of the NFL.

==Early life==
Bryant was born in [[Miami, Florida]] and graduated from [[Miami Northwestern High School]], where he was a standout [[high school football]] player for the Bulls.<ref>{{Cite news |url=http://www.maxpreps.com/news/rtk0-D08zUqiamc4NnPQ_w/high-schools-that-have-produced-the-most-nfl-draft-picks.htm |title=High schools that have produced the most NFL draft picks - MaxPreps |date=May 15, 2014 |work=MaxPreps.com |access-date=October 11, 2018 |language=en-US}}</ref> He was selected as a team captain in three straight years and helped lead his team as a senior to a Class 6A state title and an undefeated record (16–0).

==College career==
Bryant attended the University of Pittsburgh, and played for the [[Pittsburgh Panthers football]] team from 1999 to 2001.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Antonio Bryant College Stats, School, Draft, Gamelog, Splits |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/antonio-bryant-1.html |access-date=2024-07-24 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> He was a first-team All-[[Big East Conference (1979–2013)|Big East]] selection in 2000 and 2001, and was recognized as a consensus first-team All-American as a sophomore in 2000.<ref>''2011 NCAA Football Records Book'', [http://fs.ncaa.org/Docs/stats/football_records/2011/Awards.pdf  Award Winners], National Collegiate Athletic Association, Indianapolis, Indiana, p. 11 (2011).  Retrieved June 24, 2012.</ref>  He also won the [[Fred Biletnikoff Award]] as the season's outstanding college football receiver in 2000; he was the second sophomore to win the award (after [[Randy Moss]]). He declared for the [[NFL draft]] after his junior year, leaving as the conference's record holder for regular-season touchdowns (26) and 100-yard receiving games (13).<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/conferences/big-east/leaders/rec-td-player-career.html |title=Big East Conference Career Leaders and Records for Receiving Touchdowns |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en |access-date=October 11, 2018}}</ref>

===Dallas Cowboys===

====2002 season====
Bryant was selected by the [[Dallas Cowboys]] in the second round (63rd overall) of the [[2002 NFL draft]], after dropping because of character concerns.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2002/draft.htm |title=2002 NFL Draft Listing |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |access-date=October 11, 2018}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Aron |first=Jamie |date=September 14, 2002|agency=Associated Press |title=Former Pitt star grabs starting job with Cowboys |url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?nid=1129&dat=20020914&id=UvBRAAAAIBAJ&sjid=YXADAAAAIBAJ&pg=6688,1563160&hl=es |access-date=February 19, 2016 |website=Pittsburgh Post-Gazette|via=Google News}}</ref> He was given number 88 with the expectation of developing into a great player and was the first rookie [[wide receiver]] to start in a season opener since [[Michael Irvin]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=October 17, 2002 |title=Productive rookie making big catches for Cowboys |url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?nid=861&dat=20021017&id=9BdZAAAAIBAJ&sjid=eEYNAAAAIBAJ&pg=1852,3827964&hl=es |access-date=February 19, 2016 |website=The Victoria Advocate|agency=Associated Press|via=Google News}}</ref> At the time, his 44 receptions ranked third, his 733 receiving yards ranked fourth and his 6 [[touchdown]] receptions ranked second all-time for a Cowboys rookie in a season.{{citation needed|date=December 2024}} On October 13, he had his signature moment against the [[Carolina Panthers]] on a 4th and 14, last minute game-winning acrobatic [[touchdown]] reception from quarterback [[Quincy Carter]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Carolina Panthers at Dallas Cowboys - October 13th, 2002 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200210130dal.htm |access-date=2026-05-10 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=XOmPgGZSduo |title=Quincy Carter to Antonio Bryant Game Winning TD |publisher=YouTube |access-date=January 3, 2022}}</ref> In Week 17, he had seven receptions for 170 yards and a touchdown in a 20–14 loss to Washington.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Dallas Cowboys at Washington Redskins - December 29th, 2002 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200212290was.htm |access-date=2026-05-17 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> As a rookie, he finished with 44 receptions for 733 yards and six touchdowns.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Antonio Bryant 2002 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/B/BryaAn00/gamelog/2002/ |access-date=2026-05-14 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> He was named to the PFWA All-Rookie Team.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2002 NFL All-Rookie Team |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/awards/nfl-all-rookie-2002.htm |access-date=2026-05-14 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

====2003 season====
In [[2003 NFL season|2003]], Bryant was moved to third [[wide receiver|receiver]] after [[Terry Glenn]] was signed as a [[free agent]]. He finished the 2003 season with 39 receptions for 550 yards and two touchdowns.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Antonio Bryant 2003 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/B/BryaAn00/gamelog/2003/ |access-date=2026-05-14 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

====2004 season====
In [[2004 NFL season|2004]], the arrival of [[free agent]] [[Keyshawn Johnson]] started to affect his attitude. During a [[mini-camp]] practice after being unsatisfied with the number of reps he had, he started cursing and threw his jersey aiming at [[Bill Parcells]] head, before the team broke up the fight. Although Parcells gave him a second chance, tensions kept escalating from that point forward. He was eventually traded to the [[Cleveland Browns]] after the fifth game of the season, in exchange for [[wide receiver]] [[Quincy Morgan]], who also had issues with his team.<ref>{{cite web | last=McManus | first=Tim | title=Receiver shift: Cowboys trade Bryant to Browns | website=ESPN.com | date=2004-10-19 | url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/news/story?id=1905409 | access-date=2024-07-24}}</ref> 

===Cleveland Browns===
In Week 12 of the 2004 season, Bryant had eight receptions for 131 yards and two touchdowns in a 58–48 loss to the Cincinnati Bengals.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Cleveland Browns at Cincinnati Bengals - November 28th, 2004 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200411280cin.htm |access-date=2026-05-17 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> In Week 13, he had seven receptions for 115 yards and two touchdowns in a 42–15 loss to the New England Patriots.<ref>{{Cite web |title=New England Patriots at Cleveland Browns - December 5th, 2004 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200412050cle.htm |access-date=2026-05-17 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> He finished the 2004 season with 58 receptions for 812 yards and four touchdowns.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Antonio Bryant 2004 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/B/BryaAn00/gamelog/2004/ |access-date=2026-05-14 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

In Week 17 of the 2005 season, Bryant had nine receptions for 123 yards and a touchdown in the 20–16 loss to the Baltimore Ravens.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Baltimore Ravens at Cleveland Browns - January 1st, 2006 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200601010cle.htm |access-date=2026-05-17 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> In [[2005 NFL season|2005]], Bryant led the Browns in catches (69), receiving yards (1,009 yards) and touchdowns (four).<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/teams/cle/2005.htm |title=2005 Cleveland Browns Statistics & Players |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |access-date=October 11, 2018}}</ref> He became a free agent at the end of the year.

===San Francisco 49ers===
Bryant signed as a free agent with the [[San Francisco 49ers]] in [[2006 NFL season|2006]]. In Week 2, against the St. Louis Rams, he had four receptions for 131 yards and one touchdown in the 20–13 win.<ref>{{Cite web |title=St. Louis Rams at San Francisco 49ers - September 17th, 2006 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200609170sfo.htm |access-date=2026-05-17 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> On December 22, 2006, he was suspended four games for violating the NFL's substance abuse policy.<ref>{{cite web |author=Pasquarelli |first=Len |author-link=Len Pasquarelli |date=December 22, 2006 |title=Bryant suspended for violating substance abuse policy |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/news/story?id=2706588 |accessdate=June 13, 2024 |publisher=[[ESPN]]}}</ref> He finished the 2006 season with 40 receptions for 733 yards and three touchdowns.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Antonio Bryant 2006 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/B/BryaAn00/gamelog/2006/ |access-date=2026-05-14 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> On March 1, [[2007 NFL season|2007]], he was released one year after he signed a four-year, $14 million contract.<ref name="espn.com">{{cite web |date=October 27, 2007 |title=Ex-49ers receiver Bryant files motion over drug testing |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/news/story?id=3081855 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071027150009/http://sports.espn.go.com/nfl/news/story?id=3081855 |archive-date=October 27, 2007 |access-date=October 27, 2007 |work=ESPN.com|agency=Associated Press}}</ref>

===Free agency===
On September 17, [[2007 NFL season|2007]], Bryant was reinstated by the league, but was not able to sign with a team, partly because of a failed drug test over the summer. In October, he filed a lawsuit against the NFL to try to get them to stop drug testing him since he was not a player at the time, and to drop the failed drug test.<ref name="espn.com"/> In December, the case was resolved without the details being released.<ref name="f676">{{cite web | last=McManus | first=Tim | title=Ex-Niner Bryant gets resolution in lawsuit vs. NFL | website=ESPN.com | date=2007-12-12 | url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/news/story?id=3150947&campaign=rss&source=NFLHeadlines | access-date=2024-07-24}}</ref>

===Tampa Bay Buccaneers===
After not playing the previous year, on March 10, [[2008 NFL season|2008]], Bryant signed a deal for the veteran minimum with the [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]]. He had a career game against the [[Carolina Panthers]] in Week 14, finishing with nine receptions for 200 yards, including a one-handed touchdown catch dubbed "catch of the year".<ref>{{cite web | last=Smith | first=Scott | title=Top Five Receiving Performances in Bucs History | website=Buccaneers.com| date=May 27, 2025 | url=https://www.buccaneers.com/news/top-five-receiving-performances-bucs-history-50-seasons | access-date=May 14, 2026}}</ref> Despite his performance, the Buccaneers lost 38–23.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Carolina Panthers - December 8th, 2008 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200812080car.htm |access-date=2026-05-17 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> In Week 16, he had six receptions for 127 yards and a touchdown in the 41–24 loss to the San Diego Chargers.<ref>{{Cite web |title=San Diego Chargers at Tampa Bay Buccaneers - December 21st, 2008 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200812210tam.htm |access-date=2026-05-17 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> Bryant finished his best season as a professional with 83 catches for 1,248 yards and seven touchdowns while averaging 15 yards per catch.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Antonio Bryant 2008 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/B/BryaAn00/gamelog/2008/ |access-date=2026-05-14 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> He became the team's leading receiver and the second player in franchise history to record three or more consecutive 100-yard receiving games. On February 18, [[2009 NFL season|2009]], he was given the [[franchise tag]] by the Buccaneers.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.tampabay.com/sports/football/bucs/article977564.ece |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090223145350/http://www.tampabay.com/sports/football/bucs/article977564.ece |url-status=dead |archive-date=February 23, 2009 | newspaper=St. Petersburg Times | title=Tampa Bay Buccaneers receiver Antonio Bryant 'not happy or pleased' with franchise player tag, agent says | first1=Rick | last1=Stroud | first2=Stephen F. | last2=Holder | name-list-style=amp | date=February 20, 2009 }}</ref> In the 2009 season, he finished with 39 receptions for 600 yards and four touchdowns.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Antonio Bryant 2009 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/B/BryaAn00/gamelog/2009/ |access-date=2026-05-14 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> On February 25, [[2010 NFL season|2010]], he was waived after a somewhat disappointing and injury-plagued season.{{Citation needed|date=February 2021}}

===Cincinnati Bengals===
After finishing an injury-plagued season and coming off surgery to repair cartilage damage in his left knee, the [[Cincinnati Bengals]] signed Bryant on March 10, [[2010 NFL season|2010]], to a four-year contract worth a reported $28 million, along with multiple incentives.<ref>{{Cite web |date=March 12, 2010 |title=Bryant signs four-year contract, wants to further Bengals' success |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/bryant-signs-four-year-contract-wants-to-further-bengals-succes-09000d5d816ea0ed |access-date=May 10, 2026 |website=NFL.com}}</ref>

After the Bengals signed [[Terrell Owens]], Bryant gave up his No. 81 jersey for Owens, who had worn the number his entire career.  In return for the number, Bryant requested Owens make a donation to his charity and wore jersey No. 19 instead.<ref name="sports.espn.go.com">{{Cite web |date=2010-07-29 |title=Owens finally shows at Bengals camp, practices |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/trainingcamp10/news/story?id=5419405 |access-date=2024-12-26 |website=ESPN.com|agency=Associated Press |language=en}}</ref> After struggling in practices and not being able to play in any of the pre-season games because of problems with his left knee, the Bengals released him on August 29.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/trainingcamp10/news/story?id=5509631 |title=Antonio Bryant cut by Cincinnati Bengals after struggling in camp despite $8 million guaranteed - ESPN |last=Walker |first=James |date=August 30, 2010 |work=ESPN.com |access-date=July 23, 2012}}</ref>

===Seattle Seahawks===
On June 12, [[2012 NFL season|2012]], Bryant worked out for the [[Seattle Seahawks]] by attending their three-day mini-camp and took a physical for the team as well.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Rosenthal |first=Gregg |date=June 12, 2012 |title=Antonio Bryant gets another shot with Seahawks |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/antonio-bryant-gets-another-shot-with-seahawks-09000d5d829c1869 |access-date=March 20, 2026 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> On June 15, 2012, it was reported that he finished all three of the minicamp practices, indicating that his chronic knee injury had healed.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Sessler |first=Marc |date=June 15, 2012 |title=Pete Carroll: Antonio Bryant 'not in very good shape' |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/pete-carroll-antonio-bryant-not-in-very-good-shape-09000d5d829dc130 |access-date=March 20, 2026 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> After being out of football for two years, Bryant signed with the Seahawks on July 26.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2012-07-27 |title=Seattle signs WR Antonio Bryant to active roster |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story?id=8204371&src=desktop |access-date=2024-12-26 |website=ESPN.com|agency=Associated Press |language=en}}</ref> His stay with the team was short lived, as he was released on August 5.<ref>{{Cite web |date=August 5, 2012 |title=Seahawks release Antonio Bryant |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/profootballtalk/rumor-mill/news/seahawks-release-antonio-bryant |access-date=March 6, 2024 |website=NBC Sports |language=en-US}}</ref>

'''Antonio Ethan Gates Jr.''' (born June 18, 1980) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who spent his entire 16-year career as a [[tight end]] for the [[San Diego Chargers|San Diego]] / [[Los Angeles Chargers]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL) from 2003 to 2018. He was named to the [[Pro Bowl]] eight times and was a six-time [[All-Pro]] selection. Gates was inducted to the [[Pro Football Hall of Fame]] in 2025. 

Gates was signed as an [[undrafted free agent]] in 2003 after playing [[college basketball]] for the [[Kent State Golden Flashes men's basketball|Kent State Golden Flashes]]. He attended college at [[Kent State University]] in his junior and senior years after brief stints at [[Michigan State University]] and [[Eastern Michigan University]].<ref name="DraftDay">{{Cite web |year=2003 |title=Antonio Gates |url=http://www.draftdaypicks.com/Antonio_Gates.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120125024102/http://www.draftdaypicks.com/Antonio_Gates.html |archive-date=January 25, 2012 |access-date=February 23, 2011 |website=Draft Day Picks}}</ref> He is the Chargers' career leader in receiving yards and receiving [[touchdown]]s.<ref name="gehlken_12292014">{{Cite web |last=Gehlken |first=Michael |date=December 29, 2014 |title=Antonio Gates ends year with milestone |url=https://www.sandiegouniontribune.com/2014/12/29/antonio-gates-ends-year-with-milestone/ |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://archive.today/20141230083717/http://www.utsandiego.com/news/2014/dec/29/antonio-gates-record-sister-pamela/all/?print |archive-date=December 30, 2014 |access-date=June 14, 2026 |website=U-T San Diego}}</ref> In 2015, he became the second tight end and ninth player overall to record 100 career touchdown receptions.<ref>{{Cite magazine |date=October 12, 2015 |title=Antonio Gates catches his 100th career touchdown |url=https://www.si.com/nfl/2015/10/12/san-diego-chargers-antonio-gates-100th-career-touchdown |access-date=April 18, 2023 |magazine=Sports Illustrated |archive-date=June 29, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180629102413/https://www.si.com/nfl/2015/10/12/san-diego-chargers-antonio-gates-100th-career-touchdown |url-status=live }}</ref> He ranks seventh in [[List of National Football League career receiving touchdowns leaders|career touchdown receptions]], with 116, and leads all tight ends in NFL history. ==Early life==
Antonio Ethan Gates Jr. was born on June 18, 1980,<ref name="pfr"/> in [[Detroit]], Michigan.<ref name=miller_01142020/> He wore a [[shoe size|size]] 12 shoe by [[sixth grade]] and stood {{convert|6|ft|3|in}} entering [[high school]].<ref name=krasovic_12022016>{{cite news|first=Tom|last=Krasovic|title=Antonio Gates as 6-9 NBA star? NFL pass-rusher?|date=December 2, 2016|newspaper=The San Diego Union-Tribune|url=https://www.sandiegouniontribune.com/2016/12/01/antonio-gates-as-6-9-nba-star-nfl-pass-rusher/|access-date=April 14, 2025}}</ref> Gates played [[high school football]] and [[high school basketball|basketball]] at [[Central High School (Detroit)|Central High School]].<ref name="Stack">{{Cite web |last=Clark |first=Zac |date=March 1, 2011 |title=Antonio Gates: A Recruiting Story Like No Other |url=http://www.stack.com/a/antonio-gates-a-recruiting-story-like-no-other |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181023123633/http://www.stack.com/a/antonio-gates-a-recruiting-story-like-no-other |archive-date=October 23, 2018 |access-date=October 17, 2018 |website=Stack.com |language=en}}</ref> As a [[freshman]], he led their basketball team in scoring.<ref name=krasovic_12022016/>

==College career==
Gates played basketball rather than football in college.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Antonio Gates College Stats |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/antonio-gates-1.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221006000316/https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/antonio-gates-1.html |archive-date=October 6, 2022 |access-date=2025-01-22 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en}}</ref><ref name="miller_01142020">{{Cite web |last=Miller |first=Jeff |date=January 14, 2020 |title=Chargers great Antonio Gates announces his retirement |url=https://www.sandiegouniontribune.com/sports/chargers-rams/story/2020-01-14/chargers-great-antonio-gates-announces-his-retirement |access-date=January 17, 2020 |website=San Diego Union Tribune |archive-date=January 28, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210128100922/https://www.sandiegouniontribune.com/sports/chargers-rams/story/2020-01-14/chargers-great-antonio-gates-announces-his-retirement |url-status=live }}</ref> He originally enrolled at [[Michigan State University]] wanting to play football under then-coach [[Nick Saban]] as well as basketball under coach [[Tom Izzo]]. Upon enrolling, he learned that Saban wanted him to play only football.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Neumann |first=Thomas |date=December 15, 2010 |title=Neumann: Q&A with Chargers TE Antonio Gates |url=https://www.espn.com/espn/page2/story?page=neumann/101215_antonio_gates_chargers_tight_end&sportCat=nfl |access-date=April 18, 2023 |website=ESPN.com |archive-date=November 13, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141113063215/http://sports.espn.go.com/espn/page2/story?page=neumann/101215_antonio_gates_chargers_tight_end&sportCat=nfl |url-status=live }}</ref> Moreover, the coach wanted to move him to defense as a [[defensive end]] or [[linebacker]].<ref name=krasovic_12022016/> Gates then chose to pursue playing basketball by transferring to [[Eastern Michigan Eagles men's basketball|Eastern Michigan University]]. He played there part of a season before transferring to the [[College of the Sequoias]], a junior college in California, to focus on academics. Recruited by [[Stan Heath]], Gates transferred to [[Kent State University]] in northeastern Ohio.<ref name="Stack" />

As a member of the Golden Flashes, Gates played two seasons as [[power forward]]. In his junior season he averaged 16.0 points, 8.1 rebounds and 2.7 assists per game.<ref name="Kent State">{{Cite web |title=Antonio Gates |url=http://dept.kent.edu/athletics/mbasketball/mbbio/gates.htm |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20030527225636/http://dept.kent.edu/athletics/mbasketball/mbbio/gates.htm |archive-date=May 27, 2003 |website=Kent State Golden Flashes Athletics}}</ref> His junior season his team won its first regular season [[Mid-American Conference]] (MAC) championship in school history after finishing the regular season with a 24–5 overall record with a 17–1 record in the MAC.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2001–02 Men's Mid-American Conference Season Summary |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/conferences/mac/men/2002.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230409221708/https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/conferences/mac/men/2002.html |archive-date=April 9, 2023 |access-date=April 19, 2023 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=2001–02 Kent State Golden Flashes Men 's Roster and Stats |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/schools/kent-state/men/2002.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230417044528/https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/schools/kent-state/men/2002.html |archive-date=April 17, 2023 |access-date=April 19, 2023 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> Gates helped the Golden Flashes win their second consecutive MAC tournament and earn its resulting berth in the [[2002 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament|2002 NCAA Tournament]]. In the tournament, he gave crucial performances that helped Kent State reach the [[Elite Eight]] as a 10 seed by upsetting 7 seed Oklahoma State (69–61), 2 seed Alabama (71–58) and 3 seed Pittsburgh (78–73).<ref>{{Cite web |title=2002 Men's NCAA Tournament Summary |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/postseason/men/2002-ncaa.html |access-date=April 19, 2023 |website=College Basketball at Sports-Reference.com |language=en |archive-date=April 13, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230413164944/https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/postseason/men/2002-ncaa.html |url-status=live }}</ref> He was named second-team All-MAC for the 2002 season.<ref name="Cbb">{{cite web | url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/antonio-gates-1.html | title=Antonio Gates | publisher=[[Sports Reference]] | accessdate=13 April 2025}}</ref>

As a senior, Gates received honorable mention [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]] honors from the [[Associated Press]] after averaging 20.6 points, 7.7 rebounds, and 4.1 assists per game. He finished with a record of 54–16 in two years of playing.<ref name="Kent_State">{{Cite web |date=February 24, 2010 |title=Kent State to Retire Antonio Gates' No. 44 on Saturday |url=http://www.kent.edu/news/newsdetail.cfm?customel_datapageid_9299%3D1935765 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110719222536/http://www.kent.edu/news/newsdetail.cfm?customel_datapageid_9299=1935765 |archive-date=July 19, 2011 |access-date=April 14, 2011 |website=Kent State University}}</ref> He also earned first-team All-MAC recognition in 2003.<ref name="Cbb"/>

His jersey number, 44, was retired on February 27, 2010, making him just the fourth Golden Flash to receive the honor.<ref>{{Cite web |date=January 14, 2020 |title=Former Kent State basketball star Antonio Gates retires from NFL as record-setting tight end |url=https://www.beaconjournal.com/story/sports/college/basketball/2020/01/14/former-kent-state-basketball-star/1899568007/ |access-date=April 19, 2023 |website=Akron Beacon Journal |language=en-US |archive-date=April 19, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230419012907/https://www.beaconjournal.com/story/sports/college/basketball/2020/01/14/former-kent-state-basketball-star/1899568007/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

==Professional career==
After being told by scouts that he was too much of a "[[Tweener (basketball)|tweener]]" to make the [[National Basketball Association|NBA]], Gates ({{convert|6|ft|4|in}}) arranged a workout in front of [[National Football League|NFL]] scouts. Despite never having played college football,<ref>{{Cite news |last=Mihoces |first=Gary |date=April 20, 2005 |title=NFL seeks best players on the court or mat |work=[[USA Today]] |url=http://usatoday30.usatoday.com/sports/football/2005draft/2005-04-20-no-college-experience_x.htm |url-status=live |access-date=October 28, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131029210147/http://usatoday30.usatoday.com/sports/football/2005draft/2005-04-20-no-college-experience_x.htm |archive-date=October 29, 2013}}</ref> as many as 19 teams were believed to have contacted Gates about a tryout.  Gates chose to work out first for the San Diego Chargers. Recognizing his potential, the Chargers immediately signed him to a contract as an [[undrafted free agent]].

===2003===
Lost in the disappointment of San Diego's league-worst 4–12 record was Gates' rise from third string to starter.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2003 San Diego Chargers Rosters, Stats, Schedule, Team Draftees |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/teams/sdg/2003.htm |access-date=April 18, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |archive-date=July 15, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190715173924/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/teams/sdg/2003.htm |url-status=live }}</ref> He made his first catch in week 4 against the [[2003 Oakland Raiders season|Oakland Raiders]], scored his first touchdown in week 10 against the [[2003 Minnesota Vikings season|Minnesota Vikings]], and enjoyed his first 100-yard receiving game (117 yards) against the [[2003 Green Bay Packers season|Green Bay Packers]] in week 15.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Green Bay Packers at San Diego Chargers – December 14th, 2003 ===2008===
[[File:AntonioGatesByPhilKonstantin.jpg|thumb|Gates in 2008]]
Gates said he was leaning toward having surgery to repair a dislocated left big toe that slowed his performance during the [[2007–08 NFL playoffs]], but was undecided on whether to have surgery or not, "There is higher chance I'm going to have surgery". Gates also pulled out of his fifth Pro Bowl selection<ref>{{Cite web |title=2008 NFL Pro Bowlers |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2008/probowl.htm |access-date=April 18, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |archive-date=March 16, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180316160330/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2008/probowl.htm |url-status=live }}</ref> because of his injuries alongside his teammate LaDainian Tomlinson. Gates finished the season with 60 receptions for 704 yards and eight touchdowns.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Antonio Gates 2008 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/G/GateAn00/gamelog/2008/ |access-date=April 18, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |archive-date=October 7, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221007091422/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/G/GateAn00/gamelog/2008/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

On February 23, 2008, Gates said he would have foot surgery to fix the injury that had slowed him in the final part of the season.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kleiss |first=Peter |date=August 17, 2011 |title=San Diego Chargers: Will Antonio Gates' Plantar Fascia Ever Heal? |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/809171-san-diego-chargers-will-antonio-gates-plantar-fascia-ever-heal#:~:text=In%2520February%2520of%25202008%252C%2520Gates,704%2520yards%2520and%2520eight%2520touchdowns. |access-date=April 18, 2023 |website=Bleacher Report |language=en-US |archive-date=September 2, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120902042337/http://bleacherreport.com/articles/809171-san-diego-chargers-will-antonio-gates-plantar-fascia-ever-heal#:~:text=In%2520February%2520of%25202008%252C%2520Gates,704%2520yards%2520and%2520eight%2520touchdowns. |url-status=live }}</ref> He would face a 4–6 month recovery time. Gates seemed questionable for week 1 and even sounded worried about his status for the opening day of the [[2008 San Diego Chargers season|2008 season]]; however, he ended up playing every game despite complaints that his toe was bothering him during the first half of the season.{{Citation needed|date=October 2020}}

Finally healthy after consecutive injury-plagued seasons, Gates enjoyed the most productive year of his career. He caught 79 passes for a career-high 1,157 yards and eight touchdowns.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Antonio Gates 2009 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/G/GateAn00/gamelog/2009/ |access-date=April 18, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |archive-date=October 3, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221003064345/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/G/GateAn00/gamelog/2009/ |url-status=live }}</ref> He was named to his sixth consecutive Pro Bowl.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2009 NFL Pro Bowlers |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2009/probowl.htm |access-date=April 18, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |archive-date=August 21, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180821031640/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2009/probowl.htm |url-status=live }}</ref>

The team finished the year with 13 wins, one of the best records of the year.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2009 NFL Standings & Team Stats |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2009/index.htm |access-date=April 18, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |archive-date=March 21, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190321050728/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2009/index.htm |url-status=live }}</ref> However, they were eliminated in their first postseason game by the [[2009 New York Jets season|New York Jets]] in the [[2009–10 NFL playoffs#AFC: New York Jets 17, San Diego Chargers 14|Divisional Round]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Divisional Round – New York Jets at San Diego Chargers – January 17th, 2010 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201001170sdg.htm |access-date=April 18, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |archive-date=November 13, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121113163225/http://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201001170sdg.htm |url-status=live }}</ref>

===2011===
Gates tried to play through his chronic foot problems but was forced to sit out Weeks 3–5.<ref>{{Cite web |last=McIntyre |first=Brian |date=September 25, 2011 |title=Antonio Gates Status Update: Out With Foot Injury, According To Report |url=https://www.sbnation.com/fantasy/2011/9/25/2445671/antonio-gates-fantasy-status-injury-san-diego-chargers |access-date=April 18, 2023 |website=SBNation.com |language=en |archive-date=December 28, 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111228143409/http://www.sbnation.com/fantasy/2011/9/25/2445671/antonio-gates-fantasy-status-injury-san-diego-chargers |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=October 1, 2011 |title=Gates inactive again for Bolts with foot injury |url=https://www.columbian.com/news/2011/oct/01/gates-inactive-again-for-bolts-with-foot-injury/ |access-date=April 18, 2023 |website=The Columbian |language=en-US |archive-date=April 19, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230419012902/https://www.columbian.com/news/2011/oct/01/gates-inactive-again-for-bolts-with-foot-injury/ |url-status=live }}</ref> He came back after the bye week and started every game the rest of the way. In week 14, against the [[2011 Buffalo Bills season|Buffalo Bills]], he had two receiving touchdowns in the 37–10 victory.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Buffalo Bills at San Diego Chargers – December 11th, 2011 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201112110sdg.htm |access-date=April 18, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |archive-date=November 18, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221118173849/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201112110sdg.htm |url-status=live }}</ref> He finished with more than 60 catches (64) for the seventh time in his career. He also scored seven touchdowns and was voted into his eighth Pro Bowl.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Antonio Gates 2011 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/G/GateAn00/gamelog/2011/ |access-date=April 18, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |archive-date=October 7, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221007184520/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/G/GateAn00/gamelog/2011/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=2011 NFL Pro Bowlers |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2011/probowl.htm |access-date=April 18, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |archive-date=August 30, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180830174119/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2011/probowl.htm |url-status=live }}</ref> Gates became the Chargers' all-time receptions leader on a six-yard catch on a fourth-and-5, early in the fourth quarter against [[2011 Detroit Lions|Detroit]]. It was his 587th career catch, surpassing [[Charlie Joiner]]'s 586.<ref>{{Cite web |date=December 8, 2016 |title=The Right Combination for Antonio Gates |url=https://www.chargers.com/news/the-right-combination-for-antonio-gates-143644 |access-date=April 18, 2023 |website=Chargers.com |language=en-US |archive-date=December 5, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221205133710/https://www.chargers.com/news/the-right-combination-for-antonio-gates-143644 |url-status=live }}</ref>

===2012===
In week 6, Gates had two receiving touchdowns in a 35–24 loss to the [[2012 Denver Broncos season|Denver Broncos]], on a night where the Chargers held a 24–0 halftime lead.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Denver Broncos at San Diego Chargers – October 15th, 2012 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201210150sdg.htm |access-date=April 18, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |archive-date=August 12, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210812181944/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201210150sdg.htm |url-status=live }}</ref> Gates had another record-breaking season, becoming the fifth tight end in NFL history with 600 career catches and runner-up for most touchdowns in Chargers franchise history with 83.{{citation needed|date=April 2023}} The tight end and his quarterback Philip Rivers connected for a total of 56 touchdown catches, the most out of any quarterback-tight end combination in the NFL.{{Citation needed|date=October 2020}} He was ranked 73rd by his fellow players on the [[NFL Top 100 Players of 2013]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=2013 NFL Top 100 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/awards/2013-nfl-top-100.htm |access-date=April 18, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |archive-date=May 27, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220527175924/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/awards/2013-nfl-top-100.htm |url-status=live }}</ref>

===2013===

On September 2, 2018, Gates re-signed with the [[Los Angeles Chargers]] following an injury to Hunter Henry.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Henne |first=Ricky |date=September 2, 2018 |title=He's Back! Antonio Gates Returns to Chargers |url=https://www.chargers.com/news/he-s-back-antonio-gates-returns-to-chargers |access-date=April 18, 2023 |website=Chargers.com |archive-date=April 3, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230403232400/https://www.chargers.com/news/he-s-back-antonio-gates-returns-to-chargers |url-status=live }}</ref> In week 4, against the [[2018 San Francisco 49ers|San Francisco 49ers]], he scored his first receiving touchdown of the season.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Posey |first=Kyle |date=October 1, 2018 |title=Antonio Gates makes history against 49ers |url=https://chargerswire.usatoday.com/2018/10/01/antonio-gates-makes-history-against-49ers/ |access-date=October 17, 2018 |website=USA Today |language=en-US |archive-date=October 17, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181017203422/https://chargerswire.usatoday.com/2018/10/01/antonio-gates-makes-history-against-49ers/ |url-status=live }}</ref> He finished the 2018 season with 28 receptions for 333 receiving yards and two receiving touchdowns in 16 games and one start.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Antonio Gates 2018 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/G/GateAn00/gamelog/2018/ |access-date=April 18, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |archive-date=October 3, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221003175224/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/G/GateAn00/gamelog/2018/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

In what would be his final NFL game, Gates recorded a receiving touchdown in the 41–28 loss to the [[2018 New England Patriots season|New England Patriots]] in the [[2018–19 NFL playoffs#AFC: New England Patriots 41, Los Angeles Chargers 28|Divisional Round]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Divisional Round – Los Angeles Chargers at New England Patriots – January 13th, 2019 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201901130nwe.htm |access-date=April 18, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |archive-date=February 2, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190202042131/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201901130nwe.htm |url-status=live }}</ref>

===Retirement===
Gates announced his retirement on January 14, 2020.<ref name="Retirement">{{Cite web |last=Patra |first=Kevin |date=January 14, 2020 |title=Chargers TE Antonio Gates announces retirement |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/chargers-te-antonio-gates-announces-retirement-0ap3000001096657 |access-date=April 18, 2023 |website=NFL.com |archive-date=February 29, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200229130910/http://www.nfl.com/news/story/0ap3000001096657/article/chargers-te-antonio-gates-announces-retirement |url-status=live }}</ref> He ended his career with a record 116 touchdown catches by a tight end, including 89 thrown by Rivers for the most ever by a quarterback–tight end duo at the time.<ref>{{Cite web |date=November 16, 2021 |title=The Best Quarterback-Tight End Combo of All Time |url=https://www.chargers.com/news/best-quarterback-tight-end-combo |access-date=April 18, 2023 |website=Chargers.com |language=en-US |archive-date=September 27, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220927120442/https://www.chargers.com/news/best-quarterback-tight-end-combo |url-status=live }}</ref> He also finished as the Chargers' franchise leader in receptions (955) and receiving yards (11,841).<ref name="San Diego/Los Angeles Chargers Career Receiving Leaders" />

In 2020, Gates announced he was joining the [[Los Angeles Chargers]] front office as Legends Ambassador.<ref>{{Cite web |date=January 14, 2020 |title=Chargers legend Antonio Gates announces retirement |url=https://www.sportsnet.ca/football/nfl/chargers-legend-antonio-gates-announces-retirement/ |access-date=April 18, 2023 |website=Sportsnet.ca |agency=Associated Press |archive-date=April 3, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230403235530/https://www.sportsnet.ca/football/nfl/chargers-legend-antonio-gates-announces-retirement/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

([[Los Angeles|Los Angeles, California]]) | college = [[Cincinnati Bearcats football|Cincinnati]] | undraftedyear = 2002 | pastteams = * [[San Francisco 49ers]] ({{NFL Year|2002}})* * [[Chicago Rush]] ({{AFL Year|2002}}–{{AFL Year|2003}}) * [[Green Bay Packers]] ({{NFL Year|2003}}–{{NFL Year|2005}}) * [[Cincinnati Bengals]] ({{NFL Year|2006}}–{{NFL Year|2009}}) * [[Sacramento Mountain Lions]] ({{UFL Year|2010}}) | highlights = * Second-team [[All-Arena]] ([[2003 All-Arena Team|2003]]) | statlabel1 = [[Reception (American football)|Receptions]] | statvalue1 = 114 | statlabel2 = [[Receiving yards]] | statvalue2 = 1,160 | statlabel3 = [[Touchdown|Receiving touchdowns]] | statvalue3 = 6 | statlabel4 = [[Return yards]] | statvalue4 = 2,809 | statlabel5 = [[Touchdown|Return touchdowns]] | statvalue5 = 1 }} '''Antonio Tavaras Chatman''' (born February 12, 1979) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[wide receiver]] and [[punt returner]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Cincinnati Bearcats football|Cincinnati Bearcats]] and was signed by the [[San Francisco 49ers]] as an [[undrafted free agent]] in 2002. Chatman also played for the [[Chicago Rush]], [[Green Bay Packers]] and [[Cincinnati Bengals]]. ==College career== Chatman was born in [[Jackson, Alabama]] and attended the [[Susan Miller Dorsey High School]] in [[Los Angeles, California]].{{cite web|url=http://www.databasefootball.com/players/playerpage.htm?ilkid=CHATMANT01 |title=Antonio Chatman |publisher=databaseFootball.com |accessdate=October 19, 2012 |url-status=usurped |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20121017071408/http://databasefootball.com/players/playerpage.htm?ilkid=CHATMANT01 |archivedate=October 17, 2012 }} He attended [[El Camino College]]{{cite web|url=http://www.databasefootball.com/players/playerpage.htm?ilkid=CHATMANT01 |title=Antonio Chatman |publisher=databaseFootball.com |accessdate=October 19, 2012 |url-status=usurped |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20121017071408/http://databasefootball.com/players/playerpage.htm?ilkid=CHATMANT01 |archivedate=October 17, 2012 }} and the [[University of Cincinnati]]{{cite web|url= https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/C/ChatAn00.htm|title= Antonio Chatman |publisher=Pro-Football-Reference.Com|accessdate= October 19, 2012}} where he was a [[Criminology]] major. ==Professional career== ===San Francisco 49ers=== Chatman signed as an [[undrafted free agent]] with the [[San Francisco 49ers]] of the [[National Football League|NFL]] but was soon released. ===Chicago Rush=== He then joined the [[Chicago Rush]] of the [[Arena Football League (1987–2008)|AFL]] in 2002. After two weeks on the bench behind offensive specialist [[Joe Douglass]], a freak season-ending injury to Douglass during pre-game warmups pushed Chatman into the starting job in Week 3, and he responded with a strong [[rookie]] season, leading the Rush in receiving with 74 catches for 1,068 yards and 23 touchdowns, and earning [[Arena Football League (1987–2008)|AFL]] All-Rookie Team honors in the process. He followed that campaign with an even better season in 2003, catching 123 passes for 1,636 yards and 29 touchdowns, and added 2,062 yards and 7 touchdowns on kick returns to set an AFL record for all-purpose yardage. Chatman was named to the All-Arena Second-team and was a runner-up for the league's Offensive Player of the Year award. ===Green Bay Packers=== His success in Chicago attracted the attention of the NFL's [[Green Bay Packers]], and he signed with that team for the [[2003 NFL season|2003 season]]. Upon joining the [[Green Bay Packers]], Chatman was largely relegated to a [[Kick returner|kick returning]] role, seeing only sparing action as a wide receiver his first season. In 2004, he gradually saw an increased role in the offense at receiver, before finally seeing extensive action as a [[Starting lineup|starter]] in 2005 due to injuries to [[Javon Walker]] and [[Robert Ferguson (American football)|Robert Ferguson]]. In his second to last game with the Packers, Chatman returned a punt 85 yards for a touchdown. It was the first punt returned for touchdown for the Packers since [[Allen Rossum]] did it in 2001. ===Cincinnati Bengals=== Chatman signed with the [[Cincinnati Bengals]] prior to the [[2006 NFL season]]. However, in 2006 he missed several of the Bengals early games due to injury, and eventually was put on [[injured reserve]]. On September 7, 2007, the Bengals cut him but re-signed him a few days later for the 2007 season. On February 26, 2008, the Bengals reached a new two-year agreement with Chatman. On November 16, 2008, Chatman suffered a cervical injury in a game against the Philadelphia Eagles. Chatman was released on November 17, 2009, with an injury settlement after being placed on [[injured reserve]] earlier in the year. ===Sacramento Mountain Lions=== Chatman was selected with the third pick of the sixth round and 28th selection overall in the [[2010 UFL draft]] by the [[Sacramento Mountain Lions]] on June 4, 2010, re-uniting him with former [[Cincinnati Bengals]] teammates [[Chris Perry (American football)|Chris Perry]] and [[Doug Gabriel]]. ==NFL career statistics== ===Regular season=== {| class="wikitable" style="text-align: center;" |- ! rowspan="2"|Year !! rowspan="2"|Team !! colspan="2"|Games !! colspan="5"|Receiving !! colspan="2"|Fumbles |- ! '''Antoine Duane Winfield Sr.''' (born June 24, 1977) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[cornerback]] for 14 seasons in the [[National Football League]] (NFL).  He played [[college football]] for the [[Ohio State Buckeyes football|Ohio State Buckeyes]], earning consensus [[College Football All-America Team|All-American]] honors and winning the [[Jim Thorpe Award]]. He was selected by the [[Buffalo Bills]] in the first round of the [[1999 NFL draft]] and played five seasons for the Bills and nine seasons for the [[Minnesota Vikings]]. He was a three-time [[Pro Bowl]] selection as a member of the Vikings.

==Early life==
Winfield was born in [[Akron, Ohio]].  He attended [[Garfield High School (Akron, Ohio)|Garfield High School]] in his hometown of Akron.

==College career==
Winfield received an athletic scholarship to attend [[Ohio State University]], where he played for the [[Ohio State Buckeyes football]] team from 1995 to 1998.  As a senior in 1998, he was a consensus first-team [[All-American]], and won the [[Jim Thorpe Award]] as the nation's top [[defensive back]].

===Buffalo Bills===
The [[Buffalo Bills]] selected Winfield in the first round (23rd overall pick) of the 1999 NFL draft, and he played for the Bills from {{NFL Year|1999}} to {{NFL Year|2003}}.<ref>{{Cite web |title=1999 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/1999/draft.htm |access-date=2023-03-28 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

====1999====
On July 30, 1999, the Buffalo Bills signed Winfield to a five-year, [[United States dollar|$]]7.98 million contract.<ref name="spotrac">{{cite web |title=Spotrac.com: Antoine Winfield contract |url=https://www.spotrac.com/nfl/seattle-seahawks/antoine-winfield-4790/ |access-date=November 29, 2018 |website=Spotrac.com}}</ref> Head coach [[Wade Phillips]] named Winfield the third cornerback in the depth chart to begin the regular season, behind veterans [[Thomas Smith (cornerback)|Thomas Smith]] and [[Ken Irvin]].<ref>{{cite web |title=1999 Buffalo Bills Starters, Roster, & Players |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/teams/buf/1999_roster.htm |access-date=November 29, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref>

Winfield made his professional regular season debut in the [[1999 Buffalo Bills season|Buffalo Bills’]] season-opener at the [[1999 Indianapolis Colts season|Indianapolis Colts]] and recorded three combined tackles and made his first career interception during their 31–14 loss. Winfield made his first career interception off a pass attempt by Colts’ quarterback [[Peyton Manning]], that was originally intended for the wide receiver [[Jerome Pathon]], and returned it for a three-yard gain in the fourth quarter.<ref>{{cite web |title=Buffalo Bills at Indianapolis Colts – September 12th, 1999 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/199909120clt.htm |access-date=November 30, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref><ref name="1999 games">{{cite web|title=Antoine Winfield game logs, 1999|url=http://www.nfl.com/player/antoinewinfield/2503765/gamelogs?season=1999|publisher=NFL|access-date=September 11, 2012}}</ref> On December 26, 1999, Winfield earned his first career start in place of [[Ken Irvin]] who was placed on injured reserve due to a foot injury he sustained the previous week.<ref>{{cite web |title=Bills Daily 1999 News Archives |url=http://www.billsdaily.com/weekinreview/1999/dec4.html |access-date=November 30, 2018 |website=BillsDaily.com}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Bills' best better than the Cardinals |url=http://tucsoncitizen.com/morgue2/1999/12/20/170480-bills-best-better-than-the-cardinals/ |access-date=November 30, 2018 |newspaper=Tucson Citizen |last=Walsh |first=Chris |date=December 20, 1999 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141010174403/http://tucsoncitizen.com/morgue2/1999/12/20/170480-bills-best-better-than-the-cardinals/ |archive-date=October 10, 2014 |url-status=dead }}</ref> He finished his first career start with one tackle during their 13–10 victory at the [[1999 New England Patriots season|New England Patriots]] in a Week 16. In Week 17, Winfield collected a season-high 11 combined tackles as the Bills defeated the Indianapolis Colts 31–6.<ref>{{cite web |title=NFL Player stats: Antoine Winfield (1999) |url=http://www.nfl.com/player/antoinewinfield/2503765/gamelogs?season=1999 |access-date=November 30, 2018 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> He finished his rookie season in [[1999 NFL season|1999]] with 40 combined tackles and two interceptions in 16 games and two starts.<ref>{{cite web |title=NFL #21 Antoine Winfield -ESPN (1999) |url=http://espn.com/nfl/playergamelog?playerId=1775&season=1999&lang=EN |access-date=November 30, 2018 |website=ESPN.com }}{{Dead link|date=June 2020 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref>

The Buffalo Bills finished second in the [[AFC East]] with an 11–5 record and earned a wildcard berth. On January 8, 2000, Winfield started in his first career playoff game and recorded three combined tackles and intercepted a pass by Titans’ quarterback [[Steve McNair]] during their 22–16 loss at the [[1999 Tennessee Titans season|Tennessee Titans]] in the AFC Wildcard Game.<ref>{{cite web |title=Wild Card – Buffalo Bills at Tennessee Titans – January 8th, 2000 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200001080oti.htm |access-date=November 30, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref>

====2000====
Winfield entered training camp slated as a starting cornerback after Thomas Smith departed during free agency and signed with the [[Chicago Bears]]. Head coach Wade Phillips named Winfield and Ken Irvin the starting cornerbacks to begin the regular season. In Week 9, Winfield collected a season-high nine combined tackles during a 23–20 victory against the [[2000 New York Jets season|New York Jets]]. On November 5, 2000, Winfield sustained a shoulder injury during a 16–13 win at the [[2000 New England Patriots season|New England Patriots]]. On November 19, 2000, Winfield further aggravated his shoulder injury during a 21–17 victory at the [[2000 Kansas City Chiefs season|Kansas City Chiefs]]. On November 24, 2000, the Buffalo Bills placed Winfield on injured reserve after it was discovered he had a torn labrum cartilage in his right shoulder that would require surgery.<ref>{{cite web |title=N.F.L.: ROUNDUP; Bucs' Alstott Injured, Out for Season |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2000/11/21/sports/nfl-roundup-bucs-alstott-injured-out-for-season.html |access-date=November 30, 2018 |newspaper=New York Times |date=November 21, 2000}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=NFL Injury Report |url=https://www.nhregister.com/news/article/NFL-injury-report-11697642.php |access-date=November 30, 2018 |newspaper=New Hampshire Register |date=November 24, 2000}}</ref>

====2001====
On January 8, 2001, the Buffalo Bills fired head coach Wade Phillips after they finished with an 8–8 record in 2000.<ref>{{cite web |title=Bills fire Wade Phillips |url=https://www.upi.com/Archives/2001/01/08/Bills-fire-Wade-Phillips/8621978930000/ |access-date=November 30, 2018 |website=UPI.com |date=January 8, 2001}}</ref> Head coach [[Gregg Williams]] retained Winfield and Ken Irvin as the starting cornerbacks to begin the regular season. On September 23, 2001, Winfield recorded three combined tackles, a pass deflection, forced a fumble, and intercepted a pass by Colts’ quarterback Peyton Manning during a 42–26 loss at the [[2001 Indianapolis Colts season|Indianapolis Colts]] in Week 2. In Week 14, he collected a season-high eight solo tackles as the Bills loss 12–9 to the [[2001 New England Patriots season|New England Patriots]].<ref>{{cite web |title=NFL Player stats: Antoine Winfield (2001) |url=http://www.nfl.com/player/antoinewinfield/2503765/gamelogs?season=2001 |access-date=November 30, 2018 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> He started in all 16 games in [[2001 NFL season|2001]] and recorded 80 combined tackles (68 solo), nine pass deflections, and two interceptions.<ref name="career">{{cite web |title=NFL Player stats: Antoine Winfield (career) |url=http://www.nfl.com/player/antoinewinfield/2503765/careerstats |access-date=November 30, 2018 |website=NFL.com}}</ref>

====2002====
Winfield returned as a starting cornerback in 2002. He started alongside his former Ohio State teammate [[Nate Clements]].<ref>{{cite web |title=2002 Buffalo Bills Starters, Roster, & Players |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/teams/buf/2002_roster.htm |access-date=November 30, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref> In Week 3, Winfield collected a season-high nine combined tackles during a 28–23 loss at the [[2002 Denver Broncos season|Denver Broncos]] in Week 3. Winfield missed three games (Weeks 7–9) due to a knee injury. On October 18, 2002, Winfield underwent [[arthroscopic surgery]] on his knee.<ref>{{cite web |title=Bills Injuries take Toll |url=https://www.orlandosentinel.com/news/os-xpm-2002-10-19-0210190385-story.html |access-date=November 30, 2018 |newspaper=Orlando Sentinel |date=October 19, 2002}}</ref> He finished the season with 56 combined tackles (51 solo) and seven pass deflections in 13 games and 13 starts.<ref name="career" />

====2003====
Defensive coordinator [[Jerry Gray]] retained Winfield and Nate Clements the starting cornerback duo in 2003.<ref>{{cite web |title=2003 Buffalo Bills Starters, Roster, & Players |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/teams/buf/2003_roster.htm |access-date=December 1, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref> On October 5, 2003, Winfield collected a season-high 12 combined tackles (11 solo) as the Bills defeated the [[2003 Cincinnati Bengals season|Cincinnati Bengals]] 22–16.<ref>{{cite web |title=NFL Player stats: Antoine Winfield (2003) |url=http://www.nfl.com/player/antoinewinfield/2503765/gamelogs?season=2003 |access-date=December 1, 2018 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> On November 23, 2003, Winfield recorded ten combined tackles (seven solo) and made his first career sack during a 17–14 loss against the [[2003 Indianapolis Colts season|Indianapolis Colts]] in Week 12. Winfield sacked Colts’ quarterback [[Peyton Manning]] for a six-yard loss during the first quarter.<ref>{{cite web |title=Indianapolis Colts at Buffalo Bills – November 23rd, 2003 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200311230buf.htm |access-date=December 1, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref> Winfield started in all 16 games in [[2003 NFL season|2003]] and recorded a career-high 107 combined tackles (92 solo), 11 pass deflections, two forced fumbles, one sack, and an interception.<ref name="career" />

====2004====
Winfield became an unrestricted free agent in 2004 and was considered by many analysts to be the top free agent cornerback on the market. He was heavily pursued by multiple teams, including the [[New York Jets]], [[Miami Dolphins]], [[Houston Texans]], and [[Minnesota Vikings]]. On March 4, 2004, it was reported that the New York Jets and Winfield has agreed, in principle, to a six-year, $30 million contract with $10 million guaranteed. Winfield attended a visit with the Minnesota Vikings and officially signed with them the following day.<ref>{{cite web |title=Winfield Jets Away |url=https://www.nydailynews.com/archives/sports/winfield-jets-article-1.569564 |access-date=December 1, 2018 |website=New York Daily News |date=March 4, 2004}}</ref>

===Minnesota Vikings===
[[File:Antoine Winfield 2010.jpg|thumb|left|Winfield in 2010]]
On March 5, 2004, the [[Minnesota Vikings]] signed Winfield to a six-year, $34.8 million contract that includes a [[signing bonus]] of $10.8 million.<ref>{{cite web|last=Banks|first=Dow|title=Change in plans |url=http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/2004/football/nfl/03/05/vikings.winfield/index.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20040419094602/http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/2004/football/nfl/03/05/vikings.winfield/index.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=April 19, 2004 |work=SI.com|access-date=September 11, 2012|date=March 5, 2004}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Vikings Sign Antoine Winfield |url=https://www.upi.com/Vikings-sign-Antoine-Winfield/93841078537487/ |access-date=November 29, 2018 |website=UI.com|date=March 4, 2004}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Vikes Work Cap Room With Winfield Deal |url=https://247sports.com/nfl/minnesota-vikings/Article/Vikes-Work-Cap-Room-With-Winfield-Deal-104076504/ |access-date=December 1, 2018 |website=247Sports.com |date=March 11, 2004}}</ref> Head coach [[Mike Tice]] named Winfield and [[Brian Williams (cornerback)|Brian Williams]] the starting cornerbacks to start the regular season.<ref>{{cite web |title=2004 Minnesota Vikings Starters, Roster, & Players |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/teams/min/2004_roster.htm |access-date=December 1, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref>

On October 17, 2004, Winfield recorded seven combined tackles, deflected a pass, and made his first interception as a member of the Vikings during a 38–31 win at the [[2004 New Orleans Saints season|New Orleans Saints]]. Winfield intercepted a pass by Saints’ quarterback [[Aaron Brooks (American football)|Aaron Brooks]], that was intended for wide receiver [[Ernie Conwell]], and returned it for a 56-yard gain during the first quarter.<ref>{{cite web |title=Minnesota Vikings at New Orleans Saints – October 17th, 2004 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200410170nor.htm |access-date=December 1, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref> The following week, Winfield made eight solo tackles, two pass deflections, and intercepted a pass attempt by Titans’ quarterback [[Billy Volek]] during a 20–3 victory against the [[2004 Tennessee Titans season|Tennessee Titans]] in Week 7.<ref>{{cite web |title=Tennessee Titans at Minnesota Vikings – October 24th, 2004 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200410240min.htm |access-date=December 1, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref> In Week 9, he collected a season-high 13 combined tackles (ten solo) and broke up two passes during a 31–28 loss at the [[2004 Indianapolis Colts season|Indianapolis Colts]]. Winfield was inactive for two games (Weeks 14–15) due to an ankle injury.<ref>{{cite web |title=Football |url=https://products.kitsapsun.com/archive/2004/12-24/24277_football.html |access-date=December 1, 2018 |website=products.kitsapsun.com |date=December 24, 2004}}</ref> Winfield finished the [[2004 NFL season]] with 85 combined tackles (70 solo), five passes defenses, three interceptions, and two forced fumbles in 14 games and 14 starts.<ref name="career" />

====2005====
Head coach Mike Tice named Winfield and newly acquired free agent [[Fred Smoot]] the starting cornerbacks to begin 2005. They started alongside safeties [[Corey Chavous]] and [[Darren Sharper]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Vikings Believe the Smoke Has Finally Cleared |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/wp-dyn/content/article/2005/09/05/AR2005090501088.html |access-date=December 1, 2018 | newspaper=Washington Post |last=Campbell |first=Rich |date=September 7, 2005}}</ref> On November 6, 2005, Winfield collected a season-high 14 combined tackles (11 solo), deflected two passes, and made an interception off Lions’ quarterback [[Joey Harrington]] during a 27–14 win against the [[2005 Detroit Lions season|Detroit Lions]] in Week 9.<ref>{{cite web |title=Detroit Lions at Minnesota Vikings – November 6th, 2005 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200511060min.htm |access-date=December 1, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref> In Week 12, Winfield made nine combined tackles, a season-high three pass deflections, and intercepted a pass by [[Trent Dilfer]] as the Vikings defeated the [[2005 Cleveland Browns season|Cleveland Browns]] 24–12.<ref>{{cite web |title=Cleveland Browns at Minnesota Vikings – November 27th, 2005 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200511270min.htm |access-date=December 1, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref>

====2006–2008====
In the Vikings' 30–27 win over the [[New Orleans Saints]] on Week 5 (October 6) of 2008, a ''[[Monday Night Football]]'' game, Winfield returned a blocked field goal attempt by [[Martin Gramatica]] 59 yards for a touchdown.<ref>{{cite news|author=Alonzo, Rick|title=Winfield returns blocked field goal, forces fumble|url=http://www.twincities.com/vikings/ci_10656186|work=St. Paul Pioneer-Press|date=October 7, 2008|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081010100633/http://www.twincities.com/vikings/ci_10656186|archive-date=October 10, 2008}}</ref> Additionally, Winfield had 8 tackles and one [[pass deflected|deflected pass]] that game.<ref name="2008 games">{{cite web|title=Antoine Winfield game logs, 2008|url=http://www.nfl.com/player/antoinewinfield/2503765/gamelogs?season=2008|publisher=NFL|access-date=September 11, 2012}}</ref> Winfield finished 2008 with 95 total tackles, 2 sacks, 5 passes defended, and one interception.<ref name="NFL profile">{{cite web|title=Antoine Winfield|url=http://www.nfl.com/player/antoinewinfield/2503765/profile|publisher=NFL|access-date=September 11, 2012}}</ref> He made his first Pro Bowl in 2008.

====2009====
On July 23, 2009, the Vikings signed Winfield to a new five-year, $36 million contract. The deal includes $16.1 million in guarantees. He made his second straight Pro Bowl in 2010 after replacing injured [[Dominique Rodgers-Cromartie]]. After making the [[2011 Pro Bowl|2010]] Pro Bowl squad, he made an interception that led to a touchdown in an NFC 55–41 victory.  He is regarded as one of the most physical corners in the league, known for his bone-jarring hits, and was ranked by [[Peter King (sportswriter)|Peter King]] of ''[[Sports Illustrated]]'' as the 31st best player in the NFL.<ref>{{cite news |first=Peter |last=King |title=My list of the NFL's 500 best players |url=http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/2007/writers/peter_king/08/28/1to100/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071013065030/http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/2007/writers/peter_king/08/28/1to100/ |url-status=dead |archive-date=October 13, 2007 |work=Sports Illustrated |date=August 29, 2007 }}</ref>

====2010–2012====
Winfield was the only player on the Vikings' active 2012 roster who played during the 1990s.<ref name="Pioneer Press interview 2012">{{cite news|last=Sansevere |first=Bob |title=Minnesota Vikings: Antoine Winfield, 35, all about experience, savvy ... and big hits |url=http://www.twincities.com/vikings/ci_21329540/minnesota-vikings-antoine-winfield-35-all-about-experience |newspaper=St. Paul Pioneer-Press |date=August 16, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120818003730/http://www.twincities.com/vikings/ci_21329540/minnesota-vikings-antoine-winfield-35-all-about-experience |archive-date=August 18, 2012 |url-status=live }}</ref>

====2013====
Winfield was released by the [[Minnesota Vikings]] on March 12, 2013, in a move to clear $7.25 million in salary cap space.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.yardbarker.com/nfl/articles/report_vikings_release_cb_antoine_winfield/13121476|title=Minnesota Vikings: Breaking News, Rumors & Highlights}}</ref>

===Seattle Seahawks===
Winfield signed with the [[Seattle Seahawks]] on April 17, 2013, to a one-year, $3 million contract. He was assigned number 21 due to starting fullback Michael Robinson having already been assigned 26 in 2010. He was released from the team during final cuts on August 31, 2013.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.seahawks.com/news/articles/article-1/Antoine-Winfield-brings-his-skills-to-Seahawks-secondary/f387290c-ced6-49ef-8e68-f24ac09b952c |title=Antoine Winfield brings his skills to Seahawks secondary |access-date=April 18, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130419005654/http://www.seahawks.com/news/articles/article-1/Antoine-Winfield-brings-his-skills-to-Seahawks-secondary/f387290c-ced6-49ef-8e68-f24ac09b952c |archive-date=April 19, 2013 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

===Retirement===
On August 31, 2013, [[Seattle Seahawks]] coach [[Pete Carroll]] announced on Twitter that Winfield was retiring.<ref>{{cite web | title=Antoine Winfield decides to retire after 14 NFL seasons | website=NFL.com | date=August 31, 2013 | url=https://www.nfl.com/news/antoine-winfield-decides-to-retire-after-14-nfl-seasons-0ap1000000237046 | access-date=April 19, 2026}}</ref>

'''Antonio Michael Freeman''' (born May 27, 1972) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[wide receiver]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL), most notably for the [[Green Bay Packers]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Antonio Freeman |url=https://www.packers.com/history/hof/antonio-freeman |website=Green Bay Packers |access-date=20 June 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Antonio Freeman Bio |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/player/bio/_/id/890/antonio-freeman |website=ESPN |access-date=20 June 2026}}</ref>. He attended the [[Baltimore Polytechnic Institute]] and [[Virginia Tech]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Antonio Freeman |url=https://vasportshof.com/inductee/antonio-freeman/ |website=Virginia Sports Hall of Fame |access-date=20 June 2026}}</ref>

==College career==
Freeman played [[college football]] at [[Virginia Tech Hokies football|Virginia Tech]], where he caught 121 passes for 2,207 yards and 22 touchdowns in four seasons.  He also returned 64 punts for 652 yards and another touchdown, and rushed for 37 yards. His accomplishments earned him enshrinement in the [[List of Virginia Tech Sports Hall of Fame inductees|Virginia Tech Sports Hall of Fame]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Antonio Freeman |url=https://www.packers.com/history/hof/antonio-freeman |website=Green Bay Packers |access-date=20 June 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Antonio Freeman |url=https://vasportshof.com/inductee/antonio-freeman/ |website=Virginia Sports Hall of Fame |access-date=20 June 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Antonio Freeman College Stats, School, Draft, Gamelog, Splits |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/antonio-freeman-1.html |website=Sports-Reference.com |access-date=20 June 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Antonio Freeman |url=https://www.eventusa.com/packers-player-reception/antonio-freeman/ |website=Event USA |access-date=20 June 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Antonio Freeman Biography |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/player/bio/_/id/890/antonio-freeman |website=ESPN |access-date=20 June 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Antonio Freeman |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070208223948/http:/www.databasefootball.com/players/playerpage.htm?ilkid=FREEMANT01 |website=DatabaseFootball.com (archived) |via=Wayback Machine |access-date=20 June 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web

==Professional career==

Freeman was drafted by the Green Bay Packers in the third round with the 90th overall pick in the [[1995 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=1995 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/1995/draft.htm |access-date=2023-03-31|website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> In his rookie season, he returned a punt 76 yds for a touchdown during a playoff win over Atlanta.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Wild Card - Atlanta Falcons at Green Bay Packers - December 31st, 1995 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/199512310gnb.htm |access-date=2025-06-11 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> He went on to lead the Packers in receiving in four seasons from 1996 to 1999, and led the NFL in receiving in 1998.

The peak of Freeman's career occurred during his first tenure with the [[Green Bay Packers]] including a victory in [[Super Bowl XXXI]] in 1997 over the [[New England Patriots]]. During that Super Bowl, Freeman caught a then-Super Bowl record-length touchdown pass of 81 yards from [[Brett Favre]]. The record was eclipsed in [[Super Bowl XXXVIII]] when [[Muhsin Muhammad]] caught an 85-yard touchdown pass. That play would give the Packers the lead for good as they went on to win 35–21.  Freeman finished the game with three receptions for 105 yards.  The following year, Freeman gained over 1,200 receiving yards as Green Bay advanced to their second consecutive Super Bowl, where he caught 9 passes for 126 yards and 2 touchdowns in the 31–24 loss to the [[Denver Broncos]].  His 230 all-purpose yards in the game was the third highest total in Super Bowl history.

In [[1998 NFL season|1998]], Freeman had his best NFL season, catching 84 passes for a league leading 1,424 receiving yards and earning his only [[Pro Bowl]] appearance.

During [[overtime (sports)|overtime]] of a Monday night game on November 6, 2000, despite bad weather conditions, Freeman caught what initially appeared to be an incomplete pass while lying on his side—after almost being intercepted by [[Minnesota Vikings]] cornerback [[Cris Dishman]], the ball actually bounced off multiple parts of Freeman's body without hitting the ground. Untouched by the defender, Freeman jumped to his feet and ran the ball in for the winning touchdown over the Vikings, the Packers' [[Packers–Vikings rivalry|rival]]. The touchdown prompted [[ESPN on ABC|ABC]] play-by-play announcer [[Al Michaels]], who was stunned by the play, to shout, "He did WHAT?!"<ref>{{cite news|last=Sandomir|first=Richard|title=TV SPORTS; The Ratings Don't Tell The Story On Monday|url=https://query.nytimes.com/gst/fullpage.html?res=9F01E5D61139F93BA35752C1A9669C8B63&sec=&spon=&pagewanted=all|newspaper=[[The New York Times]]|date=November 8, 2000|access-date=April 25, 2010}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://m.youtube.com/watch?v=lQmyLLxRNcA|title = Antonio Freeman Monday Night Catch (ACTUAL BROADCAST SOUND)|website = [[YouTube]]| date=December 10, 2011 }}</ref> In 2005, [[ESPN]] labeled the catch as the greatest play in the history of ''[[Monday Night Football]]''.{{citation needed|date=August 2017}}  Freeman has said it was the second best catch of his career (claiming his best to be an 81-yard touchdown reception in Super Bowl XXXI).

Freeman played for the Green Bay Packers from [[1995 NFL season|1995]] through the [[2001 NFL season]]. After feuding with Packers Head Coach [[Mike Sherman]] in 2001, Freeman signed with the [[Philadelphia Eagles]].  His final game in his first Packers tenure was against the [[St. Louis Rams]] during the 2001 NFL playoffs.  He then went on to play a year for the Eagles in 2002 before coming back to Green Bay for the 2003 season and a second tenure with the club.  His final catch with the Packers occurred on the road in December 2003 during the fourth quarter of Brett Favre's phenomenal performance against the Oakland Raiders on ABC's Monday Night Football, following the death of Favre's father.  He played his final game with Green Bay in the infamous "[[4th and 26]]" debacle in the NFL playoffs against the Philadelphia Eagles in January 2004.  Freeman last played in the NFL with the [[Miami Dolphins]] during 2004 training camp.<ref>{{cite web | title=Dolphins cut 20 players, including WR Freeman | website=ESPN.com|agency=Associated Press | date=2004-09-05 | url=https://www.espn.com/espn/wire?section=nfl&id=1875472 | access-date=2026-03-10}}</ref>

In his ten NFL seasons, Freeman caught 477 passes for 7,251 yards, gained 1,007 yards returning kickoffs and punts, and scored 61 touchdowns. He played in the [[Pro Bowl]] in 1999. His teams made the playoffs in seven of his NFL seasons.  He appeared in four NFC Championship Games and two Super Bowls.  He ranks sixth all-time on the Green Bay Packers receivers list with 6,651 yards on 431 catches.  Freeman had three 1,000 yard receiving seasons in his career, 1997–1999. Nicknamed "Free", in 2006 Freeman won a [[Pop Warner Little Scholars|Pop Warner]] Award for his work with youth.

On June 16, 2007, Freeman signed with the Packers to retire with the team.<ref>[http://www.jsonline.com/sports/packers/29351654.html Freeman will retire as a Packer]</ref> He was inducted into the [[Green Bay Packers Hall of Fame]] in 2009.<ref>{{Cite web | url = https://www.packers.com/history/hof/antonio-freeman | title = Antonio Freeman | last = Christl | first = Cliff | author-link = Cliff Christl | website = Packers.com | access-date = September 20, 2023 | archive-date = May 23, 2023 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20230523012438/https://www.packers.com/history/hof/antonio-freeman | url-status = live }}</ref>

==Post-playing career==
Freeman occasionally participates as an analyst on ''[[ESPN First Take]]'' and ''[[NFL Live]]'', mostly during NFL season. He has also appeared on ''[[College GameDay (football)|ESPN College Gameday]]'' in support of his alma mater Virginia Tech. Freeman was also a commentator on ''Redskins Kickoff'' and ''Redskins Postgame Live'' for [[Comcast SportsNet Washington]]. Freeman was inducted into the [[Virginia Sports Hall of Fame and Museum|Virginia Sports Hall of Fame]] in 2012.<ref>{{cite web |title=Antonio Freeman (2012) |url=https://vasportshof.com/inductees/?v_sport=Football&v_keyword=&v_year=2012&ind_search=Search |website=Virginia Sports Hall of Fame |access-date=August 20, 2018}}</ref>

Freeman has hosted his own radio show ''The End Zone with Antonio Freeman'' since 2010, the show currently airs on WTSO in Madison and WOKY in Milwaukee, Wisconsin.

==Personal life==
He is the father of [[Alex Freeman]], a soccer player who currently plays for [[Villarreal CF]] in [[La Liga]], and received his first call-up to the [[United States men's national soccer team]] on May 22, 2025.<ref>{{Cite web |date=May 22, 2025 |title=Pochettino Names 27-Player Roster for Training Camp ahead of June Matches Against Turkey and Switzerland |url=https://www.ussoccer.com/stories/2025/05/mauricio-pochettino-27-player-roster-training-camp-june-matches-turkey-switzerland |access-date=May 22, 2025 |website=[[United States Soccer Federation]]}}</ref>
