'''Anthony Lavon Wright''' (born February 14, 1976) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[quarterback]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) for the [[Pittsburgh Steelers]], [[Dallas Cowboys]], [[Baltimore Ravens]], [[Cincinnati Bengals]], and [[New York Giants]]. He played [[college football]] for the [[South Carolina Gamecocks football|South Carolina Gamecocks]].

==Early life==
Wright attended [[West Craven High School (Vanceboro)|West Craven High School]], where he played as a [[quarterback]]. As a senior, he was named All-state, SuperPrep [[All-American]] and Gatorade Player-of-the-Year. He finished his high school career with 4,890 passing yards, 44 [[touchdown]]s and 15 [[interception]]s.

==College career==
Wright accepted a football scholarship from the [[University of South Carolina]]. As a [[Redshirt (college sports)|redshirt]] freshman, he was a backup behind [[Steve Taneyhill]], making 17 out of 27 completions for 207 yards, 2 touchdowns and one interception. As a sophomore, he became a starter after Taneyhill graduated, posting 1,850 passing yards, 8 passing touchdowns, 3 interceptions, 90 rushing yards and 3 rushing touchdowns.

As a junior, he suffered a torn anterior cruciate ligament in his right knee against the [[University of Tennessee]], missing the final two games of the season.<ref>{{Cite web |date=November 14, 1997 |title=South Carolina Turns To Freshman Quarterback |url=https://www.orlandosentinel.com/1997/11/14/south-carolina-turns-to-freshman-quarterback/ |access-date=February 19, 2018 |website=Orlando Sentinel}}</ref> He had 1,685 passing yards, a school record 18 passing touchdowns, 5 interceptions, 44 rushing yards and one rushing touchdown.

As a senior, head coach [[Brad Scott (American football)|Brad Scott]] platooned him with freshman Phil Petty, but still recorded 1,899 passing yards, 10 passing touchdowns, 10 interceptions, 56 rushing yards and 3 rushing touchdowns. He left as the school's fifth all-time passer, leading the school to a 12–21 record over the three years he was the starter, including one winning campaign and a 1–10 record in his last season.

==Professional career==

===Pittsburgh Steelers===
Wright was signed as an [[undrafted free agent]] by the [[Pittsburgh Steelers]] after the [[1999 NFL draft]]. He made such a good impression in preseason that the team made the unusual move keeping him as the fourth-string quarterback, behind [[Kordell Stewart]], [[Mike Tomczak]], and [[Pete Gonzalez]]. On August 27, 2000, he was waived after being passed on the depth chart by rookie [[Tee Martin]].<ref>{{cite web| url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?nid=1129&dat=20000828&id=R7JRAAAAIBAJ&sjid=em8DAAAAIBAJ&pg=6475,5834731&hl=es | title=Farmer among 13 waived by the Steelers | access-date=February 19, 2018}}</ref>

===Dallas Cowboys===
On August 30, 2000, Wright was signed by the [[Dallas Cowboys]] to their practice squad. Even though he hadn't played in an NFL regular season game, he was scouted in a preseason game between the Cowboys and the Steelers.

In November, he was promoted to the active roster after backup quarterback [[Randall Cunningham]] was injured.<ref>{{cite web| url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?nid=1346&dat=20001213&id=vb0wAAAAIBAJ&sjid=df0DAAAAIBAJ&pg=6524,752796&hl=es | title='Pactice Dummy' Takes Dallas Quarterback Role | access-date=February 19, 2018}}</ref> On December 10, when [[Troy Aikman]] suffered a concussion playing against the [[Washington Redskins]], Wright played the remaining three quarters in a 32–13 win. Although he had attempted only 5 passes (3 completions) in the previous game, he was given the start in the next game against the [[New York Giants]], which resulted in a 17–13 loss.<ref>{{cite web| url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?nid=861&dat=20001222&id=ZERTAAAAIBAJ&sjid=YoUDAAAAIBAJ&pg=4570,6016361&hl=es | title=Foul play against Giants produced foul odor| access-date=February 19, 2018}}</ref> He would also start the final game of the season against the [[Tennessee Titans]], which resulted in a 31–0 loss after he had three critical turnovers in the third quarter.<ref>{{cite web| url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?nid=1350&dat=20001226&id=yVhPAAAAIBAJ&sjid=7AMEAAAAIBAJ&pg=3595,3402620&hl=es | title=Titans rip Cowboys with big third-quarter spurt | access-date=February 19, 2018}}</ref>

In 2001, he became the backup quarterback after [[Tony Banks (American football)|Tony Banks]] was cut. When starter [[Quincy Carter]] injured his throwing thumb, Wright became his replacement and started on September 23 against the [[San Diego Chargers]], but had two costly turnovers in a 21–32 loss.<ref>{{cite web| url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?nid=1817&dat=20010920&id=5YUfAAAAIBAJ&sjid=MKYEAAAAIBAJ&pg=4396,3884056&hl=es | title=Wright ready to start for Dallas Cowboys | access-date=February 19, 2018}}</ref> The next week he started in an 18–40 loss against the [[Philadelphia Eagles]], in which he was ineffective.<ref>{{cite web| url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?nid=1346&dat=20011001&id=2J8sAAAAIBAJ&sjid=jf0DAAAAIBAJ&pg=3403,175496&hl=es | title=Eagles Soar Past Cowboys | access-date=February 19, 2018}}</ref> On October 7, he replaced an injured Carter but the team still lost 21–28 against the [[Oakland Raiders]].<ref>{{cite web| url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?nid=1310&dat=20011008&id=VVFWAAAAIBAJ&sjid=_OsDAAAAIBAJ&pg=2523,1944034&hl=es | title=Raiders keep Cowboys on skids, 28-21 | access-date=February 19, 2018}}</ref> The next week he started on [[Monday Night Football]] and contributed to a 9–7 win against Tony Banks and the [[Washington Redskins]].<ref>{{cite web| url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?nid=932&dat=20011017&id=W8RPAAAAIBAJ&sjid=9FIDAAAAIBAJ&pg=3317,1408980&hl=es | title=Cowboys, Redskins rivalry fell a bit short on Monday | access-date=February 19, 2018}}</ref> Having a chronic right knee injury, he decided to have his knee scoped to repair the cartilage damage, forcing him to sit the rest of the season. The Cowboys would use a combination of [[Clint Stoerner]] and [[Ryan Leaf]] as the starters until Carter recovered from a torn hamstring, starting a franchise-high four quarterbacks in a season.<ref>{{cite web| url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?nid=1314&dat=20011025&id=po9XAAAAIBAJ&sjid=efIDAAAAIBAJ&pg=5533,4700486&hl=es | title=Colts finish in a flurry | access-date=February 19, 2018}}</ref>

Head coach [[Dave Campo]] released Wright from the team on September 1, 2002, following the acquisition of [[quarterback]] [[Chad Hutchinson]] during the offseason, while stating that Stoerner was better suited for the third-string quarterback role, in light of Wright's ambition to be a starter.<ref>{{cite web| url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?nid=861&dat=20020902&id=-hVZAAAAIBAJ&sjid=bkYNAAAAIBAJ&pg=6893,479219&hl=es | title=Cowboys release Seder, 17 others | access-date=February 19, 2018}}</ref>

===Baltimore Ravens===
Wright was signed by the [[Baltimore Ravens]] to their [[practice squad]] in 2002. He was activated from the practice squad on October 15.<ref>{{cite web| url=http://articles.baltimoresun.com/2002-10-16/sports/0210160036_1_practice-squad-base-coach-bench-coach | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304100026/http://articles.baltimoresun.com/2002-10-16/sports/0210160036_1_practice-squad-base-coach-bench-coach | url-status=dead | archive-date=March 4, 2016 | title=Transactions | date=October 16, 2002 | access-date=February 19, 2018}}</ref> In the 2003 season, the team’s first-round draft pick, quarterback [[Kyle Boller]], injured his thigh in a game against the [[St. Louis Rams]] on November 9 (Week 10). This gave way to an opportunity for Wright to start games.

Wright’s first start was in Week 11 against the [[Miami Dolphins]]. His performance was unremarkable, and the Ravens lost 9-6 (OT). In the following week, however, Wright led a spectacular comeback against the [[2003 Seattle Seahawks season|Seahawks]]. With the score tied at three in the final minute of the first half, the Seahawks scored two quick touchdowns, and stormed to a 41–24 lead with seven minutes remaining, but Wright erupted with four touchdown throws to [[Marcus Robinson (American football)|Marcus Robinson]] and 319 passing yards in a 44–41 overtime triumph. Ravens head coach [[Brian Billick]] gave the game ball to Wright's wife, for waiting until after the contest to induce labor.

The Ravens won five of their last six games with Wright posting a 5–2 record and having a critical role in the team reaching the playoffs, where they lost a close game against the [[Tennessee Titans]] with a score of 20–17, with the difference being a 46-yard field goal with 29 seconds left. He finished the season with 1,199 passing yards, 9 touchdowns and 8 interceptions.

Wright missed the 2004 season after having surgery to repair a torn labrum in his right shoulder. Following another injury to Boller during the first game of the 2005 season, he was named the starting quarterback but was again demoted after having a 2–5 record.

===Cincinnati Bengals===
With the departure of [[Carson Palmer]]'s former backup quarterback [[Jon Kitna]] to the [[Detroit Lions]], Wright signed a one-year deal with the [[Cincinnati Bengals]] on April 21, 2006, winning a competition with [[Craig Krenzel]] and [[Doug Johnson (American football)|Doug Johnson]] for the backup job.

===New York Giants===
On April 13, 2007, he signed as a [[free agent]] with the [[New York Giants]], throwing him into a four-quarterback scramble for roster spots with [[Eli Manning]], [[Tim Hasselbeck]], and [[Jared Lorenzen]]. He was named the third-string quarterback in a season that saw the team win [[Super Bowl XLII]], beating the previously undefeated [[New England Patriots]].

On August 18, 2008, Wright suffered a back injury in a preseason game against the [[Cleveland Browns]] and was eventually placed on the [[injured reserve list]] on August 30. He wasn't re-signed the next season and decided to announce his retirement.

'''Antonio Garay Jr.''' (born November 30, 1979) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[nose tackle]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He was selected by the [[Cleveland Browns]] in the sixth round of the [[2003 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=2003 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2003/draft.htm |access-date=2023-03-27 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> He played [[college football]] and [[Collegiate wrestling|wrestled]] for the [[Boston College Eagles]]. He was an [[NCAA Division I Wrestling Championships|NCAA wrestling]] All-American his sophomore year, placing 4th at the NCAA Championships while at Boston College.

Garay was also a member of the [[Chicago Bears]], [[San Diego Chargers]], and [[New York Jets]].

He is notable for his outrageous hairstyles and for driving a Hello Kitty-themed [[Smart Fortwo|smart car]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/nfl/blog/shutdown_corner/post/antonio-garay-the-nose-tackle-who-drives-a-hello-kitty-smart-car?urn=nfl,wp8318|title=Antonio Garay: The nose tackle who drives a Hello Kitty smart car|work=Yahoo Sports}}</ref>

==Early life==
Garay is Jewish.<ref name=JSR911>{{cite journal|title=2011 NFL Football Preview|journal=Jewish Sports Review|date=September{{ndash}}October 2011|volume=8|issue=87|pages=6–7}}</ref><ref name="chargers.com">{{cite web|url=http://www.chargers.com/team/roster/Antonio-Garay/GAR023506 |title=San Diego Chargers: Antonio Garay |access-date=2011-05-11 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101229112922/http://www.chargers.com/team/roster/Antonio-Garay/GAR023506 |archive-date=December 29, 2010 |df=mdy }}</ref><ref>''[[Jewish Sports Review]]'', September/October 2010, Vol. 7, Issue 81</ref>  Garay's mother is Jewish and his father is a Catholic of Jamaican, Costa Rican, and Puerto Rican descent.<ref name="chargers.com"/> He and his two siblings were exposed to both parents' faiths.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.theinsightfulplayer.com/post/antonio-garay|title=Antonio Garay|first=Chrissy|last=Carew|date=April 15, 2020|website=Insightful Player}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.signonsandiego.com/news/2010/aug/29/garays-comeback-wasnt-kids-play/|title=Comeback by Chargers' Garay wasn't kids' play|author=Chris Jenkins|work=U-T San Diego |date=August 29, 2025 }}</ref>  He attended [[Rahway High School]] in [[Rahway, New Jersey]], and was a standout offensive and defensive lineman.  He was also the NJSIAA {{convert|275|lb|abbr=on}}. state and national wrestling champion in 1998 and a high school All-American, winning the National High School Wrestling Tournament in Pittsburgh in 1998.<ref name=autogenerated1>{{Cite web|url=https://newspapers.bc.edu/?a=d&d=bcheights20000328.2.42|title=The Heights, Volume LXXXI, Number 009 — 28 March 2000 — Boston College Newspapers|website=newspapers.bc.edu}}</ref>

==College career==
He played [[college football]] and wrestled at [[Boston College]]. He was an NCAA wrestling All-American his sophomore year, placing 4th at the NCAA Championships while at Boston College in 2000. During the 2000 season, he was also named the Most Outstanding Wrestler at the [[East Coast Wrestling Association]] tournament (ECWA) for the second year.<ref name=autogenerated1 />

Garay spent two seasons with the [[Chicago Bears]] and was a member of the [[2006 Chicago Bears season|2006 NFC Championship team]].  In a December 2007 game against the [[Washington Redskins]], Garay was injured by an illegal block.  He was placed on injured reserve for the remainder of the 2007 season.  On March 8, 2008, the Chicago Bears announced that they would part ways with the defensive tackle, and he became an [[free agent|unrestricted free agent]] on February 29, 2008.

On October 20, 2009, the [[New York Jets]] announced that they had signed Garay to their practice squad.

Garay was signed off of the New York Jets' [[practice squad]] on December 9, 2009, by the [[San Diego Chargers]]. He was re-signed to a two-year deal on March 6, 2010. Garay was able to earn the starting job at nose tackle for the bulk of the 2010 season, and he finished 2010 with 48 tackles and 5.5 sacks, leading all San Diego defensive linemen in both categories.

Garay was signed by the Jets on March 15, 2013.<ref>{{cite news|title=Jets sign former Chargers nose tackle Antonio Garay |url=http://www.nj.com/jets/index.ssf/2013/03/jets_sign_former_chargets_nt_a.html |work=The Star-Ledger |author=Orr, Conor |date=March 15, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130321031740/http://www.nj.com/jets/index.ssf/2013/03/jets_sign_former_chargets_nt_a.html |archive-date=March 21, 2013 |access-date=March 15, 2013 |url-status=live |df=mdy }}</ref> He was released on August 31, 2013.<ref>{{cite web|title=Jets Move 22, Get Down to 53-Man Active Roster |url=http://www.newyorkjets.com/news/article-randylangefb/Jets-Move-22-Get-Down-to-53-Man-Active-Roster/0e4010de-3ce3-4e94-b5f8-13a17c710ba0 |author=Lange, Randy |date=31 August 2013 |publisher=New York Jets |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130903000730/http://www.newyorkjets.com/news/article-randylangefb/Jets-Move-22-Get-Down-to-53-Man-Active-Roster/0e4010de-3ce3-4e94-b5f8-13a17c710ba0 |archive-date=September 3, 2013 |access-date=1 September 2013 |url-status=dead |df=mdy }}</ref>

==Personal life==
Four of Garay's family members were athletes at [[Hofstra University]]: his father Tony and brother Daniel both played football and wrestled at Hofstra, his mother Marsha played softball and tennis at Hofstra, and his sister Francesca played volleyball there.<ref name="Hofstra"/> His cousin [[Carlos Garay]] played in the [[Arena Football League]].<ref name="Hofstra">{{cite web | url=https://gohofstra.com/news/2022/1/3/athletics-ath-hofstra-mourns-the-passing-of-tony-garay | title=ATH: Hofstra Mourns The Passing Of Tony Garay | publisher=gohofstra.com | date=January 3, 2022 | accessdate=5 December 2024}}</ref>

Sports}} After his playing career, he was a graduate assistant for the [[Texas A&M Aggies football|Texas A&M Aggies]]. ==Early life== Cromartie was born in [[Tallahassee, Florida]],{{Cite web |date=January 14, 2010 |title=NFL pledges $2.5M to aid Haiti earthquake relief efforts |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/nfl-pledges-2-5m-to-aid-haiti-earthquake-relief-efforts-09000d5d815bff52 |access-date=September 23, 2023 |website=NFL.com |language=en-US}}{{cite news|url=https://www.wsj.com/news/articles/SB125987130978175269 |title=These Days, Everybody's All-American Just May Be a Haitian |newspaper=Wall Street Journal |date=December 4, 2009 |access-date=March 10, 2014|last1=Millman |first1=Joel }} He was a versatile player at Tallahassee's [[Lincoln High School (Tallahassee, Florida)|Lincoln High School]]. This was enough to earn Cromartie 2002 ''[[USA Today]]'' defensive player of the year.{{cite news|url=https://www.usatoday.com/sports/preps/football/02allusa.htm|title=All-USA 2002 high school football team|date=May 20, 2005|publisher=USATODAY.com|access-date=May 6, 2008}} Considered a four-star recruit by ''[[Rivals.com]]'', Cromartie ranked sixth among cornerback prospects in the nation.{{cite web|title=Rivals.com Cornerbacks 2003|url=https://footballrecruiting.rivals.com/viewrank.asp?ra_key=179|work=Rivals.com|date=February 5, 2003}} Cromartie also participated in the 2003 [[U.S. Army All-American Bowl]]. Cromartie also ran [[Track and field|track]] in high school and placed 3rd in the 110-metres hurdles and as a member of the 4 x 100-metres relay team at the Class 5A County track meet. He also cleared 14.3 meters in [[triple jump]].{{cite web|url=http://fl.milesplit.com/athletes/2698-antonio-cromartie/feed#.VBc9a_mSwrk |title=Antonio Cromartie - Feed |access-date=September 15, 2014 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150402133848/http://fl.milesplit.com/athletes/2698-antonio-cromartie/feed |archive-date=April 2, 2015 }} ==College career== Cromartie decided to stay close to home for college and accepted an athletic scholarship offer from [[Florida State University]], where he played for coach [[Bobby Bowden]]'s [[Florida State Seminoles football]] team from 2003 to 2004. After flashing playmaking potential as a [[nickelback (American football)|nickelback]] and [[kick returner]] his first two years, Cromartie tore the [[Anterior cruciate ligament injury|anterior cruciate ligament]] in his left knee in July 2005 during voluntary workouts before his junior year and was forced to miss the entire 2005 season. He was potentially going to play at [[wide receiver]] during his junior year.[https://www.espn.com/college-football/news/story?id=2106962 ESPN - Cromartie to miss 2005 season. - College Football] In addition to football, Cromartie also joined the [[Florida State Seminoles]] track team in 2004. He was a member of the FSU track team that won the ACC Championship in 2004, where he placed 10th in the 200 meters with a time of 21.35 seconds.{{cite web|url=http://nc.milesplit.com/meets/7213/results/311711 |title=ACC Championships 2004 - Complete Results |access-date=September 15, 2014 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141015073609/http://nc.milesplit.com/meets/7213/results/311711 |archive-date=October 15, 2014 }} He ran a career-best time of 46.39 seconds in the [[400 meters]] at the NCAA Division I Championships, placing 6th in the prelims.{{cite web|url=http://fl.milesplit.com/meets/7396/results/15410 |title=NCAA D1 East Regional Championships- Collegiate Men |access-date=September 15, 2014 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141015073808/http://fl.milesplit.com/meets/7396/results/15410 |archive-date=October 15, 2014 }} He was timed at 21.27 seconds in the [[200 meters]]. ==Professional career== ===Pre-draft=== On March 16, 2006, Cromartie attended the [[NFL Scouting Combine]], but performed limited drills as he was only 8 months removed from his torn ACL that required him undergoing surgery. His 4.47s in the 40–yard dash was slower then normally expected with his background in track and field who was known especially for his speed. He decided against performing the short-shuttle and three-cone drill, but performed well in the broad jump, tying Ohio State's [[Donte Whitner]] for the second best broad jump among defensive backs with 11'0" with his FSU teammate [[Pat Watkins]] finishing first with 11'1".{{cite web| title=Jets' Combine Bests: Antonio Cromartie| url=https://www.newyorkjets.com/news/jets-combine-bests-antonio-cromartie-16835925 |access-date=June 12, 2025| website=newyorkjets.com| author=Randy Lange| date=February 17, 2016}} Cromartie performed at his [[pro day]] in 2006 for scouts.{{cite web|url=http://www.nfldraftscout.com/ratings/profile.php?pyid=8269|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060423012316/http://www.nfldraftscout.com/ratings/profile.php?pyid=8269|url-status=dead|archive-date=April 23, 2006|title=NFL Draft Scout, Powered by The SportsXchange - *Antonio Cromartie, CB, Florida State - Draft Profile|date=April 23, 2006|access-date=January 11, 2018}}[http://sfo.scout.com/2/525567.html Scout.com] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120217201038/http://sfo.scout.com/2/525567.html |date=February 17, 2012 }} {{NFL predraft | height ft = 6 | height in = 2 1/8 | weight = 208 | dash = 4.52 | ten split = 1.58 | twenty split = 2.63 | shuttle = 3.89 | cone drill = 7.02 | vertical = 38 | broad ft = 11 | broad in = 0 | bench = 18 | wonderlic = | arm span = 33 3/4 | hand span = 10 1/2 | note = All values from [[NFL Combine]]/[[Pro Day]]{{Cite web |url=https://www.nfl.com/prospects/antonio-cromartie/32004352-4f16-1100-3649-bf987cab65ab |title=Antonio Cromartie Draft and Combine Prospect Profile |website=NFL.com |access-date=October 23, 2021}}{{Cite web |url=http://draftscout.com/dsprofile.php?PlayerId=8269&DraftYear=2006 |title=Antonio Cromartie, Florida State, CB, 2006 NFL Draft Scout, NCAA College Football |website=draftscout.com |access-date=October 23, 2021}} }} ===San Diego Chargers=== ====2006==== The [[San Diego Chargers]] selected Cromartie in the first round (19th overall) in the [[2006 NFL draft]], despite being removed from competitive football for an entire year. He was the second cornerback drafted in 2006, following the [[Denver Broncos]] selecting [[Tye Hill]] (15th overall). The Chargers entered the 2006 NFL Draft without any glaring needs that needed immediate attention and were able to have the ability to make what was described as a "luxury pick" in Cromartie after he fell to them at 19th overall only due to his injury causing him to not play for 15 months and a delayed transition to the professional game due to his recovery.{{cite web| title=Grading Ancient History: The 2006 Chargers Draft| url=https://www.boltsfromtheblue.com/2013/7/18/4535514/2006-chargers-draft-cromartie-mcneill-clary |access-date=June 12, 2025| website=boltsfromtheblue.com| date=July 18, 2018}} [[File:Antonio Cromartie.jpg|thumb|right|Cromartie with the Chargers in 2007]] On July 25, 2006, the Chargers signed Cromartie to a five—year, $12.50 million rookie contract that included $7.35 million guaranteed.{{cite web| title=Spotrac.com: Antonio Cromartie contract| url=https://www.spotrac.com/nfl/player/_/id/3482/antonio-cromartie |access-date=June 12, 2025| website=Spotrac.com}} He was expected to compete against [[Drayton Florence]] for the role as the No. 2 starting cornerback, but was unable to fully participate physically for the majority of training camp as he continued to recover from his torn ACL. Head coach [[Marty Schottenheimer]] named him the starting nickelback and the third cornerback on the depth chart to begin the season, behind starting cornerbacks Drayton Florence and [[Quentin Jammer]].{{cite web| title=Cromartie's quite a catch| url=https://sports.yahoo.com/jc-chargers081906.html |access-date=June 12, 2025| website=sports.yahoo.com| date=August 16, 2006}} On September 11, 2006, Cromartie made his professional regular season debut in the [[2006 San Diego Chargers season|San Diego Chargers']] season-opener at the [[2006 Oakland Raiders season|Oakland Raiders]] as they won 27–0. On November 26, 2006, Cromartie had a 91–yard kick return for his best of the season and had three kick returns for a total of 130–yards as the Chargers defeated the Oakland Raiders 14–21.{{cite web| title=Oakland Raiders at San Diego Chargers - November 26th, 2006|url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200611260sdg.htm |access-date=June 12, 2025 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com}} In Week 16, he set a season-high with four solo tackles as the Chargers won 20–17 at the [[2006 Seattle Seahawks season|Seattle Seahawks]].{{cite web| title=Pro-Football-Reference: Antonio Cromartie Game Logs (2006) |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/C/CromAn20.htm |access-date=June 12, 2025 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com}} He finished his rookie season with only 24 combined tackles (20 solo) and made five pass deflections while appearing in all 16 games without a start under defensive coordinator [[Wade Phillips]]. He also played special teams as a kick returner for six games and finished with ten kick returns for 297–yards.{{cite web| title=Pro-Football-Reference: Antonio Cromartie Career Overview|url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/C/CromAn20.htm |access-date=June 12, 2025 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com}} ====2007==== On February 12, 2007, the San Diego Chargers unexpectedly fired head coach [[Marty Schottenheimer]] although they finished in first place in the [[AFC West]] with a 14–2 record. Before the start of OTAs and spring camp, Cromartie elected to change his jersey number, switching from the No. 25 he wore throughout his entire rookie season to No. 31. Although No. 31 was available in 2006, he opted to wear No. 25 instead. Throughout training camp, he competed against Drayton Florence for the role as the No. 2 starting cornerback under new defensive coordinator [[Ted Cottrell]]. Head coach [[Norv Turner]] named him the starting nickelback and the third outside cornerback on the depth chart to begin the season, behind Drayton Florence and Quentin Jammer.{{cite web| title=Ourlads.com: San Diego Chargers Depth Chart (09/02/2007)| url=https://www.ourlads.com/nfldepthcharts/archive/17/LAC |access-date=June 13, 2025| website=Ourlads.com}} {{quote box |align=right |width=50% |quote="I didn't know a lot about him, but as I started watching him I became aware that he was a real good athlete with good range, good hands and great speed. I thought, 'Man, we have the possibility of having a heck of a player, here.'" |source=–[[Ted Cottrell]] [[2007 San Diego Chargers season|(Chargers' defensive coordinator)]] }} In Week 6, Cromartie made three solo tackles, two pass deflections, and made the first interception of his career on a pass [[Daunte Culpepper]] threw to wide receiver [[Jerry Porter (American football)|Jerry Porter]] as the Chargers defeated the [[2007 Oakland Raiders season|Oakland Raiders]] 14–28.{{cite web| title=Oakland Raiders at San Diego Chargers - October 14th, 2007|url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200710140sdg.htm |access-date=June 12, 2025 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com}} On October 28, 2007, Cromartie made two solo tackles, three pass deflections, two interceptions, and two touchdowns during a 35–10 victory at the [[2007 Houston Texans season|Houston Texans]]. During the first quarter, Cromartie appeared on special teams acting as a blocker on the punt return team and scored his first career touchdown when punter [[Matt Turk]] botched his punt attempt by mishandling the set up, leading to a loose ball in the endzone that was recovered for a touchdown by Cromartie. He then had the first pick-six of his career when he picked off a pass [[Matt Schaub]] threw to wide receiver [[Kevin Walter]] and returned it 70–yards to score his second touchdown of the game.{{cite web| title=Houston Texans at San Diego Chargers - October 28th, 2007|url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200710280sdg.htm |access-date=June 12, 2025 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com}} On November 4, 2007, Cromartie recorded two solo tackles and made NFL history during a 57–yard field goal attempt by [[Minnesota Vikings]] kicker [[Ryan Longwell]] with four seconds remaining at the end on the second quarter before halftime. Special teams coordinator [[Steve Crosby]] strategically positioned Cromartie under the goal post in order to field the kick in the opportunity of the field goal attempt falling short. As expected, the 57–yard field goal attempt by Longwell did fall short, but required Cromartie to leap fully extended in order to keep the ball from exiting the endzone. Cromartie successfully made an acrobatic catch while landing with both his feet in bounds.{{cite web| title=Chargers cornerback's return longest play in NFL history| url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/news/story?id=3094481 |access-date=June 13, 2025| website=ESPN.com| author=O'Shea Jackson| date=November 4, 2007}} Starting nine yards deep at the back of the endzone, Cromartie took it up the right sideline and raced down the field, going untouched behind a few blocks as he returned the kick 100 yards for a touchdown to set the [[List of National Football League records (individual)|NFL record]] for the longest play in history with his entire kick return from the back of the endzone to the goal line being 109 yards in total, the maximum possible.{{cite web| title=Cromartie Returns Missed FG 109 Yards| url=https://www.nfl.com/100/originals/100-greatest/plays-88 |access-date=June 13, 2025| website=NFL.com| author=O'Shea Jackson| date=November 4, 2007}} The Chargers would lose 17–35 to the [[2007 Minnesota Vikings season|Minnesota Vikings]] at the [[Hubert H. Humphrey Metrodome|Metrodome]]. Barring any rule changes, Cromartie's 109–yard kick return for a touchdown can not be broken, only equaled as 109 yards is theoretically the maximum possible due to regulation lengths set for the field and endzone. His performance earned him Special Teams Player of the Week. Entering Week 10, head coach Norv Turner announced that Cromartie would make his first start in place of [[Quentin Jammer]], who remained inactive for two games (Weeks 10–11) due to a hamstring injury.{{cite web| title=Chargers cornerback's return longest play in NFL history| url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/news/story?id=3102914 |access-date=June 13, 2025| website=ESPN.com| author=O'Shea Jackson| date=November 4, 2007}} On November 11, 2007, Cromartie earned his first career start and recorded six solo tackles, set a season-high with four pass deflections, and set a career-high with three interceptions on passes thrown by [[Peyton Manning]] during a 21–23 win against the [[2007 Indianapolis Colts season|Indianapolis Colts]].[http://www.signonsandiego.com/sports/sullivan/20071112-9999-1s12sullivan.html SignOnSanDiego.com > Sports - Give Cromartie a party, more starts] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110604144851/http://www.signonsandiego.com/sports/sullivan/20071112-9999-1s12sullivan.html |date=June 4, 2011 }} At the beginning of the second quarter, Cromartie made a highlight-reel one-handed interception, leaping in front of wide receiver [[Reggie Wayne]] to pick off Peyton Manning for the third time.{{cite web| title=Indianapolis Colts at San Diego Chargers - November 11th, 2007 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200711110sdg.htm |access-date=June 12, 2025 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com}} Cromartie called the interception the best play of his short career.[https://www.espn.com/nfl/columns/story?columnist=clayton_john&id=3106487 ESPN - Cromartie's first start at corner a smash hit - NFL] He is the first player to intercept Peyton Manning three times in one game during the regular season, and earned Defensive Player of the Week honors for his performance in the game.[http://www.chargers.com/news/headlines/sproles-cromartie-earn.htm Chargers.com - News » Headlines » Sproles, Cromartie earn League honors] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071116073006/http://www.chargers.com/news/headlines/sproles-cromartie-earn.htm|date=November 16, 2007}} Entering Week 12, head coach Norv Turner demoted [[Drayton Florence]] and named Cromartie the No. 2 starting cornerback alongside Quentin Jammer for the last six games (Weeks 12–17) of the season.{{cite web| title=Team defense: Too much unpredictability to warrant high pick| url=https://www.espn.com/fantasy/football/ffl/story?page=nfldk2k8dstpreview |access-date=June 13, 2025| website=ESPN.com| author=Christopher Harris| date=June 17, 2008}} In Week 13, he made five solo tackles, two pass break-ups, and had two interceptions off passes by [[Tyler Thigpen]] during a 24–10 victory at the [[2007 Kansas City Chiefs season|Kansas City Chiefs]]. On December 16, 2007, Cromartie made six solo tackles, one pass deflection, and set a career-high with his tenth interception of the season on a pass by [[Jon Kitna]] to wide receiver [[Shaun McDonald (American football)|Shaun McDonald]] during a 51–14 win against the [[2007 Detroit Lions season|Detroit Lions]]. His tenth interception set a [[professional sports league organization|franchise]] record for most interceptions in a season, previously held by [[Charlie McNeil (American football)|Charlie McNeil]] with nine interceptions in [[1961 NFL season|1961]]. He finished the season with a total of 44 combined tackles (39 solo) in 16 games and eight starts. He set a career-highs in interceptions (10), pass deflections (18), fumble recoveries (2), and in total touchdowns (3). His breakout season in 2007 earned him an invitation to the [[2008 Pro Bowl]], marking the first [[Pro Bowl]] of his career and he was also selected as first-team All-Pro.{{cite web| title=This could be one of many Pro Bowls for Chargers' Cromartie| url=https://www.nfl.com/news/this-could-be-one-of-many-pro-bowls-for-chargers-cromartie-09000d5d806960d7 |access-date=June 13, 2025| website=NFL.com| date=February 8, 2008}} {{quote box | align = right | width = 50% | quote = ""He's a special player and a great athlete. He has the ability to be one of the top cover cornerbacks in this league for a long time." | source = –[[Peyton Manning]] (2009 Pro Bowl) }} The [[2007 San Diego Chargers season|San Diego Chargers]] finished in first place in the AFC West with an 11–5 record, earning a playoff berth. The Chargers defeated the [[2007 Tennessee Titans season|Tennessee Titans]] 17–6 in the AFC Wild-Card Game. On January 13, 2008, Cromartie started in the AFC Divisional Round and made six solo tackles, one pass break-up, a forced fumble, and intercepted a pass by Peyton Manning to wide receiver Reggie Wayne during a 28–24 victory at the [[2007 Indianapolis Colts season|Indianapolis Colts]]. During the second quarter, wide receiver [[Marvin Harrison]] had a 17–yard reception before Cromartie forced a fumble by Harrison that was recovered by Chargers' safety [[Marlon McCree]].{{cite web| title=Divisional Round - San Diego Chargers at Indianapolis Colts - January 13th, 2008|url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200801130clt.htm |access-date=June 12, 2025 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com}} On January 20, 2008, Cromartie started in the [[AFC Championship Game]] and led the team with nine combined tackles (seven solo), had one pass deflection, and intercepted a pass by [[Tom Brady]] to tight end [[Ben Watson (American football)|Ben Watson]] as the Chargers lost 12–21 at the [[2007 New England Patriots season|New England Patriots]].{{cite web| title=AFC Championship Game- San Diego Chargers at New England Patriots - January 20th, 2008|url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200801200nwe.htm |access-date=June 12, 2025 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com}} ====2008==== He entered training camp as a starting cornerback following the departure of [[Drayton Florence]]. The [[2008 San Diego Chargers season|San Diego Chargers]] selected [[Antoine Cason]] in the first round (27th overall) of the [[2008 NFL draft]] to replace Drayton Florence. Head coach Norv Turner named Cromartie and Quentin Jammer the starting cornerbacks to begin the season with Antoine Cason at nickelback.{{cite web| title=Ourlads.com: San Diego Chargers Depth Chart (08/31/2008)| url=https://www.ourlads.com/nfldepthcharts/archive/29/LAC |access-date=June 13, 2025| website=Ourlads.com}} On September 22, 2008, Cromartie had his best performance of the season, recording nine combined tackles (seven solo), set a season-high with four pass deflections, set a season-high with two interceptions, and returned one for a touchdown during a 48–29 victory against the [[2008 New York Jets season|New York Jets]]. He intercepted a pass by [[Brett Favre]] to wide receiver [[Laveranues Coles]] and returned it for a 52–yard touchdown in the second quarter.{{cite web| title=New York Jets at San Diego Chargers - September 22nd, 2008 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200809220sdg.htm |access-date=June 12, 2025 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com}} In Week 10, Cromartie set a season-high with 11 combined tackles (10 solo) and had one pass deflection during a 20–19 victory against the [[2008 Kansas City Chiefs season|Kansas City Chiefs]].{{cite web| title=Pro-Football-Reference: Antonio Cromartie Game Logs (2008) |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/C/CromAn20.htm |access-date=June 12, 2025 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com}} On October 28, 2008, Chargers' head coach Norv Turner fired [[Ted Cottrell]] and subsequently promoted inside linebackers coach [[Ron Rivera]].[https://www.espn.com/nfl/news/story?id=3669441 ESPN - Chargers fire Cottrell, name Rivera new defensive coordinator] He finished with a career-high of 64 combined tackles (60 solo), nine pass deflections, two interceptions, and a touchdown in 16 games and 15 starts. At the conclusion of the season, Cromartie stated that he had fractured his hip during the Chargers' 24–21 loss against the [[2008 Carolina Panthers season|Carolina Panthers]] and continued to play through the injury over the span of the entire season. Following his trade to the [[New York Jets]] in 2010, Cromartie claimed that his fractured hip in 2008 was initially hidden from him by team doctors that told Cromartie it was a [[hip flexor]].{{cite web| title=Antonio Cromartie on playing with the Chargers: 'I wasn't happy there.'| url=https://www.nydailynews.com/2011/10/20/antonio-cromartie-on-playing-with-the-chargers-i-wasnt-happy-there/ |access-date=June 13, 2025| website=MYDaulyNews.com| date=April 13, 2014}} ====2009==== He returned to training camp and was slated to be a starting cornerback, but had minor competition from [[Antoine Cason]]. Head coach [[Norv Turner]] retained Cromartie and [[Quentin Jammer]] as the starting cornerbacks to begin the season with Antoine Cason as the starting nickelback and primary backup cornerback.{{cite web|title=An Updated San Diego Chargers Depth Chart| url=https://www.boltsfromtheblue.com/2009/8/24/1000617/an-updated-san-diego-chargers |access-date=June 14, 2025| website=boltsfromtheblue.com| date=August 24, 2009| author= John Gennaro}} In Week 8, he made one solo tackle, a pass deflection, and had his first interception of the season during a pass attempt by [[JaMarcus Russell]] to tight end [[Zach Miller (tight end, born 1985)|Zach Miller]] on the opening drive im their 16–24.{{cite web| title=Oakland Raiders at San Diego Chargers - November 1st, 2025 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200911010sdg.htm |access-date=June 12, 2025 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com}} On November 15, 2009, Cromartie made one solo tackle, had one pass break-up, and sealed the Chargers 31–23 win against the [[2009 Philadelphia Eagles season|Philadelphia Eagles]] by intercepting a pass thrown by [[Donovan McNabb]] to wide receiver [[Jason Avant]] with two seconds remaining.{{cite web| title=Philadelphia Eagles at San Diego Chargers - November 15th, 2009 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200911150sdg.htm |access-date=June 12, 2025 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com}} He started in all 16 games throughout the [[2009 NFL season]] and finished with a total of 33 combined tackles (31 solo), made ten pass deflections, and had three interceptions.{{Cite web |title=Antonio Cromartie 2009 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/C/CromAn20/gamelog/2009/ |access-date=September 23, 2023 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}} ===New York Jets (first stint)=== ====2010==== On March 4, 2010, the [[New York Jets]] traded the [[2010 San Diego Chargers season|San Diego Chargers]] for Cromartie in exchange for a third-round pick in the [[2011 NFL draft]] that was upgraded into a 2011 second-round pick (61st overall) due to performance options based on Cromartie's performance in 2010.{{Cite web |last=Schefter |first=Adam |date=March 4, 2010 |title=Former All-Pro Cromartie headed to Jets|agency=Associated Press |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/news/story?id=4967508 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100307175513/http://sports.espn.go.com/nfl/news/story?id=4967508 |archive-date=March 7, 2010 |access-date=September 23, 2011 |website=ESPN.com}} He was signed to be their No. 2 starting cornerback following the departure of [[Lito Sheppard]]. He entered training camp slated as the ''de facto'' No. 2 starting cornerback even with the Jets selecting [[Kyle Wilson (cornerback)|Kyle Wilson]] in the first round (29th overall) of the [[2010 NFL draft]]. No. 1 starting cornerback [[Darrelle Revis]] did not attend training camp and did not appear in any of the preseason games as he held out for a contract extension with one—year remaining. Head coach [[Rex Ryan]] named Cromartie and Darrelle Revis the starting cornerbacks to begin the season.{{cite web| title=Ourlads.com: New York Jets Depth Chart (09/04/2010)| url=https://www.ourlads.com/nfldepthcharts/archive/111/nyj |access-date=June 14, 2025| website=Ourlads.com}} On September 13, 2010, Cromartie started in the [[2010 New York Jets season|New York Jets']] home-opener against the [[2010 Baltimore Ravens season|Baltimore Ravens]] and made two solo tackles, one pass deflection, and intercepted a pass by [[Joe Flacco]] to wide receiver [[Anquan Boldin]] for 66–yards as they lost 10–9.{{Cite web |date=September 13, 2010 |title=Ravens grind out victory over host Jets |url=http://scores.espn.go.com/nfl/recap?gameId=300913020 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100918031326/http://scores.espn.go.com/nfl/recap?gameId=300913020 |archive-date=September 18, 2010 |access-date=September 23, 2011 |website=ESPN.com |agency=Associated Press}} In Week 3, he set a season-high with six combined tackles (five solo) and made one pass deflection during a 31–23 victory at the [[2010 Miami Dolphins season|Miami Dolphins]]. In Week 5, Cromartie recorded one solo tackle and set a season-high with four pass deflections as the Jets defeated the [[2010 Minnesota Vikings season|Minnesota Vikings]] 29–20. Head coach Rex Ryan elected to rest starters, including Cromartie and Darrelle Revis in preparation for the playoffs and had them listed as healthy scratches as they routed the [[2010 Buffalo Bills season|Buffalo Bills]] 38–7 in Week 17. He finished the [[2010 NFL season]] with 42 combined tackles (41 solo), 18 pass deflections, and had three interceptions in 15 games and 15 starts.{{cite web|title=Source: Antonio Cromartie, Jets agree |url=https://www.espn.com/new-york/nfl/story/_/id/6822990/source-antonio-cromartie-new-york-jets-agree-new-deal |publisher=ESPN |author=Cimini, Rich |date=August 1, 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121107175710/http://espn.go.com/new-york/nfl/story/_/id/6822990/source-antonio-cromartie-new-york-jets-agree-new-deal |archive-date=November 7, 2012 |access-date=September 23, 2011 |url-status=live }} His kickoff return in the wild card round against the [[Indianapolis Colts]] helped to set up [[Nick Folk]]'s game-winning field goal.{{cite web|title=Cromartie is a hero ... on special teams |url=https://www.espn.com/new-york/nfl/columns/story?columnist=mcmanus_jane&id=6004415 |publisher=ESPN |author=McManus, Jane |date=January 9, 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110110194654/http://sports.espn.go.com/new-york/nfl/columns/story?columnist=mcmanus_jane&id=6004415 |archive-date=January 10, 2011 |access-date=September 23, 2011 |url-status=live }} ====2011==== On August 1, 2011, the [[2011 New York Jets season|New York Jets]] signed Cromartie to a four—year, $32.00 million contract extension that included $12.80 million guaranteed and an initial [[signing bonus]] of $5.00 million. He returned as the No. 2 starting cornerback to begin the season, alongside Darrelle Revis and nickelback Kyle Wilson. On September 18, 2011, Cromartie made three combined tackles (two solo), two pass deflections, and set a season-high with two interceptions on passes thrown by [[Luke McCown]] as the Jets defeated the [[2011 Jacksonville Jaguars season|Jacksonville Jaguars]] 32–3.{{cite news|title=Antonio Cromartie rebounds from poor performance vs. Cowboys to dominate Jaguars for NY Jets |url=http://www.nydailynews.com/sports/football/jets/2011/09/19/2011-09-19_cromartie_picks_up_his_game.html |work=New York Daily News |author=Ackert, Kristie |date=September 19, 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110927044023/http://www.nydailynews.com/sports/football/jets/2011/09/19/2011-09-19_cromartie_picks_up_his_game.html |archive-date=September 27, 2011 |access-date=September 23, 2011 |url-status=live }} His performance earned him the AFC Defensive Player of the Week for his performance against the Jaguars in Week 2.{{cite news|title=Nick Mangold lobbying to play vs. Raiders, giving Colin Baxter pointers |url=http://www.nydailynews.com/blogs/jets/2011/09/nick-mangold-lobbying-to-play-vs-raiders-giving-colin-baxter-pointers |work=New York Daily News |author=Armstrong, Kevin |date=September 21, 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110928120630/http://www.nydailynews.com/blogs/jets/2011/09/nick-mangold-lobbying-to-play-vs-raiders-giving-colin-baxter-pointers |archive-date=September 28, 2011 |access-date=September 23, 2011 |url-status=live }} In Week 3, Cromartie set a season-high with nine combined tackles (six solo), but also committed four errant penalties for 46–yards and also fumbled a kickoff return which resulted in a turnover that led to a Raiders go-ahead touchdown during their 24–34 loss at the [[2011 Oakland Raiders season|Oakland Raiders]]. He left the game in the second half and was transported to Eden Medical Center where he was diagnosed with bruised ribs and a [[pulmonary contusion]].{{cite web|title=Antonio Cromartie bruised lung, ribs |url=https://www.espn.com/new-york/nfl/story/_/id/7023812/new-york-jets-mark-sanchez-broke-nose-antonio-cromartie-bruised-lung |publisher=ESPN |author1=Begley, Ian |author2=Mike Mazzeo |date=September 26, 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110928042056/http://espn.go.com/new-york/nfl/story/_/id/7023812/new-york-jets-mark-sanchez-broke-nose-antonio-cromartie-bruised-lung |archive-date=September 28, 2011 |access-date=September 26, 2011 |url-status=live }} He started in all 16 games throughout the [[2011 NFL season]] and finished with 45 combined tackles (36 solo), 12 pass deflections, and made four interceptions. ====2012==== He returned as the No. 2 starting cornerback to begin the season, alongside Darrell Revis. On September 9, 2012, Cromartie started in the [[2012 New York Jets season|New York Jets']] home-opener against the [[2012 Buffalo Bills season|Buffalo Bills]] and made four combined tackles (two solo), one pass deflection, and had a pick-six when he intercepted a pass by [[Ryan Fitzpatrick]] to wide receiver [[David Nelson (wide receiver)|David Nelson]] and returned it 40–yards for a touchdown during their 48–28 victory. On October 12, 2012, the Jets placed Darrell Revis on injured reserve after he tore his ACL in Week 3 during a 23–20 overtime victory at the [[2012 Miami Dolphins season|Miami Dolphins]]. Head coach [[Rex Ryan]] subsequently named Cromartie the No. 1 starting cornerback for the rest of the season, alongside [[Kyle Wilson (cornerback)|Kyle Wilson]]. On October 14, 2012, Cromartie made four combined tackles (three solo), set a season-high with two pass deflections, and intercepted a pass by [[Andrew Luck]] to wide receiver [[Reggie Wayne]] during a 35–9 victory against the [[2012 Indianapolis Colts season|Indianapolis Colts]]. He started in all 16 games throughout the [[2012 NFL season]] and finished with a total of 35 combined tackles (30 solo), made 13 pass deflections, and had three interceptions. He was named to the [[2013 Pro Bowl]], marking the second of his career. ====2013==== The [[2013 New York Jets season|New York Jets]] made multiple changes following the [[2012 NFL season]], including the departure of [[Darrelle Revis]] and defensive coordinator [[Mike Pettine]] after he accepted the head coach position with the [[2013 Cleveland Browns season|Cleveland Browns]]. Defensive backs coach [[Dennis Thurman]] received a promotion to defensive coordinator and the Jets went on to select [[Dee Millner]] with the ninth overall pick in the [[2013 NFL draft]]. Head coach Rex Ryan named Cromartie the No. 1 starting cornerback to begin the season and paired him with Dee Millner.{{cite web| title=New York Jets Release 2013 Depth Chart| url=https://www.jetnation.com/2013/09/03/ny-jets-release-the-2013-depth-chart-include-a-few-surprises/ |access-date=June 16, 2025| website=JetsNation.com| date=September 3, 2013}} On November 3, 2013, Cromartie made one solo tackle, a pass deflection, and intercepted a pass by [[Drew Brees]] to wide receiver [[Nick Toon]] as the Jets defeated the [[2013 New Orleans Saints season|New Orleans Saints]] 26–20.{{cite web| title=New Orleans Saints at New York Jets - November 3rd, 2013|url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201311030nyj.htm |access-date=June 16, 2025| website=Pro-Football-Reference.com}} In Week 11, he set a season-high with five solo tackles and made two pass deflections during a 14–37 loss at the [[2013 Buffalo Bills season|Buffalo Bills]]. The following week, he recorded two solo tackles, set a season-high with two pass deflections, and intercepted a pass by [[Joe Flacco]] to wide receiver [[Marlon Brown]] during a 3–19 loss at the [[2013 Baltimore Ravens season|Baltimore Ravens]] in Week 12. He finished the [[2013 NFL season]] with 38 combined tackles (35 solo), made nine pass deflections, and three interceptions. He was selected as an alternate to the [[2014 Pro Bowl]], for the third selection of his career. On March 9, 2014, the [[2014 New York Jets season|New York Jets]] released Cromartie.{{cite web|title=Jets release Antonio Cromartie |url=https://www.espn.com/new-york/nfl/story/_/id/10578545/antonio-cromartie-released-new-york-jets |publisher=ESPN New York |author=Cimini, Rich |date=March 9, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140309214324/http://espn.go.com/new-york/nfl/story/_/id/10578545/antonio-cromartie-released-new-york-jets |archive-date=March 9, 2014 |access-date=March 9, 2014 |url-status=live }} ===Arizona Cardinals=== On March 19, 2014, the [[Arizona Cardinals]] signed Cromartie to a one—year, $3.50 million contract that included $3.25 million guaranteed and a signing bonus of $1 million.[http://www.azcardinals.com/news-and-events/article-2/Cardinals-Land-Antonio-Cromartie/4c50ec93-c5c6-4211-bb2d-785200c3113a Cardinals Land Antonio Cromartie] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304083303/http://www.azcardinals.com/news-and-events/article-2/Cardinals-Land-Antonio-Cromartie/4c50ec93-c5c6-4211-bb2d-785200c3113a |date=March 4, 2016 }} He entered training camp slated as the No. 2 starting cornerback under defensive coordinator [[Todd Bowles]]. '''Antone Smith''' (born September 17, 1985) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[running back]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Florida State Seminoles football|Florida State Seminoles]]. Smith was signed by the [[Detroit Lions]] as an [[undrafted free agent]] in 2009. He was also a member of the [[Minnesota Vikings]], [[Houston Texans]], [[Atlanta Falcons]], [[Chicago Bears]], [[New York Jets]], and [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]].

==Early life==
In his senior year at [[Pahokee High School]], Smith led Pahokee to the state football title and rushed for 276 yards and three touchdowns in the championship game, finishing with 2,814 yards and 44 touchdowns on the season. During his four-year high school playing career he compiled over 6000 rushing yards.

Smith was ranked as the number 25 player overall by Rivals.com. He was a [[Parade (magazine)|Parade]] All-American, the [[Palm Beach County]] Player of the Year, the [[Old Spice]] National Player of the Year, and was voted as Mr. Football for the state of Florida. Smith was voted the [[Most valuable player|MVP]] of the [[Nike, Inc.|Nike]] Camp and while there recorded an extremely fast 40-yard dash time of 4.25. He played in the CaliFlorida Bowl and was named the offensive MVP.

Smith was also on the school's [[track and field|track]] team, where he competed as a sprinter. At the 2003 FHSAA 2A Region 4 Championships, he won both the [[100 meters|100-meter dash]] and [[200 meters|200-meter dash]] with career-best times of 10.63 seconds and 21.71 seconds.<ref>{{Cite web |title=FHSAA 2A Region 4 – Boys (Raw) |url=http://fl.milesplit.com/meets/4389/results/8126}}</ref> He also spent a part of the spring with Florida State's track team. He finished fifth in the [[60 meters|60-meter dash]] at the 2006 ACC Championships, with a personal-best time of 6.83 seconds.<ref>{{Cite web |title=ACC Championships – Complete Results |url=http://va.milesplit.com/meets/15545/results/311650 |access-date=2025-03-26 |website=MileSplit VA}}</ref>

Smith was the focus and narrator of "The Muck Bowl," an independently produced feature-length documentary.

==College career==
During his freshman year at Florida State in 2005, Smith saw action in nine games, playing behind [[Lorenzo Booker]] and [[Leon Washington]]. He carried the ball 36 times for 188 yards (5.2 avg) and three touchdowns, and was third on team behind Booker and Washington in carries, rushing yards, and yards per game. In Florida State's 55–24 blowout win over [[Duke University]], Smith ran seven times for a season-high 76 yards and two [[touchdown]]s, the second of which came on a season-long 45-yard run where he eluded multiple Duke defenders.

As a senior, Smith led the ACC in touchdowns with 15, with 792 rushing yards on 177 carries (for a 4.5 yd average).<ref>{{Cite web |date=December 3, 2018 |title=Florida State Seminoles Official Athletic Site |url=http://www.seminoles.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=32900&ATCLID=209587848 |website=Florida State Seminoles}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Antone Smith College Stats, School, Draft, Gamelog, Splits |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/antone-smith-1.html |access-date=2024-12-30 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

Smith ended his career with 2,253 rushing yards and 26 touchdowns.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Antone Smith |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/player/_/id/13158/antone-smith |website=ESPN.com}}</ref>

'''Antoine Akeem Bethea'''<ref>{{cite web | title=ESPN Profile | work= ESPN.com | url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/player/_/id/9793 }}</ref> ({{IPAc-en|b|ə|ˈ|θ|eɪ}}; born July 27, 1984) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[safety (gridiron football position)|safety]] for 14 seasons in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Howard Bison football|Howard Bison]] and was selected by the [[Indianapolis Colts]] in the sixth round of the [[2006 NFL draft]]. Bethea also played for the [[San Francisco 49ers]], [[Arizona Cardinals]], and [[New York Giants]]. He was selected for the [[Pro Bowl]] three times and won [[Super Bowl XLI]] as a member of the Colts, beating the [[Chicago Bears]].

==College career==
Bethea attended [[Howard University]], where he majored in administration of justice, and played for the [[Howard Bison football]] team.  He started 31 of 37 games at safety. His freshman year, he saw action in five games as a backup in the secondary collecting 13 total tackles. He would have a career-best 109 total tackles his sophomore year while seeing action as a starter in 10 of 11 games that year. That year, he had three games where he tallied 13 tackles and another game against [[Bethune-Cookman]] where he made 14 tackles. He ended that year also adding one sack, three forced fumbles, two fumble recoveries, six pass deflections and a blocked kick.

He would record three interceptions his junior year, along with two sacks, four forced fumbles and eight pass deflections in 11 starts. Ending the year with 99 total tackles and two sacks, Bethea would earn All-Mid-Eastern Conference honors and selection to the American Urban Radio Network Sheridan Broadcasting Network Black College All-American Team joining the likes of NFL greats such as former [[Tennessee Titans|Houston Oilers/Tennessee Titans]] quarterback and NFL MVP [[Steve McNair]] and NFL tight end, [[Shannon Sharpe]]. He would earn these honors three years in a row.

Bethea would continue his success in his senior season, collecting 88 tackles, six passes defensed and a career-high four interceptions in 10 games. This would mark the third straight year he would lead his team in tackles. His senior season performance would earn him 1st-Team All-America honors from the NFL Draft Report.

As a three-year starter at Howard, Bethea made 309 stops that included 187 solo tackles and twelve for a loss, seven forced fumbles, two fumble recoveries, 18 passes defensed and seven interceptions. He also returned two recoveries for a touchdown: one coming on a blocked kick and the other on a fumble recovery, both returned 26 yards.<ref name="colts.com">[http://www.colts.com/sub.cfm?page=bio&player_id=385 Colts.com] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081028152217/http://www.colts.com/sub.cfm?page=bio&player_id=385 |date=October 28, 2008 }}</ref>

==Professional career==
Bethea was projected to be a third- or fourth-round pick by the majority of NFL draft experts and scouts. He was ranked as the sixth best free safety prospect in the draft by DraftScout.com and was ranked the 17th best safety in the draft by [[ESPN|ESPN Scouts Inc.]]<ref>{{cite web| title=Antoine Bethea, DS #6 FS, Howard| url=http://draftscout.com/ratings/dsprofile.php?pyid=55512&draftyear=2006&genpos=| access-date=May 4, 2018| website=draftscout.com}}</ref><ref>{{cite web| title=ESKN Draft Card: Antoine Bethea (Howard)| url=http://espn.com/nfl/draftcard?playerId=9802&src=desktop| access-date=May 4, 2018| website=ESPN.com}}{{dead link|date=July 2024|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref>
