===Tennessee Titans===
After going undrafted in the [[2005 NFL draft]], Harris was signed by the [[Tennessee Titans]] as an [[undrafted free agent]] on April 28. He was waived on August 29.<ref>{{cite news |title=TRANSACTIONS |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2005/08/30/sports/transactions.html |work=[[The New York Times]] |date=August 30, 2005 |access-date=July 29, 2010}}</ref> The team re-signed him to the [[practice squad]] on November 1, where he spent the remainder the season.

Harris was re-signed by the Titans on January 13, 2006. He was waived on September 2<ref>{{cite news
 |title=Titans Waive 22 Including Calico, Payton, Fleming 
 |url=http://www.ketv.com/nfl/9782807/detail.html 
 |work=ketv.com 
 |date=September 2, 2006 |access-date=July 29, 2010 
 |url-status=dead 
 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120306060143/http://www.ketv.com/nfl/9782807/detail.html 
 |archive-date=March 6, 2012 }}</ref> but re-signed to the practice squad the following day,<ref>{{cite news |title=NFL: Titans add five players; form practice squad |url=http://www.noticias.info/Archivo/2006/200609/20060904/20060904_215470.shtm |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191209090835/http://www.noticias.info/Archivo/2006/200609/20060904/20060904_215470.shtm |url-status=dead |archive-date=December 9, 2019 |work=noticias.info |date=September 3, 2006 |access-date=July 29, 2010 }}</ref> where he spent the entire 2006 regular season.

===Atlanta Falcons===
Harris was signed with the [[Atlanta Falcons]] on January 10, 2007. He appeared in 13 games for the Falcons in 2007, recording 10 tackles (seven solo) and pass defensed.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Antoine Harris 2007 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/H/HarrAn98/gamelog/2007/ |access-date=2025-05-11 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

In 2008, Harris appeared in 12 games for the Falcons and recorded three tackles. He was placed on season-ending [[injured reserve]] with a groin injury on December 9.<ref>{{cite news |title=Tuesday's sports transactions |url=http://www.pittsburghlive.com/x/pittsburghtrib/sports/s_602345.html |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=December 10, 2008 |access-date=July 29, 2010 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20130131145519/http://www.pittsburghlive.com/x/pittsburghtrib/sports/s_602345.html |archive-date=January 31, 2013 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

Harris was re-signed to a one-year contract on March 3, 2009.<ref>{{cite news |title=Falcons re-sign nine players |url=http://www.espnstar.com/us-sports/news/detail/item215103/Falcons-re-sign-nine-players/ |work=espnstar.com |date=March 4, 2009 |access-date=July 29, 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120324205130/http://www.espnstar.com/us-sports/news/detail/item215103/Falcons-re-sign-nine-players/ |archive-date=March 24, 2012 |url-status=usurped }}</ref> On December 21, he was placed on injured reserve due to a knee injury.<ref>{{cite news |author=Ledbetter, D. Orlando |title=Lofton turning in Pro Bowl worthy season |url=http://www.ajc.com/sports/atlanta-falcons/lofton-turning-in-pro-252757.html |work=[[The Atlanta Journal-Constitution]] |date=December 22, 2009 |access-date=July 29, 2010}}</ref>

===Philadelphia Eagles===
Harris was signed by the [[Philadelphia Eagles]] on July 29, 2010.<ref>{{cite news |author=Domowitch, Paul |title=Eagles add safety Harris |url=http://www.philly.com/philly/sports/blogs/Eagles_add_safety_harris.html |work=philly.com |date=July 29, 2010 |access-date=July 29, 2010}}</ref> He suffered a [[Lisfranc sprain]] during a preseason game against the [[Jacksonville Jaguars]] on August 14, and was placed on [[injured reserve]] on August 15.<ref>{{cite news |author=McPherson, Chris |title=Harris Placed On IR; Safeties Worked Out |url=http://www.philadelphiaeagles.com/news/Story.asp?story_id=21592 |work=philadelphiaeagles.com |date=August 15, 2010 |access-date=August 15, 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100822010853/http://www.philadelphiaeagles.com/news/Story.asp?story_id=21592 |archive-date=August 22, 2010 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

Harris now lives in Georgia, US with his wife and two children.

'''Antonio Edwards''' (born March 10, 1970) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[defensive end]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) for the [[Seattle Seahawks]], the [[New York Giants]], [[Atlanta Falcons]], and [[Carolina Panthers]].  He played [[college football]] for the [[Valdosta State Blazers football|Valdosta State Blazers]] and was selected in eighth round of the [[1993 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=1993 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/1993/draft.htm |access-date=2023-03-31 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>  In 2000, Edwards was the twelfth pick of the [[XFL (2001)|XFL]] [[2001 XFL Draft|draft]] as a member of the [[Las Vegas Outlaws (XFL)|Las Vegas Outlaws]].  Edwards is currently the defensive line [[Coach (sport)|coach]] of the [[Collegiate School (Richmond, Virginia)|Collegiate School]] in [[Richmond, Virginia]].

==Early life==
Edwards attended Colquitt County High School in Moultrie, Georgia, and was a student and a [[Letterman (sports)|letterman]] in [[high school football|football]].

==Personal life==
Edwards was a criminal justice major at [[Valdosta State University]]. While a member of the Seahawks, Antonio sponsored a reading enrichment program and helped build a playground at Brighton Elementary School in Seattle. He has a son Amahn and a daughter named Ashanti.

'''Antonio Donnell Armstrong''' (born '''Antonio Donnell Shorter'''; October 15, 1973 {{ndash}} July 29, 2016) was an American professional [[gridiron football|football]] [[linebacker]] who played in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) and [[Canadian Football League]] (CFL).

==Early life and college==
Armstrong started at [[Kashmere High School]] and signed with nearby [[Texas A&M Aggies football|Texas A&M]]. As a junior at A&M, Armstrong earned Defensive Player of the Game honors after making eight [[Tackle (football move)|tackles]] and three [[Quarterback sack|sacks]] in the 1994 [[Cotton Bowl Classic]] against [[Notre Dame Fighting Irish|Notre Dame]]. Armstrong earned [[Associated Press|AP]] [[All-America]] honors his senior year (1994) after making 62 tackles, including 17 behind the [[line of scrimmage]] as a senior. He was a semifinalist for the [[Butkus Award]] that year, and was a two-time All-[[Southwest Conference|SWC]] selection.

===National Football League===
Armstrong was selected in the sixth round of the [[1995 NFL draft]] by the [[San Francisco 49ers]], but fractured his ankle on the third day of [[Training camp (National Football League)|training camp]] and was signed to the practice squad.<ref>{{Cite web |title=1995 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/1995/draft.htm |access-date=2023-03-31 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> He was released from the practice squad on October 15, 1995. On October 16, he was signed to the [[Miami Dolphins]]' [[Scout team|practice squad]] and placed on the active roster a week later. Armstrong appeared in four games that season for the Dolphins and recorded four solo tackles. He was signed by the [[St. Louis Rams]] the following year, but was released after training camp.

===Canadian Football League===
Armstrong signed with the [[British Columbia Lions]] of the Canadian Football League in 1998 and made an immediate impact as a [[Starting lineup|starter]] for two seasons with the team. In 2000, Armstrong was traded to the [[Winnipeg Blue Bombers]]. He was Winnipeg's defensive player of the year and an [[Canadian Football League East Division|East Division]] All-star in 2000. On October 15, 2000, Armstrong suffered a fracture of his left ankle. The injury essentially ended his career, although he re-signed with the Bombers in September 2001 and started in the [[89th Grey Cup|2001 Grey Cup]] game. In 2002, Armstrong retired due to both a contract dispute and the physical limitations caused by his ankle injury two years before.

==Death==
Armstrong was shot along with his wife, Dawn Armstrong in Houston, Texas, on July 29, 2016. Dawn was pronounced dead at the scene in her bedroom. Antonio was transported to [[Memorial Hermann]] in critical condition and later died at age 42.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://sportsday.dallasnews.com/college-sports/texasamaggies/2016/07/29/report-former-texas-am-lb-antonio-armstrong-wife-shot-son|title=Report: Former Texas A&M LB Antonio Armstrong and his wife shot by son|date=July 29, 2016|work=[[The Dallas Morning News]]|accessdate=July 29, 2016|archive-date=April 16, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190416095943/https://sportsday.dallasnews.com/college-sports/texasamaggies/2016/07/29/report-former-texas-am-lb-antonio-armstrong-wife-shot-son|url-status=dead}}</ref> Their 16-year-old son AJ (Antonio Armstrong Jr.) was charged with murder.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.kagstv.com/news/crime/double-shooting-wife-husband-sw-houston-home-1/284299643|title=16-year-old charged with shooting his parents near Bellaire|date=July 29, 2016|publisher=[[KAGS-LD|KAGS]]|accessdate=July 29, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161029003443/http://www.kagstv.com/news/crime/double-shooting-wife-husband-sw-houston-home-1/284299643|archive-date=October 29, 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref>

The first two murder trials ended in mistrials. In 2019, the first jury deadlocked after failing to reach a unanimous verdict, with eight jurors voting guilty, and four voting not guilty. In the 2022 retrial, a second set of jurors was also unable to reach a verdict, with four convinced of AJ Armstrong's guilt, and the other eight, while not believing he was innocent, convinced that the defense had introduced reasonable doubt.<ref name="Hensley2022-10-26">{{Cite web| last = Hensley| first = Nicole| title = Second mistrial declared in Antonio Armstong Jr. trial, accused of killing his Houston parents| work = Houston Chronicle| accessdate = 2023-08-17| date = 2022-10-26| url = https://www.houstonchronicle.com/news/houston-texas/crime/article/antonio-armstrong-mistrial-murder-parents-17536588.php}}</ref>

In 2023, a third trial focused on the alarm system, which showed no activity or signs of an intruder on the first floor of the residence, as well as newly discovered DNA evidence revealing the presence of Armstrong Sr.'s blood on his son's shirt.<ref name="Hensley2023-08-16" /> On August 16, 2023, AJ Armstrong was found guilty of murdering both his parents and was immediately sentenced to life in prison, with the possibility of parole after 40 years. Because he was a minor at the time he committed the murders, the death penalty was not an option.<ref name="FOXGaydos">{{Cite web |last=Gaydos |first=Ryan |date=2023-08-17 |title=Son of ex-NFL player found guilty of killing parents, sentenced to life in prison |url=https://www.foxnews.com/sports/son-ex-nfl-player-found-guilty-killing-parents-sentenced-life-prison |access-date=2023-08-17 |website=Fox News |language=en-US}}</ref> Jurors told prosecutors that they had been convinced of AJ Armstrong's guilt due to his 911 call, his interview with investigators, and the fact that he had set a fire in the house and test-fired the murder weapon in the days before he had killed his parents.<ref name="Hensley2023-08-16">{{Cite web| last = Hensley| first = Nicole| title = Antonio Armstrong Jr. found guilty in third capital murder trial over 2016 deaths of parents| work = Houston Chronicle| accessdate = 2023-08-17| date = 2023-08-16| url = https://www.houstonchronicle.com/news/houston-texas/crime/article/antonio-armstrong-jr-verdict-third-trial-18299279.php}}</ref>

'''Antoine Caldwell''' (born April 19, 1986) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[Center (American football)|center]] and [[Guard (American football)|guard]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Alabama Crimson Tide football|Alabama Crimson Tide]], earning consensus [[College Football All-America Team|All-American]] honors in 2008.  He was selected by the [[Houston Texans]] in the third round of the [[2009 NFL draft]].

He was also a member of the [[Buffalo Bills]] and [[Jacksonville Jaguars]].

==Early life==
Caldwell was born in [[Montgomery, Alabama]].  He attended [[Robert E. Lee High School (Montgomery, Alabama)|Robert E. Lee High School]] in [[Montgomery, Alabama|Montgomery]], where he was a standout lineman for his [[high school football]] team. Considered a three-star recruit by [[Rivals.com]], Caldwell was listed as the No. 10 center prospect of his class.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/ncaa/football/recruiting/rankings/rank-527 |title=Archived copy |access-date=April 22, 2014 |archive-date=May 31, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160531001913/https://sports.yahoo.com/ncaa/football/recruiting/rankings/rank-527 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

==College career==
Caldwell received an [[athletic scholarship]] to attend the [[University of Alabama]], where he played for coach [[Mike Shula]] and coach [[Nick Saban]]'s [[Alabama Crimson Tide football]] teams from 2005 to 2008.  As a senior in 2008, he was recognized as a first-team [[List of All-SEC football teams|All-Southeastern Conference]] (SEC) selection and a consensus first-team [[College Football All-America Team|All-American]].

==Professional career==

===Houston Texans===
Caldwell was graded as the No. 3 center available in the [[2009 NFL draft]], behind [[Alex Mack]] and [[Eric Wood]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=View Draft by Positions - 2009 Draft Tracker - SI.com |url=http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/football/2009/draft/breakdowns/by_position/C.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121112131445/http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/football/2009/draft/breakdowns/by_position/C.html |archive-date=November 12, 2012 |access-date=December 11, 2012}}</ref> As projected, he was the third center selected off the board, in the third round by the [[Houston Texans]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=2009 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2009/draft.htm |access-date=February 25, 2019 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

From 2009 to 2012, Caldwell played 39 games, including 19 starts, for the Texans.<ref>[http://www.nfl.com/player/antoinecaldwell/71239/profile "Antoine Caldwell"]. nfl.com. Retrieved February 8, 2013.</ref>

===Buffalo Bills===
Caldwell signed with the [[Buffalo Bills]] on July 28, 2013.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Brown |first=Chris |date=July 28, 2013 |title=Bills sign OL Antoine Caldwell, Tony Hills |url=http://www.buffalobills.com/news/article-2/Bills-sign-OL-Antoine-Caldwell-Tony-Hills/6ab5e237-f35b-45df-8ea6-9ee167040b42 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130731225718/http://www.buffalobills.com/news/article-2/Bills-sign-OL-Antoine-Caldwell-Tony-Hills/6ab5e237-f35b-45df-8ea6-9ee167040b42 |archive-date=July 31, 2013 |access-date=July 29, 2013 |website=BuffaloBills.com}}</ref> He was released on August 30, 2013.<ref name="a357">{{cite web | last=Brown | first=Chris | title=Bills release Leinart among 18 player cuts | website=BuffaloBills.com| date=2013-08-30 | url=https://www.buffalobills.com/news/bills-release-leinart-among-18-player-cuts-11019575 | access-date=2024-10-31}}</ref>

===Jacksonville Jaguars===
In May 2014, Caldwell went to Jaguars Rookie Mini-Camp on a tryout basis. He was not offered on contract. However, he was signed to the active roster on August 13, 2014. The Jaguars released Caldwell on August 24, 2014.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Oehser |first=John |date=August 24, 2014 |title=CB Mike Harris among 11 players released |url=http://www.jaguars.com/news/article-JaguarsNews/CB-Mike-Harris-among-11-players-released/84f13d9c-d7ac-4905-88ed-faa71930f994 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140826114703/http://www.jaguars.com/news/article-JaguarsNews/CB-Mike-Harris-among-11-players-released/84f13d9c-d7ac-4905-88ed-faa71930f994 |archive-date=August 26, 2014 |access-date=August 24, 2014 |website=Jaguars.com}}</ref>

'''Antonio Coleman''' (born September 1, 1986) is an American former professional [[gridiron football|football]] player who was a [[defensive end]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Auburn Tigers football|Auburn Tigers]], was named to the ''[[Associated Press]]'' [[List of All-SEC football teams|All-Southeastern Conference]] football first-team in 2008<ref>{{cite web | title=Coleman, Marks Named To Associated Press All-SEC Team | url=http://auburntigers.cstv.com/sports/m-footbl/spec-rel/120808aaa.html | date=December 8, 2008 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081218013738/http://auburntigers.cstv.com/sports/m-footbl/spec-rel/120808aaa.html | archive-date=December 18, 2008 | url-status=dead }}</ref> and was considered one of the top [[outside linebacker]] prospects for the [[2010 NFL draft]].<ref name="CooneyUSAToday">{{cite news |first=Frank |last=Cooney |title=Who's next? Looking ahead to the best of the 2010 draft class |url=https://www.usatoday.com/sports/football/nfl/2009-05-05-2010-draft-preview_N.htm |work=[[USA Today]] |date=May 11, 2009 }}</ref>

He was a member of the [[Buffalo Bills]], [[New York Giants]] and [[Arizona Cardinals]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL), the [[Sacramento Mountain Lions]] of the [[United Football League (2009–2012)|United Football League]] (UFL), and the [[Saskatchewan Roughriders]] and [[Hamilton Tiger-Cats]] of the [[Canadian Football League]] (CFL).

==College career==
Coleman led Auburn with six sacks and 10.5 tackles for loss in 2008. He finished the season with 46 tackles (29 solo, 17 assists) and had a team-high 13 quarterback hurries, as well as a forced fumble and a pass break-up. He was named the SEC's Defensive Lineman of the Week following Auburn's 14–12 victory over Tennessee September 27 after completing four tackles including a sack and 1.6 tackles for loss.

Coleman was named to the [[ESPN.com]] 2009 preseason All-SEC first-team.<ref>{{cite news|first=Chris |last=Low |title=ESPN.com's preseason All-SEC team |url=http://myespn.go.com/blogs/secconf/0-8-86/ESPN-com-s-preseason-All-SEC-team.html |publisher=[[ESPN]] |date=August 14, 2009 }} {{dead link|date=July 2017 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref> Despite having a cast on his right hand the first 7 weeks of the season, Coleman still finished as the best pass rusher in the SEC,<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www2.oanow.com/oan/sports/college/article/au_football_coleman_has_season_to_remember/118066 |title=AU FOOTBALL: Coleman has season to remember | Opelika-Auburn News |website=www2.oanow.com |access-date=22 May 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091229182457/http://www2.oanow.com/oan/sports/college/article/au_football_coleman_has_season_to_remember/118066 |archive-date=29 December 2009 |url-status=dead}}</ref> finishing the 2009 season ranked first in sacks<ref>{{cite web |title=Bowl Subdivision (FBS) National Player Report Pass Sacks |url=http://web1.ncaa.org/mfb/natlRank.jsp?year=2009&div=B&rpt=IA_playerpasssacks&site=org |website=ncaa.org |access-date=17 August 2023}}</ref> and second in tackles for loss.<ref>{{cite web |title=Bowl Subdivision (FBS) National Player Report Tackles for Loss |url=http://web1.ncaa.org/mfb/natlRank.jsp?year=2009&div=B&rpt=IA_playertacklesloss&site=org |website=ncaa.org |access-date=17 August 2023}}</ref>

==Professional career==

===Buffalo Bills===
Coleman was signed as an undrafted rookie [[free agent]] by the Buffalo Bills on April 25, 2010. He was waived by the team on September 3, 2011.

===New York Giants===
On September 28, Coleman was signed to the [[New York Giants]]' practice squad.

===Return to Buffalo===
The Buffalo Bills signed Coleman off of the Giants' practice squad on October 25 after a season-ending injury to [[Shawne Merriman]]. He was released on December 17, 2011.<ref>{{cite web|last=Gaughan|first=Mark|title=Bills Sign DE, cut Coleman|url=http://blogs.buffalonews.com/billboard/2011/12/bills-sign-de-cut-coleman.html|work=Buffalo News|access-date=December 17, 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130429161115/http://blogs.buffalonews.com/billboard/2011/12/bills-sign-de-cut-coleman.html|archive-date=April 29, 2013|url-status=dead|df=mdy-all}}</ref>

===Saskatchewan Roughriders===
On April 29, 2013, he signed with the [[Saskatchewan Roughriders]] of the Canadian Football League (CFL).<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.riderville.com/article/riders-transactions-20130429122448 |title=RIDERS TRANSACTIONS |access-date=May 5, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130430215036/http://riderville.com/article/riders-transactions-20130429122448 |archive-date=April 30, 2013 |url-status=dead |df=mdy-all }}</ref>

===Hamilton Tiger-Cats===
He signed with the [[Hamilton Tiger-Cats]] of the CFL on May 31, 2014.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.ticats.ca/roster/show/id/5929 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20140907232755/http://www.ticats.ca/roster/show/id/5929 |url-status=dead |archive-date=September 7, 2014 |title=Antonio Coleman |publisher=ticats.ca |access-date=September 7, 2014 }}</ref>

'''Antonio Dixon''' (born July 17, 1985) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[nose tackle]] for the [[Philadelphia Eagles]] and [[Indianapolis Colts]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He was signed as an [[undrafted free agent]] by the [[Washington Redskins]] in 2009. He played [[college football]] for the [[Miami Hurricanes football|Miami Hurricanes]].

==Early life==
Dixon grew up in at least six homeless shelters in [[Miami]] and [[Atlanta]]. He stuttered, had [[dyslexia]], and could not read until the sixth grade. His mother, Corenthia Dixon, was a single parent raising five children, including Dixon. His father, Frazier Hawkins, served 17 years in prison for [[Illegal drug trade|drug trafficking]] charges. He was released in April 2009 and now works as a personal trainer in a health club. Corenthia Dixon used drugs for two years, which led to Dixon and his siblings to live in foster care for a year. When Dixon was in the eighth grade, his family moved into an apartment.<ref name="Homeless">{{cite web |author=Keim, John |title=From homeless shelter to Redskins camp |url=http://washingtonexaminer.com/article/98267 |date=June 9, 2009 |access-date=January 14, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160129054513/http://www.washingtonexaminer.com/article/98267 |archive-date=January 29, 2016 |url-status=dead }}</ref> He got into fights as a child, got suspended, and eventually expelled from school while in eighth grade.<ref>{{cite news |author=Newell, Patrick |title=Milford grad, Dixon, overcomes adversity to reach NFL |url=http://www.evesun.com/news/stories/2010-06-25/9919/Milford-grad-Dixon-overcomes-adversity-to-reach-NFL/ |work=The Evening Sun |date=June 25, 2010 |access-date=October 17, 2010}}</ref> Corenthia is now a cafeteria worker at a homeless shelter in Miami.<ref name="Dreams">{{cite web |author=Hayes, Marcus |title=Eagles defensive tackle Dixon succeeding beyond his wildest dreams |url=http://www.philly.com/philly/sports/78847707.html?&subscribe=y&listID=1431&action=logIn |publisher=Philly.com |date=December 9, 2009 |access-date=February 11, 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091213041853/http://www.philly.com/philly/sports/78847707.html |archive-date=December 13, 2009 |url-status=dead |df=mdy-all }}</ref>

Dixon attended [[Booker T. Washington High School (Miami, Florida)|Booker T. Washington High School]] in Miami, [[Florida]]. He started playing [[High school football|football]] in the ninth grade, and he played as an [[Offensive lineman|offensive]] and [[defensive lineman]]. He graded out at better than 90 percent in his blocking assignments as a senior. On defense, Dixon had 62 tackles and 10.5 sacks in his senior year, with 8.0 sacks during his junior year. He was ranked the 19th player in [[Florida]] by Rivals.com and was the 7th prep school prospect. By the time he finished high school, he weighed over 350 pounds.<ref name="Dreams"/>

In his only year at [[Milford Academy]] in 2004, Dixon finished with 77 tackles, including 21 tackles for loss, which was a team-high. He also had 11.5 sacks, which was tied for first on the team, as Milford finished 11-1 that season. He had to take a Greyhound bus back and forth from New York to Miami because he could not afford plane tickets.<ref>{{cite news |author=Reynolds, Tim |title=Miami's Antonio Dixon overcoming life filled with toil, torment |url=https://www.usatoday.com/sports/college/football/2007-11-22-4002863765_x.htm |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090430075522/https://www.usatoday.com/sports/college/football/2007-11-22-4002863765_x.htm |newspaper=[[USA Today]] |date=November 22, 2007 |archive-date=April 30, 2009 |access-date=February 11, 2010 |url-status=dead}}</ref>

==College career==
Dixon chose to sign with the [[Miami Hurricanes football|University of Miami]] to play [[college football]] over [[Florida Gators football|Florida]], [[Florida State Seminoles football|Florida State]], [[Rutgers Scarlet Knights football|Rutgers]] and [[South Florida Bulls football|South Florida]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Antonio Dixon - Official |url=http://miami.scout.com/2/350540.html |publisher=[[Scout.com]] |date=February 8, 2005 |access-date=February 10, 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110716021543/http://miami.scout.com/2/350540.html |archive-date=July 16, 2011 |url-status=dead }}</ref> As a true freshman in 2005, he played in eight games and had seven tackles in key goal-line and short-yardage situations. In his sophomore season in 2006, he played in 10 games (one [[Starting lineup|start]]) and made 12 tackles, including two tackles for loss and a sack. As a junior in 2007, Dixon played in nine games with four starts and made 21 tackles, 3.5 tackles for loss, 1.5 sacks and a pass deflection. In his senior year in 2008, he played in 13 games with five starts and made 31 tackles, three tackles for loss, and one fumble recovery.

In August 2008, Dixon was hospitalized due to the effects of heat in [[Miami]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Dixon hospitalized after apparently suffering effects of heat |url=https://www.espn.com/college-football/news/story?id=3522320 |work=Espn.com |date=August 7, 2008 |access-date=February 11, 2010}}</ref>

In his career at the University of Miami, Dixon made 71 tackles, 8.5 tackles for loss, 2.5 sacks, a fumble recovery and a pass deflection. He also played in 40 games, ten of which he started.

During spring of 2009, Dixon received the [[Wilma Rudolph]] Student Athlete Achievement Award along with five other college athletes. The award is given to college athletes who have overcome great personal, academic and emotional odds to achieve academic success.

Dixon graduated with a degree in liberal arts in May 2009, and became the first person in his family to graduate college.<ref name="Homeless"/>

==Professional career==

===Washington Redskins===
After being [[Undrafted sportsperson|undrafted]] in the [[2009 NFL draft]], Dixon was signed by the [[Washington Redskins]]. He was waived on September 5, 2009.

===Philadelphia Eagles (first stint)===
Dixon was claimed off waivers by the [[Philadelphia Eagles]] on September 6, 2009. Against the [[Chicago Bears]] on November 22, 2009, Dixon blocked a crucial field goal by Bears [[Placekicker|kicker]] [[Robbie Gould]], which led to a 24-20 victory for the Eagles. After tearing his triceps in a week four game against the [[San Francisco 49ers]] on October 2, 2011, Dixon was placed on season-ending [[injured reserve]]. He was re-signed to a one-year [[restricted free agent]] tender on March 14, 2012. He was waived by Philadelphia on August 31, 2012 during final roster cuts.<ref>{{cite web|title=Eagles waive DT Antonio Dixon |url=http://www.i4u.com/2012/08/antonio-dixon/53-man-dt-eagles-dixon-set-waive-antonio-roster |access-date=September 2, 2012 }}{{dead link|date=October 2016 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref>

===Indianapolis Colts===
Dixon was signed when cornerback Justin King was waived to bolster depleted defensive line.

===Philadelphia Eagles (second stint)===
Dixon was re-signed to a two-year deal by the Eagles on December 26, 2012.<ref>{{cite news|agency=Associated Press|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/news/eagles-place-foles-ir-sign-161930570--nfl.html|title=Eagles place Foles on IR, Sign DT Dixon|work=[[Yahoo! Sports]]|date=December 26, 2012|access-date=December 26, 2012}}</ref> He was released on August 30, 2013.

===West Texas Wildcatters===
In 2014, Dixon signed with the [[West Texas Wildcatters]] of the [[Lone Star Football League]] (LSFL).

===New Orleans VooDoo===
On October 29, 2014, Dixon was assigned to the [[New Orleans VooDoo]] of the [[Arena Football League]] (AFL). He was placed on reassignment on February 20, 2015.

==Personal life==
Dixon has an older half-brother, Darrell, a younger brother, Jarvis, and a younger sister, Mikesha.<ref name="Dreams"/>

On April 15, Brown told reporters that "I'm the owner, 100 percent owner" of the Empire, a statement denied by Mike Kwarta, who said that Brown and Kwarta each owned 47.5 percent of the team.{{Cite news |last=Rubel |first=Abigail |date=April 16, 2023 |title=Antonio Brown says he's the sole owner of the Albany Empire. His co-owners disagree. |url=https://www.timesunion.com/sports/article/antonio-brown-says-owns-empire-co-owners-17900329.php |access-date=May 6, 2023 |work=Albany Times Union |language=en}} Four days later, Brown bought Kwarta's ownership stake for $1, growing his position to 95% of the team, and the Empire announced that Kwarta and two other executives were no longer affiliated with the team.{{Cite news |date=April 19, 2023 |title=Antonio Brown takes over Albany Empire arena football team |url=https://spectrumlocalnews.com/nys/capital-region/news/2023/04/19/antonio-brown-takes-over-albany-empire-arena-football-team- |access-date=May 6, 2023 |work=Spectrum News |language=en}} On May 3, Brown's representatives told the ''[[Times Union (Albany)|Times Union]]'', a newspaper in Albany, that Brown has no personal ownership or control over the Empire, and that the team is actually owned by Antonio El-Allah Express Trust Enterprise, which is owned by a foreign citizen named Antonio El-Allah. A letter addressed to a ''Times Union'' reporter began:{{Cite news |last=Rubel |first=Abigail |date=May 3, 2023 |title=Does Antonio Brown really own the Empire? It's complicated. |url=https://www.timesunion.com/sports/article/antonio-brown-really-albany-empire-complicated-18069431.php |access-date=May 6, 2023 |work=Times Union}} {{Blockquote |text=I Brown, Antonio Tavaris {{sic}} a foreign national but not a citizen of the United States at birth{{sic}}, am writing to you regarding recent reports that have been circulating in the media regarding my supposed ownership of the Albany Empire team. I want to make it very clear that I am not the owner of this team, and any claims to the contrary are completely false.}} Media outlets disputed Brown's self-reference as a "foreign national", since both of his parents are US citizens, and he was born and raised in [[Miami]]. The letter cited {{USC|8|1408}} to back up Brown's claim that he is a United States national but not a citizen; this section of the United States Code applies only to people who were born in [[American Samoa]] or [[Swains Island]], or to people in a few other circumstances not applicable to Brown. Some of the language in the letter may suggest an attempt by Brown to portray himself as a [[sovereign citizen]].{{Cite news |last=Benz |first=Tim |date=May 5, 2023 |title=Ex-Steeler Antonio Brown claims he doesn't own Albany Empire — and that he's a 'foreign national' |url=https://triblive.com/sports/ex-steeler-antonio-brown-claims-he-doesnt-own-albany-empire-and-that-hes-a-foreign-national/ |access-date=May 6, 2023 |work=Pittsburgh Tribune-Review}} [[Mike Florio]] wrote that the letter "feels like a clumsy effort to create a [[Shell corporation|shell entity]] that owns the team."{{Cite news |last=Florio |first=Mike |author-link=Mike Florio |date=May 6, 2023 |title=Antonio Brown owns the Albany Empire, unless he doesn't |url=https://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2023/05/06/antonio-brown-owns-the-albany-empire-unless-he-doesnt/ |access-date=May 6, 2023 |work=[[ProFootballTalk]] |publisher=[[NBC Sports]]}} On May 25, Brown told [[WTEN]] that he intended to play for the Empire in their game against the [[Fayetteville Mustangs]] on May 27, which would have made him the first player–owner in professional football since [[George Halas]].{{Cite news |last=Williams |first=Charean |author-link=Charean Williams |date=May 25, 2023 |title=Antonio Brown says he will play for the Albany Empire on Saturday |url=https://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2023/05/25/antonio-brown-says-he-will-play-for-the-albany-empire-on-saturday/ |access-date=June 11, 2023 |work=[[ProFootballTalk]] |publisher=[[NBC Sports]]}} Because paperwork for his [[physical examination]] did not come through on time, Brown did not play in this game. As owner of the team, Brown had the option to override the physical exam requirement, but he did not exercise this option.{{Cite news |last=Gorenstein |first=Ben |date=May 27, 2023 |title=Antonio Brown doesn't play in Saturday's Albany Empire game |url=https://wnyt.com/big-board-sports/antonio-brown-not-expected-to-play-in-tonights-albany-empire-game/ |access-date=June 11, 2023 |work=WNYT}} On June 1, he told [[WNYT (TV)|WNYT]] that he would make his playing debut for the Empire in their June 17 game against the [[Jacksonville Sharks]].{{Cite news |last=Kasabian |first=Paul |date=June 1, 2023 |title=Ex-NFL WR Antonio Brown to Play for Arena Football's Albany Empire on June 17 |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/10077960-ex-nfl-wr-antonio-brown-to-play-for-arena-footballs-albany-empire-on-june-17 |access-date=June 11, 2023 |work=Bleacher Report |language=en}} On June 15, the National Arena League terminated the Empire's franchise agreement, due to Brown's failure to pay the league for dues and fines that he owed.{{Cite web |last=Breech |first=John |date=June 16, 2023 |title=Antonio Brown's arena team gets kicked out of league after former NFL star refuses to pay bills |url=https://www.cbssports.com/nfl/news/antonio-browns-arena-team-gets-kicked-out-of-league-after-former-nfl-star-refuses-to-pay-bills/ |access-date=June 16, 2023 |work=CBS Sports |language=en}} ==Other ventures== [[File:Antonio Brown (54235293299).jpg|thumb|Brown speaking with attendees at the 2024 AmericaFest at the Phoenix Convention Center in Phoenix, Arizona]] ===Television appearances=== On March 8, 2016, Brown was announced as one of the celebrities who competed on [[Dancing with the Stars (U.S. season 22)|season 22]] of ''[[Dancing with the Stars (U.S. TV series)|Dancing with the Stars]]''. Defensive line assistant | highlights = * [[PFWA All-Rookie Team]] ([[PFWA All-Rookie Team#1997|1997]]) * Second-team All-[[Big East Conference|Big East]] (1996) | statlabel1 = [[Tackle (football move)|Tackle]]s | statvalue1 = 28 | statlabel2 = [[Quarterback sack|Sack]]s | statvalue2 = 2.0 | pfr = AndeAn22 }} '''Antonio Kenneth Anderson''' (born June 4, 1973) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[defensive lineman]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) for the [[Dallas Cowboys]]. He also was a member of the [[Memphis Maniax]] in the [[XFL (2001)|XFL]]. He played [[college football]] for the [[Syracuse Orange football|Syracuse Orange]]. ==Early life== Anderson attended [[Midwood High School]], where he was a two-way player at [[defensive tackle]] and [[offensive tackle]]. He transferred to [[Milford Academy]], where he focused on playing [[defensive tackle]]. As a senior, he registered 90 tackles (30 for loss), 13 sacks, and 3 blocked punts, while receiving Super Prep Al-American and All-Northeast honors. ==College career== Anderson accepted a football scholarship from [[Syracuse University]]. As a [[Redshirt (college sports)|redshirt]] freshman, he played in every game (3 starts) at [[defensive tackle]], registering 13 tackles, one sack and one quarterback pressure. He had 2 tackles and one sack in the season opener against [[Ball State University]]. He made 4 tackles (one for loss) against the [[University of Pittsburgh]]. As a sophomore reserve [[defensive tackle|left defensive tackle]], he made 17 tackles (2 for loss), one sack and 4 quarterback pressures. He had 5 tackles, one sack and one quarterback pressure against [[Virginia Tech Hokies football|Virginia Tech]]. He had 4 tackles (one for loss), one quarterback pressures and one fumble recovery against [[Temple University]]. As a junior, he started 6 games at [[defensive tackle|left defensive tackle]] and 2 contests at [[defensive tackle|right defensive tackle]], posting 42 tackles (3 for loss), 8 quarterback pressures (led team), 3.5 sacks, 2 fumble recoveries and one pass defensed. He had 4 tackles and one fumble recovery against [[Rutgers University]]. He tallied 6 tackles against [[West Virginia University]]. He made 5 tackles and 2 quarterback pressures against Virginia Tech. He had 7 tackles (one for loss) against the [[University of Pittsburgh]]. He made 2.5 sacks against [[Boston College]]. As a senior, he started all of the games, recording 45 tackles (9 for loss), 4 sacks, 27 quarterback pressures, 2 passes defensed and 3 forced fumbles. He had 6 tackles, half a sack and 4 quarterback pressures in the season opener against the [[University of North Carolina]]. He collected 6 tackles, 4 quarterback pressures, one sack and one forced fumble against Virginia Tech. He had 7 tackles and 2 sacks against [[Boston College]]. He tallied 5 tackles (one for loss) and 7 quarterback pressures against [[United States Military Academy|Army]]. ==Professional career== {{NFL predraft | height ft = 6 | height in = 6 5/8 | weight = 314 | arm span = 37 3/4 | hand span = 10 }} ===Dallas Cowboys=== Anderson was selected by the [[Dallas Cowboys]] in the fourth round (101st pick overall) of the [[1997 NFL draft]], after dropping because his physical skills didn't match his on-field production.{{Cite web |title=1997 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/1997/draft.htm |access-date=2023-03-30 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}} As a rookie, he registered 40 tackles (2 for loss), 2 sacks, 3 quarterback pressures and 2 passes defensed. He started five games and received [[NFL]] All-rookie team honors. He had 7 tackles in the third game against the [[Philadelphia Eagles]], starting in place of an injured [[Chad Hennings]].{{cite web| url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?nid=1955&dat=19971008&id=OKYkAAAAIBAJ&sjid=w6YFAAAAIBAJ&pg=2975,4786383&hl=en | title=Cowboys' Hennings may be out 8 weeks | accessdate=April 30, 2020}} He collected 2 tackles, one quarterback pressure and one pass defensed against the [[Chicago Bears]]. He made 4 tackles and one sack against the [[Jacksonville Jaguars]]. He had 6 tackles in the eighth game against the [[Philadelphia Eagles]]. He totaled 5 tackles against the [[San Francisco 49ers]]. In [[1998 NFL season|1998]], he was limited to only five games and 5 tackles (one for loss) due to a right knee injury, eventually falling out of the [[defensive line]] rotation.{{cite web| url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?nid=861&dat=19980803&id=Nh1IAAAAIBAJ&sjid=HYEMAAAAIBAJ&pg=4206,5661153&hl=en | title=Cowboys get good news on injured Anderson | accessdate=April 30, 2020}} He was left unprotected for the [[1999 NFL expansion draft]].{{cite web| url=https://oklahoman.com/article/2642238/the-moose-is-loose-cowboys-johnston-available-in-todays-expansion-draft | title=The Moose Is Loose Cowboys' Johnston Available in Today's Expansion Draft| accessdate=April 30, 2020}} ===Cleveland Browns=== The Browns selected him in the [[1999 NFL expansion draft]].{{cite web|url=https://www.nytimes.com/1999/01/16/sports/nfl-roundup-expansion-draft-130-veteran-faces-for-the-browns.html|last=Pennington|first=Bill|title=N.F.L. Roundup—Expansion Draft; 130 Veteran Faces For the Browns|newspaper=[[The New York Times]]|date=January 16, 1999|accessdate=April 30, 2020}} He was released on April 22.{{cite web| url=https://www.nytimes.com/1999/04/23/sports/transactions-363146.html | title=Transactions | website=[[The New York Times]] | accessdate=April 30, 2020}} ===Carolina Panthers=== On June 24, [[1999 NFL season|1999]], he signed with the [[Carolina Panthers]].{{cite web| url=https://www.nytimes.com/1999/06/25/sports/transactions-333700.html | title=Transactions | website=[[The New York Times]] | accessdate=April 30, 2020}} He was released before the season started on July 21.{{cite web| url=https://www.nytimes.com/1999/07/22/sports/transactions-722618.html | title=Transactions | website=[[The New York Times]] | accessdate=April 30, 2020}} ===Memphis Maniax=== In 2001, Anderson joined the [[Memphis Maniax]] of the [[XFL (2001)|XFL]]. He was a backup [[defensive tackle]] and registered 4 tackles.{{cite web| url=http://www.all-xfl.com/memphismaniax/team/roster/antonioanderson.htm | title=Memphis Maniax bio | accessdate=April 30, 2020}} The league ceased operations in May 2001.{{cite web| url=https://money.cnn.com/2001/05/10/news/xfl/ | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20011117015513/http://money.cnn.com/2001/05/10/news/xfl/ | url-status=dead | archive-date=November 17, 2001 | title=WWF drops XFL | accessdate=April 30, 2020}} ==Personal life== Anderson was a defensive assistant coach at [[Hempstead High School (New York)|Hempstead High School]]. He was a defensive line coach with the [[Rhein Fire (NFL Europe)|Rhein Fire]] in [[NFL Europe]]. He was a defensive assistant at the [[United States Merchant Marine Academy|Merchant Marine Academy]]. He was a defensive line coach at [[Nassau Community College]]. He is currently a defensive line coach and recruiting coordinator at [[ASA College]] in New York.{{cite web| url=https://www.asacollegeavengers.com/sports/fball/coaches/Antonio_Anderson_Bio?view=bio | title=ASSA College bio | accessdate=April 30, 2020}} He is one of 14 children. '''Antonio Allen''' (born September 23, 1988) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[Safety (American football position)|safety]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[South Carolina Gamecocks football|South Carolina Gamecocks]]. Allen was selected by the [[New York Jets]] in the seventh round of the [[2012 NFL draft]].

==Early life==
Allen attended [[Trinity Catholic High School (Florida)|Trinity Catholic High School]] in [[Ocala, Florida]]. Allen earned first-team all-state honors after his senior season at Trinity Catholic.<ref>{{cite web | title= South Carolina Profile | work= gamecocksonline.com | url= http://www.gamecocksonline.com/sports/m-footbl/mtt/allen_antonio00.html | access-date= 2012-03-10 | archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20180715060922/http://www.gamecocksonline.com/sports/m-footbl/mtt/allen_antonio00.html | archive-date= 2018-07-15 | url-status= dead }}</ref>

'''Antoine McClain''' (born December 6, 1989) is an American former [[American football|football]] [[offensive guard]]. He initially signed with the [[Baltimore Ravens]] as an undrafted free agent in 2012. Originally from [[Anniston, Alabama]], McClain played [[Clemson Tigers football|college football]] at [[Clemson University]]. He currently coaches offensive line for the Phoenix Phantoms of the Arizona Gridiron Football League.

==High school==
Antoine McClain played his high school career at Anniston High School in Anniston, Alabama. He was named to the ASWA First-team All-State after his senior season.<ref name="Clemson" /> He participated in the ESPN/Under Armour All-American game.<ref name="Clemson" />

He played [[college football]] at Clemson. During his time in Clemson, he participated in 2,438 snaps and he played in 54 games and started 41 of them.<ref name="Clemson">{{cite web | title = Antoine McClain's Clemson Tigers profile | work = clemsontigers.com | url = http://www.clemsontigers.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=28500&ATCLID=205529337 | access-date = 26 August 2012 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20141129154902/http://www.clemsontigers.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=28500&ATCLID=205529337 | archive-date = 29 November 2014 | url-status = dead }}</ref>

In his freshman year, he played in 13 games and was involved in 149 snaps.<ref name="Clemson" />

In his sophomore year, he started 14 games.<ref name="Clemson" /> He was named the starting offensive guard and recorded 66 knockdown blocks.<ref name="Clemson" />

In his junior year, he played in 13 games and started all 13 games and he was involved in 704 snaps.<ref name="Clemson" /> He was selected to the Third-team All-ACC and ACC All-Academic Honor Roll.<ref name="Clemson" />

In his senior year, he played in 14 games and started all 14 games.<ref name="Clemson" />

'''Antonio Tramaine Andrews''' (born August 17, 1992) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[running back]] for three seasons with the [[Tennessee Titans]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Western Kentucky Hilltoppers football|Western Kentucky Hilltoppers]] and was signed as an [[undrafted free agent]] by the Titans in 2014. He was also a member of the [[Memphis Express (American football)|Memphis Express]] of the [[Alliance of American Football]] (AAF), before their season began.

==Early life==
Andrews played football for Fort Campbell High School. In his last two seasons, he went 29–0 as the starting [[quarterback]] and helped lead the team to two class 2A state championships. He was named Kentucky Mr. Football in 2009, his senior season. For his high school career, he threw for 3,365 yards and 50 [[touchdown]]s, and he rushed for 3,368 yards and 56 touchdowns.<ref name="WKU">[http://www.wkusports.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=5400&ATCLID=205131936 "Antonio Andrews"]. wkusports.com. Retrieved February 2, 2013. {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130530013718/http://www.wkusports.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=5400&ATCLID=205131936 |date=May 30, 2013 }}</ref>

==College career==
Andrews joined the Western Kentucky Hilltoppers in 2010 and played in nine games. He had 174 rushing yards and 429 all-purpose yards. In 2011, Andrews played in eight games. He had 505 kick return yards and 590 all-purpose yards. He had a career-best 75-yard kick return against [[Navy Midshipmen football|Navy]].<ref name="WKU" />

As a junior in 2012, Andrews became WKU's starting running back.<ref name="leaders">[https://archive.today/20130217012621/http://www.wkusports.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=5400&ATCLID=205888960 "Andrews, Smith Finish 2012 As National Stat Leaders"]. wkusports.com. January 8, 2013. Retrieved February 2, 2013.{{dead link|date=July 2014}}</ref> He led the [[Sun Belt Conference]] in rushing yards (1,728), punt return yards (234), and kickoff return yards (767). He scored 15 total touchdowns.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Antonio Andrews College Stats, School, Draft, Gamelog, Splits |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/antonio-andrews-1.html |access-date=2024-10-29 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> Andrews also led the FBS in all-purpose yards per game, and his 3,161 all-purpose yards for the season was the second-highest total in FBS history, behind only [[Barry Sanders]] in 1988. Andrews had over 300 all-purpose yards in the last four games of the regular season.<ref name="leaders" />

Andrews made the 2012 All-Sun Belt Conference Offense First-team, and he had been named the Sun Belt Conference Offensive Player of the Week three times that season.<ref>[http://www.wkusports.com//pdf8/1090985.pdf "WKU Among the 2012 Sun Belt and NCAA Leaders"]. wkusports.com. Retrieved February 2, 2013. {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150629052332/http://www.wkusports.com/ |date=June 29, 2015 }}</ref><ref>[http://www.sunbeltsports.org/Sports/MensSports/Football/Article/tabid/740/Article/18698/Week-Three-Sun-Belt-Conference-Football-Players-of-the-Week.aspx "Week Three Sun Belt Conference Football Players of the Week"]. sunbeltsports.org. Retrieved February 2, 2013. {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120920071237/http://www.sunbeltsports.org/Sports/MensSports/Football/Article/tabid/740/Article/18698/Week-Three-Sun-Belt-Conference-Football-Players-of-the-Week.aspx |date=September 20, 2012 }}</ref><ref>[http://www.sunbeltsports.org/Sports/MensSports/Football/Article/tabid/740/Article/18756/Week-Four-Sun-Belt-Conference-Football-Players-of-the-Week.aspx "Week Four Sun Belt Conference Football Players of the Week"]. sunbeltsports.org. Retrieved February 2, 2013. {{Webarchive|url=https://archive.today/20130416033418/http://www.sunbeltsports.org/Sports/MensSports/Football/Article/tabid/740/Article/18756/Week-Four-Sun-Belt-Conference-Football-Players-of-the-Week.aspx |date=April 16, 2013 }}</ref><ref>[http://www.sunbeltsports.org/Sports/MensSports/Football/Article/tabid/740/Article/19220/Week-Thirteen-Sun-Belt-Conference-Football-Players-of-the-Week.aspx "Week Thirteen Sun Belt Conference Football Players of the Week"]. sunbeltsports.org. ===Tennessee Titans===
After going undrafted in the [[2014 NFL draft]], the Tennessee Titans agreed to a contract with Andrews. On August 29, 2014, he was released by the Titans.<ref>{{Cite web |title=The unlikely journey of Tennessee Titans running back Antonio Andrews |url=http://isportsweb.com/2015/11/16/the-unlikely-journey-of-tennessee-titans-running-back-antonio-andrews/ |website=isportsweb |accessdate=December 20, 2015 |archive-date=December 22, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151222132606/http://isportsweb.com/2015/11/16/the-unlikely-journey-of-tennessee-titans-running-back-antonio-andrews/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> However, he was re-signed to the Titans' 10-man practice squad just two days later. He was activated on October 21, 2014.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Gantt |first=Darin |title=Titans to promote running back Antonio Andrews |date=October 21, 2014 |url=http://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2014/10/21/titans-to-promote-running-back-antonio-andrews/ |publisher=Pro Football Talk |accessdate=October 21, 2014}}</ref>

Andrews made his NFL debut on November 23, 2014, against the [[Philadelphia Eagles]]. On September 27, 2015, Andrews scored his first career touchdown following a 12 carry, 49 yard performance against the Colts.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Antonio Andrews 8-yard TD run |url=http://www.titansonline.com/video/videos/Antonio-Andrews-8-yard-TD-run/b1c9384f-ae32-4acc-a219-ee2f49329647 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151222133613/http://www.titansonline.com/video/videos/Antonio-Andrews-8-yard-TD-run/b1c9384f-ae32-4acc-a219-ee2f49329647 |archive-date=December 22, 2015 |website=www.titansonline.com |accessdate=December 20, 2015}}</ref> On November 4, 2015, the Tennessee Titans fired head coach [[Ken Whisenhunt]] and named tight end coach [[Mike Mularkey]] the interim head coach. The following day, Mularkey named Andrews the starting running back.<ref name="j126">{{cite web | last=Wyatt | first=Jim | title=Antonio Andrews Emerges as Top Option Running Ball | website=TennesseeTitans.com | date=2015-11-04 | url=https://www.tennesseetitans.com/news/antonio-andrews-emerges-as-top-option-running-ball-16225136 | access-date=2024-10-29}}</ref> On December 13, 2015, Andrews threw his first career passing touchdown to [[Marcus Mariota]] for 41 yards.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Titans' Antonio Andrews: Throws touchdown pass against Jets - CBSSports.com |url=http://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/football/news/titans-antonio-andrews-throws-touchdown-pass-against-jets/ |website=CBSSports.com |date=December 14, 2015 |accessdate=December 20, 2015}}</ref> Andrews finished the 2015 season with 520 rushing yards on 143 attempts and three touchdowns.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Antonio Andrews 2015 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/A/AndrAn00/gamelog/2015/ |access-date=2024-12-30 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

Andrews began the {{NFL Year|2016}} season as the third running back on the Titans' depth chart after they acquired [[DeMarco Murray]] and drafted [[Derrick Henry]].<ref name="tender" /> In the 2016 season, he appeared in all 16 games in mainly a special teams role.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Antonio Andrews 2016 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/A/AndrAn00/gamelog/2016/ |access-date=2024-12-30 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

On March 7, 2017, it was reported that Andrews would remain an unrestricted free agent after the Tennessee Titans opted to not apply a restricted free agent tender on him.<ref name="tender">{{Cite web |title=Titans' Antonio Andrews: Won't be tendered by Tennessee |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/football/news/titans-antonio-andrews-wont-be-tendered-by-tennessee/ |website=cbssports.com |date=March 8, 2017 |accessdate=April 18, 2018}}</ref>

===Memphis Express===
In 2018, Andrews signed with the [[Memphis Express]] of the [[Alliance of American Football]] (AAF) for the 2019 season.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Froyd |first=Crissy |date=August 27, 2018 |title=Zach Mettenberger and Antonio Andrews reunite in new pro league |url=https://titanswire.usatoday.com/2018/08/27/zach-mettenberger-antonio-andrews-american-alliance-of-football/ |access-date=November 28, 2018 |website=Titans Wire|publisher=USA Today}}</ref> He was released before the season began.<ref name="v924">{{cite web | last=Marsdale | first=Sam | title=Former Tennessee Titans running back Antonio Andrews arrested following domestic incident | website=247Sports | date=2021-06-03 | url=https://247sports.com/college/wisconsin/Article/Antonio-Andrews-Tennessee-Titans-arrested-following-domestic-incident-Western-Kentucky-166062547/ | access-date=2024-10-29}}</ref>

===Cabo Marlins===
In November 2021, Andrews signed with Mexican team [[Cabo Marlins]] ahead of the 2022 [[Fútbol Americano de México]] season.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://gringogazette.com/wp/2021/11/los-cabos-marlins-team-sign-former-nfl-star/|title=Los Cabos Marlins Team Sign Former NFL Star|work=Gringo Gazette|first=Fernando|last=Rodríguez|date=November 22, 2021|access-date=November 27, 2022}}</ref> However, he did not end up playing with the team.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.elvigia.net/deportes/2022/5/7/listos-marlins-para-iniciar-temporada-392427.html|title=Listos Marlins para iniciar Temporada|work=El Vigía|date=May 7, 2022|access-date=November 27, 2022|language=es}}</ref>

'''Antone Chavez Exum Jr.''' (born February 27, 1991), also known mononymously as '''Exum''', is a [[musician]] and former [[American football]] [[Safety (American and Canadian football position)|safety]]. He played [[college football]] at [[Virginia Tech Hokies football|Virginia Tech]], and was selected by the [[Minnesota Vikings]] in the sixth round of the [[2014 NFL draft]].

==Early life==
Exum attended [[Deep Run High School]] in [[Glen Allen, Virginia]], where he participated in football, basketball and track. In 2008, he was named first-team All-region and was a first-team selection for the [[Richmond Times-Dispatch]] All-Metro defensive team. As a junior, he threw for 860 yards and rushed for 658 yards, scoring 25 total touchdowns, while also adding 20 tackles and three interceptions as a defensive back. He accounted for 2,357 all-purpose yards and 30 total [[touchdowns]] in his senior season, including six on returns.

He also [[Letterman (sports)|lettered]] in [[high school basketball|basketball]] and [[track and field|track]] at Deep Run. In 2009, he earned first-place finishes in both the [[100 meters]] (11.50s) and 200 meters (23.53s) at the Douglas Freeman Meet.<ref>[http://va.milesplit.com/meets/53709/results/91157 Girls 4x800 Meter Relay]. Douglas Freeman High School. May 6, 2009</ref> He also posted a personal-best time of 23.16 seconds in the [[200-meter dash]] at the district meet, where he placed sixth.<ref>[http://va.milesplit.com/meets/49401/results/92063 Colonial District Outdoor T&F Championships]. Maggie L. Walker Governors School. May 13, 2009 – May 14, 2009</ref>

Considered a three-star recruit by [[Rivals.com]], Exum was listed as the 38th best athlete prospect of his class and the No. 14 player in the state.<ref>[https://rivals.yahoo.com/virginiatech/football/recruiting/player-Antone-Exum-63152 Antone Exum – Yahoo Sports]. Rivals.yahoo.com. Retrieved on December 2, 2015.</ref> He was rated the No. 16 prospect in Virginia by [[The Roanoke Times]]. He was rated the No. 42 athlete prospect nationally by both [[ESPN.com]] and [[Scouts Inc.|Scouts Inc]]. He was also ranked the No. 69 [[quarterback]] prospect in the nation by [[Scout.com]].

==College career==
Exum attended [[Virginia Tech]] from 2009 to 2013. In 2009, he [[redshirt (college sports)|redshirted]] as a true freshman. In 2010, Exum played in all 14 games, starting five. He played at [[free safety]], but moved around a lot in the Hokies nickel defense. He recorded 45 tackles and had a team-high nine pass breakups for the season. In 2011, he was an honorable mention All-[[Atlantic Coast Conference|ACC]] selection at safety, after he led the team with 89 tackles, while adding five tackles for loss, 1.5 sacks and an interception. He also had 10 pass breakups, two quarterback hurries, two forced fumbles and a fumble recovery. In 2012, Exum was moved to cornerback in spring practice. He started all 13 games, recording 48 tackles, including 1.5 for loss and led the team with five interceptions. He also had 16 pass break-ups, 21 passes defended, two forced fumbles and a fumble recovery. He capped off his season with an MVP performance in the [[2012 Russell Athletic Bowl]] vs [[Rutgers Scarlet Knights football|Rutgers]], and was also named second-team All-ACC.<ref>[http://www.hokiesports.com/football/recaps/20121126aaa.html Three Hokies earn second-team all-ACC honors]. Hokiesports.com (November 26, 2012). Retrieved on December 2, 2015.</ref>

In January 2013, Exum suffered a torn [[anterior cruciate ligament|ACL]] and lateral meniscus of his right knee during a pick-up basketball game.<ref>Taylor, John. (January 27, 2013) [https://collegefootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2013/01/27/vatechs-antone-exum-tears-acl/ Virginia Tech's Antone Exum tears ACL]. Collegefootballtalk.nbcsports.com. Retrieved on December 2, 2015.</ref> Before his injury, he was widely considered to be one of the best shutdown players of the season. Especially considering he had 5 interceptions and 16 pass break-ups, and 21 passes defended in his first year at the cornerback position. He missed the team's spring practice and fall camp due to the injury, but was cleared to play on October 1 by surgeon [[James Andrews (physician)|Dr. James Andrews]], just under nine months after his initial diagnosis.<ref>[http://www.cbssports.com/collegefootball/eye-on-college-football/23948609/virginia-tech-db-antone-exum-knee-surgery-cleared-to-play Virginia Tech DB Antone Exum (knee surgery) cleared to play]. Cbssports.com. Retrieved on December 2, 2015.</ref> Despite being cleared to play, Exum opted not to dress the next two games, but returned to start the next three games before spraining his ankle which caused him to miss the rest of the season, including the [[Hyundai Sun Bowl|Sun Bowl]] vs. [[UCLA Bruins football|UCLA]]. Exum and his highly touted NFL prospect teammate, [[Kyle Fuller]], also missed the Sun Bowl.<ref>[https://www.sbnation.com/college-football/2013/12/28/5251220/virginia-tech-sun-bowl-antone-exum-injury Virginia Tech CBs Antone Exum, Kyle Fuller likely out for Sun Bowl]. Sbnation.com. Retrieved on December 2, 2015.</ref>

===Minnesota Vikings===
====2014 season====
After trading down twice from 148th and 168th, the [[Minnesota Vikings]] selected Exum in the sixth round (182nd overall) of the [[2014 NFL draft]].<ref>[https://www.sbnation.com/nfl/2014/5/10/5663420/nfl-draft-results-2014-antone-exum-vikings Antone Exum taken by Vikings in Round 6]. Sbnation.com. Retrieved on December 2, 2015.</ref> Many analysts stated that, had he stayed healthy all year, he most likely would have been a 1st–2nd round pick. Exum became the first safety drafted by the Vikings since the club selected [[Harrison Smith]] 29th overall in the [[2012 NFL draft]]. He was also the highest selected defensive back of the 3 picked by the Vikings in the [[2014 NFL draft]].

Exum played in 15 games (the 2nd most by a Vikings rookie behind DT [[Shamar Stephen]]) with no starts during his rookie campaign, contributing heavily on special teams. He was tied for 5th on the team with 7 special teams tackles, compiling 3 of them in the final 4 games of the season. He finished the season with 6 [[tackle (football move)|tackles]] (4 solo).

====2015 season====
Exum was one of just two Vikings defenders to play every snap (64) in the 20–10 win over the [[Atlanta Falcons]] in Week 12, and he had a strong day in his first career start (Harrison Smith was inactive with a knee injury) as the Vikings contained wide receiver [[Julio Jones]] and the Falcons' fifth-ranked pass offense. Exum gave up only 16 yards in two passes targeted for him, knifed in to stop [[Tevin Coleman]] for a four-yard loss at the goal line and recovered [[Anthony Barr (American football)|Anthony Barr]]'s forced fumble on Coleman's 46-yard run. Exum ended the game with three tackles (one for loss) and a fumble recovery. In Minnesota's Week 13 loss against the [[Seattle Seahawks]] Exum tackled Seahawks running back [[Thomas Rawls]] to force his first career fumble in the NFL.

====2016 season====
Exum was waived/injured by the Vikings on August 30, 2016.<ref>{{cite web | last=Watkins | first=Evan G. | title=Vikings waive Antone Exum | website=247Sports | date=2016-08-31 | url=https://247sports.com/college/virginia-tech/article/vikings-waive-antone-exum-47069727/ | access-date=2025-08-03}}</ref> He was then placed on injured reserve after clearing waivers.<ref>{{cite web | title=Vikings' Antone Exum: Placed on Vikings' IR | website=CBSSports.com | date=2016-08-31 | url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/football/news/vikings-antone-exum-placed-on-vikings-ir/ | access-date=2025-08-03}}</ref>

====2017 season====
After an injury in mini-camp, Exum went into the 2017 training camp healthy, and spent the first week of practice as a nickel corner after spending his first few seasons as a safety.<ref>{{cite web|title=Often-injured Vikings DB Antone Exum says it's a 'blessing' returning to practice|url=https://www.twincities.com/2017/07/24/often-injured-vikings-db-antone-exum-says-its-a-blessing-returning-to-practice/|website=TwinCities.com|date=July 24, 2017}}</ref> He was waived by the Vikings on September 16, 2017.<ref>{{cite web|title=Vikings Sign QB Kyle Sloter To 53-Man Roster|url=http://www.vikings.com/news/article-1/Vikings-Sign-QB-Kyle-Sloter-To-53-Man-Roster/699bc78d-fa09-41a2-9976-29858e2f3168|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180427071556/http://www.vikings.com/news/article-1/Vikings-Sign-QB-Kyle-Sloter-To-53-Man-Roster/699bc78d-fa09-41a2-9976-29858e2f3168|url-status=dead|archive-date=April 27, 2018|website=Vikings.com|date=September 16, 2017}}</ref>

===San Francisco 49ers===
On November 7, 2017, Exum signed with the [[San Francisco 49ers]].<ref>{{cite web|title=49ers Sign DB Antone Exum Jr., Place OL Garry Gilliam on Injured Reserve|url=http://www.49ers.com/news/article-2/49ers-Sign-DB-Antone-Exum-Jr-Place-OL-Garry-Gilliam-on-Injured-Reserve/e8957b4a-7d93-49c8-8b10-baef996982f2|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180303175730/http://www.49ers.com/news/article-2/49ers-Sign-DB-Antone-Exum-Jr-Place-OL-Garry-Gilliam-on-Injured-Reserve/e8957b4a-7d93-49c8-8b10-baef996982f2|url-status=dead|archive-date=March 3, 2018|website=49ers.com|date=November 7, 2017}}</ref>

On June 6, 2018, Exum re-signed with the 49ers.<ref>{{cite web|title=49ers Sign DB Antone Exum Jr.|url=https://www.49ers.com/news/49ers-sign-db-antone-exum-jr?sf191233357=1|website=49ers.com|date=June 6, 2018}}</ref> He was released on September 1, 2018, and was re-signed again on September 3, 2018.<ref>{{cite web|title=49ers Cut 21 Players, Get Roster Down to 53|url=https://www.49ers.com/news/49ers-cut-21-players-get-roster-down-to-53|website=49ers.com|date=September 1, 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=49ers Announce a Series of Roster Moves|url=https://www.49ers.com/news/49ers-announce-a-series-of-roster-moves|website=49ers.com|date=September 3, 2018}}</ref> In Week 4 against [[Philip Rivers]] and the [[Los Angeles Chargers]], Exum recorded his first career interception and touchdown.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Madson |first=Kyle |date=September 30, 2018 |title=49ers highlights: Antone Exum Jr. takes first career INT back for TD |url=https://ninerswire.usatoday.com/2018/09/30/49ers-highlights-antone-exum-jr-takes-first-career-int-back-for-td/ |access-date=October 17, 2018 |work=Niners Wire|publisher=USA Today |language=en-US}}</ref>

On March 14, 2019, Exum re-signed with the 49ers.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Madson |first=Kyle |date=March 14, 2019 |title=49ers to re-sign safety Antone Exum Jr. |url=https://ninerswire.usatoday.com/2019/03/14/49ers-to-re-sign-safety-antone-exum-jr/ |access-date=2024-07-16 |website=Niners Wire |publisher=USA Today}}</ref>

On August 31, 2019, Exum was released but re-signed the next day.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.49ers.com/news/49ers-53-man-roster|title=49ers Announce 53-man Roster|date=August 31, 2019|website=49ers.com|language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nfl.com/news/seahawks-re-sign-qb-geno-smith-day-after-release-0ap3000001045997|title=Seahawks re-sign QB Geno Smith day after release|last=Scott|first=Jelani|date=September 1, 2019|website=NFL.com}}</ref> He was released on October 2, 2019.<ref>{{cite web|title=49ers promote Marcell Harris, waive Antone Exum|url=https://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2019/10/02/49ers-promote-marcell-harris-waive-antone-exum/|author=Alper, Josh|work=Pro Football Talk|publisher=NBC Sports|date=October 2, 2019}}</ref> He was re-signed on December 4, 2019.<ref>{{cite web|title=49ers Sign DB Antone Exum Jr.; Open DL Kentavius Street's Practice Window|url=https://www.49ers.com/news/49ers-sign-antone-exum-jr-open-practice-window-kentavius-street|website=49ers.com|date=December 4, 2019}}</ref> On January 1, 2020, Exum was waived by the 49ers.<ref>{{cite web|title=49ers Sign DL Earl Mitchell, Waive DB Antone Exum Jr.|url=https://www.49ers.com/news/49ers-sign-earl-mitchell-waive-antone-exum-jr|website=49ers.com|date=January 1, 2020}}</ref>

== Music career ==

After an injury ended his 2016 season with the Minnesota Vikings, Exum started recording songs. He began collaborating with Norwegian producer Erik Samkopf in 2018. Exum's music is described as "surreal pop" by ''[[The Guardian]]''.<ref>{{Cite news|last=Cragg|first=Michael|date=2021-02-12|title=Antone Exum: why the 'Dennis Rodman of the NFL' turned to surrealist pop|url=http://www.theguardian.com/music/2021/feb/12/antone-exum-the-american-football-star-making-surreal-pop|access-date=2021-05-12|website=the Guardian|language=en}}</ref>

His track ''Arrest The Dancer'' debuted on the Matt Wilkinson Show on May 6, 2021.

'''Anthony Joseph Zettel''' (born August 9, 1992) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[defensive end]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Penn State Nittany Lions football|Penn State Nittany Lions]]. He was selected by the [[Detroit Lions]] in the sixth round of the [[2016 NFL draft]].

==Early life==
Zettel attended [[Ogemaw Heights High School]] in [[West Branch, Michigan]], where he was a first-team all-state selection as a senior. He recorded 82 solo [[Tackle (football move)#Gridiron football|tackles]], 25 assisted tackles and dropped the [[quarterback]] in the backfield seven times as a senior.

Zettel also [[letterman (sports)|lettered]] in [[baseball]], [[high school basketball|basketball]] and [[track & field]] at Ogemaw Heights. As a senior in track, he set the Michigan high school state record in the [[shot put]] with a toss of {{convert|61|ft|8|in|m|abbr=off|sp=us}}, earning his second straight state championship and breaking both the school record (60'9") and the Division II state record (58'8"). That same year, he finished second in the [[discus]] with a heave of {{convert|175|ft|4|in|m|abbr=off|sp=us}}.<ref>{{cite web | last=Butzin | first=Cory | title=Anthony Zettel sets standard with new state record in the shot put for Ogemaw Heights | website=mlive | date=2011-06-04 | url=https://www.mlive.com/highschoolsports/article/anthony-zettel-sets-standard-with-new-state-record-in-the-shot-put-for-ogemaw-heights/ | access-date=2025-07-26}}</ref> He also participated in sprints, running the [[100-meter dash]] in 11.55 seconds and helping Ogemaw's [[4 x 100 metres relay|400m sprint relay]] post a season-low 45.95 in 2010.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.pennlive.com/pennstatefootball/index.ssf/2014/12/seventy-five_yard_passes_375-y.html|title=Seventy-five yard passes? 375-yard drives? 92-mph fastballs? For Penn State's Anthony Zettel, why not?|date=December 14, 2014 |publisher=}}</ref>

Zettel was rated as a four-star recruit and was listed as the nation's No. 6 prep [[defensive end]] by [[Rivals.com]].

==College career==
Zettel played inside and outside during a 2014 first-team [[List of All-Big Ten Conference football teams|All-Big Ten Conference]] season at [[Penn State Nittany Lions football|Penn State]] and recorded 17 [[tackles for loss]], eight [[Quarterback sack|sacks]], and three interceptions. He was moved inside in 2015 and his production dipped a bit with 47 tackles, 11 for loss, four sacks and six [[pass breakups]].

'''Antonio Callaway''' (born January 9, 1997) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[wide receiver]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Florida Gators football|Florida Gators]] and was selected by the [[Cleveland Browns]] in the fourth round of the [[2018 NFL draft]].

==Early life==
Callaway attended [[Booker T. Washington High School (Miami)|Booker T. Washington High School]] in [[Miami, Florida]].<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.miamiherald.com/sports/high-school/prep-miami-dade/article9320678.html |title=Booker T. Washington WR Antonio Callaway chooses Florida Gators |work=Miami Herald |access-date=October 2, 2018 |language=en}}</ref>

==College career==
As a [[wide receiver]] at the University of Florida, he made an immediate impact in his [[true freshman]] season.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.alligatorarmy.com/2015/10/18/9563331/antonio-callaway-florida-gators-best-freshman-ever-catch-punt-return-video|title=Antonio Callaway adds more highlights to case for being Florida's best freshman ever|author=Andy Hutchins|date=October 18, 2015|work=Alligator Army}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.miamiherald.com/sports/college/sec/university-of-florida/article43053165.html|title=Antonio Callaway on pace for best freshman season in Florida Gators history|work=miamiherald}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.tbo.com/sports/colleges/freshman-callaway-gives-uf-a-big-time-playmaker-20150930/|title=Freshman Callaway gives UF a big-time playmaker|author=Joey Johnston – Tribune Staff|date=September 30, 2015|work=TBO.com|access-date=December 11, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180924033827/https://www.tbo.com/sports/colleges/freshman-callaway-gives-uf-a-big-time-playmaker-20150930/|archive-date=September 24, 2018|url-status=dead}}</ref> He was selected [[College Football All-America Team|All-American]] as a [[return specialist]] by [[CBS Sports]] in 2015.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.cbssports.com/collegefootball/eye-on-college-football/25407430/cbs-sports-2015-college-football-all-america-team|title=CBS Sports 2015 College Football All-America Team|work=CBSSports.com}}</ref> The 2015 Gators got off to an unexpected 6–0 start after entering their first four games unranked in the [[AP Poll]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/schools/florida/2015-schedule.html |title=2015 Florida Gators Schedule and Results |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en |access-date=October 2, 2018}}</ref> Their fourth victory was a thrilling 28–27 come-from-behind victory over [[2015 Tennessee Volunteers football team|Tennessee]] as [[Will Grier]] completed a pass on 4th-and-14 to Callaway for a 63-yard [[touchdown]], and Tennessee could not respond as they missed a 55-yard [[field goal]] attempt as time expired.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.orlandosentinel.com/sports/florida-gators/os-gators-football-0928-20150927-story.html|title=UF hero Antonio Callaway predicted touchdown prior to Gators win against Tennessee|author=Orlando Sentinel|date=September 27, 2015|work=OrlandoSentinel.com}}</ref> Callaway finished the [[2015 Florida Gators football team|2015 season]] as Florida's leading receiver with 35 catches for 678 yards and four touchdowns.<ref name="CallawayclearedESPNSchlaback">{{cite web |url=http://www.espn.com/espnw/sports/article/17284843/florida-gators-wr-antonio-callaway-cleared-sexual-assault-title-ix-hearing |title=Florida WR Antonio Callaway cleared of sexual assault in Title IX hearing |last=Schlabach |first=Mark |date=August 12, 2016 |website=ESPN.com |access-date=August 30, 2016}}</ref>

In January 2016, Callaway and [[quarterback]] [[Treon Harris]] were suspended from the team. Florida head coach [[Jim McElwain]] said the suspensions were related to "schoolwork."<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.al.com/sports/index.ssf/2016/05/floridas_treon_harris_antonio.html |title=Florida's Treon Harris, Antonio Callaway remain suspended, Jim McElwain says |last=Stephenson |first=Creg |date=May 4, 2016 |website=AL.com |access-date=August 30, 2016}}</ref> It was later revealed that the suspensions were related to an accusation of sexual assault. A woman accused Callaway of sexual assault and Harris of attempted sexual assault in December 2015. The woman reported the alleged incident to Florida's student conduct and conflict resolution office, but did not report the incident to either Gainesville police or University of Florida police. The University of Florida suspended both players for violating the school's code of conduct policy. Both players remained suspended until June, when they returned to campus to take classes and work out at the school's facilities.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.espn.com/college-football/story/_/id/17226092/woman-accusing-florida-gators-players-sexual-assault-boycotts-title-ix-hearing |title=Accuser to boycott Title IX hearing after Florida gets booster to handle case |last1=Lavigne |first1=Paula |last2=Schlabach |first2=Mark |date=August 5, 2016 |website=ESPN.com |access-date=August 30, 2016}}</ref> Callaway was found not responsible of sexually assaulting the female student by an independent hearing officer in a Title IX hearing. The ruling was made by attorney Jake Schickel, a former track and field athlete at Florida who has donated money to Florida's football and basketball programs. Schickel cleared Callaway of three violations of Florida's student conduct code, which included endangering another's health or safety, sexual assault and sexual misconduct, and conduct causing physical injury.<ref name="CallawayclearedESPNSchlaback"/> On December 7, 2017, while suspended, Callaway made the decision that he was going to enter the [[2018 NFL draft]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Suspended Florida receiver Antonio Callaway reportedly declares for 2018 NFL Draft|date=December 7, 2017 |url=http://collegefootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2017/12/07/suspended-florida-receiver-antonio-callaway-reportedly-declares-for-2018-nfl-draft/|publisher=NBC Sports|access-date=December 7, 2017}}</ref>

[http://www.nfl.com/videos/cleveland-browns/0ap3000000931736/Antonio-Callaway-I-just-kept-my-faith-I-would-be-drafted Antonio Callaway Press Conference]
