Callaway began [[training camp (NFL)|training camp]] competing against [[Jeff Janis]], [[Ricardo Louis]], and [[Rashard Higgins]] for the job as the fourth wide receiver on the Browns' depth chart.<ref>{{cite web |title=Early Predictions for NFL's Most Interesting Training Camp Battles |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2773554-early-predictions-for-nfls-most-interesting-training-camp-battles#slide3 |access-date=November 23, 2018 |website=bleacherreport.com |last=Kruse |first=Zach |date=May 1, 2018}}</ref> Callaway and Rashard Higgins became contenders for a starting wide receiver position after [[Corey Coleman]] was granted a trade request on August 5, 2018.<ref>{{cite web |title=Rashard Higgins, Antonio Callaway in line to replace Corey Coleman as starting receiver |url=https://www.news-herald.com/sports/rashard-higgins-antonio-callaway-in-line-to-replace-corey-coleman/article_83b56895-add3-52cd-a285-b43876322382.html |access-date=November 23, 2018 |newspaper=News-Herald |last=Schudel |first=Jeff |date=August 6, 2018 |archive-date=November 24, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181124055042/https://www.news-herald.com/sports/rashard-higgins-antonio-callaway-in-line-to-replace-corey-coleman/article_83b56895-add3-52cd-a285-b43876322382.html |url-status=dead }}</ref> Head coach [[Hue Jackson]] named Callaway the third wide receiver on the depth chart to start the regular season, behind [[Jarvis Landry]] and [[Josh Gordon]].

He made his professional regular season debut in the Browns' season-opener against the [[Pittsburgh Steelers]] and returned a kick for an eight-yard gain during their 21–21 tie.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201809090cle.htm |title=Pittsburgh Steelers at Cleveland Browns - September 9th, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |access-date=October 2, 2018}}</ref> On September 16, 2018, Callaway earned his first career start and replaced Josh Gordon due to a hamstring injury. He recorded three receptions for 81-yards and scored his first career touchdown during a 21–18 loss at the [[New Orleans Saints]] in Week 2.<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.apnews.com/0b609e3c981e4882b52676e93614f074 |title=Gordon decision, Gonzalez misses, add to Browns' misfortune |work=AP News |access-date=October 4, 2018 |language=en-US}}</ref> Callaway caught his first career touchdown reception on a 47-yard pass by Browns' quarterback [[Tyrod Taylor]] during the fourth quarter.<ref>{{cite web |title=Cleveland Browns at New Orleans Saints - September 16, 2018 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201809160nor.htm |access-date=November 23, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref> The following day, head coach Hue Jackson named Callaway the starting wide receiver after the Browns traded Josh Gordon to the Patriots.<ref name="t339">{{cite web | last=Wagner-McGough | first=Sean | title=Report: Browns moved on from Josh Gordon after he misled team, injured hamstring at commercial shoot | website=CBSSports.com | date=2018-09-17 | url=https://www.cbssports.com/nfl/news/report-browns-moved-on-from-josh-gordon-after-he-misled-team-injured-hamstring-at-commercial-shoot/ | access-date=2024-12-30}}</ref> In Week 8, Callaway made a season-high five receptions for 36-yards and caught a one-yard touchdown pass thrown by [[Baker Mayfield]] as the Browns lost 33–18 at the Steelers.<ref>{{cite web |title=Cleveland Browns at Pittsburgh Steelers - October 28th, 2018 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201810280pit.htm |access-date=November 23, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref>

====2019 season====
On August 9, 2019, Callaway was suspended for the first four games of the 2019 season for violating the NFL's substance abuse policy.<ref>{{cite news |title=Browns WR Antonio Callaway suspended 4 games |url=https://www.clevelandbrowns.com/news/browns-wr-antonio-callaway-suspended-4-games |publisher=ClevelandBrowns.com |date=August 9, 2019 |archive-date=August 9, 2019 |access-date=August 9, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190809210221/https://www.clevelandbrowns.com/news/browns-wr-antonio-callaway-suspended-4-games |url-status=dead }}</ref> He was reinstated from suspension on September 30, and was activated prior to Week 5. On November 14, the Browns waived Callaway after showing up late to meetings and practices.<ref>{{cite web|title=Browns activate OL Drew Forbes from IR, waive WR Antonio Callaway|url=https://www.clevelandbrowns.com/news/browns-activate-ol-drew-forbes-from-ir-waive-wr-antonio-callaway|website=ClevelandBrowns.com|date=November 14, 2019}}</ref> He was also facing a 10-game suspension at the time of his release.<ref>{{cite web|title=WR Antonio Callaway has appealed a 10-game suspension for using a tainted CBD product, source says; waived by Browns|url=https://www.cleveland.com/browns/2019/11/browns-wr-antonio-callaway-has-appealed-a-10-game-suspension-for-using-a-tainted-cbd-product-source-says.html|website=Cleveland.com|date=November 14, 2019}}</ref> He lost his appeal on November 15, and was suspended for the final seven weeks of the 2019 regular season and the first three weeks of the 2020 regular season.<ref>{{cite news |author=Patra, Kevin |title=Former Browns WR Antonio Callaway loses appeal |url=http://www.nfl.com/news/story/0ap3000001076990/article/former-browns-wr-antonio-callaway-loses-appeal |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191115170333/http://www.nfl.com/news/story/0ap3000001076990/article/former-browns-wr-antonio-callaway-loses-appeal |url-status=dead |archive-date=November 15, 2019 |website=NFL.com |date=November 15, 2019 |access-date=November 16, 2019}}</ref>

===Tampa Bay Vipers===
Callaway was signed by the [[Tampa Bay Vipers]] of the [[XFL (2020)|XFL]] on January 16, 2020.<ref>{{cite news |author=Baer, Jack |title=Out of NFL chances, ex-Browns WR Antonio Callaway signs with XFL team |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/antonio-callaway-browns-xfl-tampa-bay-vipers-014629847.html |website=Yahoo.com |date=January 16, 2020 |access-date=January 18, 2020}}</ref> He suffered a lower leg injury in practice on January 29, and was placed on [[injured reserve]] on January 30.<ref>{{cite news |author=Encina, Eduardo A. |title=Former Gator Antonio Callaway's Vipers season ends before it starts |url=https://www.tampabay.com/sports/bucs/2020/01/31/former-gator-antonio-callaways-vipers-season-ends-before-it-starts/ |website=TampaBay.com |date=January 30, 2020 |access-date=January 31, 2020}}</ref> He had his contract terminated when the league suspended operations on April 10, 2020.<ref>{{cite news |author=Condotta, Bob |title=XFL suspends operations, terminates all employees, but Jim Zorn says he has hopes league will continue |url=https://www.seattletimes.com/sports/xfl-suspends-operations-terminates-all-employees/ |website=SeattleTimes.com |date=April 10, 2020 |access-date=July 17, 2020}}</ref>

===Miami Dolphins===
On September 7, 2020, Callaway was signed to the [[practice squad]] of the [[Miami Dolphins]], while still serving a three-game suspension.<ref>{{cite web|title=Dolphins Announce Practice Squad|url=https://www.miamidolphins.com/news/practice-squad-2020-season|website=MiamiDolphins.com|date=September 7, 2020}}</ref> He was suspended an additional four games by the NFL on September 18.<ref>{{cite news |author=Williams, Charean |title=Antonio Callaway eligible to return in Week Eight |url=https://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2020/09/18/antonio-callaway-eligible-to-return-in-week-eight/ |website=NBCSports.com |date=September 18, 2020 |access-date=October 5, 2020}}</ref> He was reinstated from suspension on November 2, and the team activated him back to the practice squad.<ref>{{cite news |author=Crabbs, Kyle |title=Dolphins cut one, activate WR Antonio Callaway onto practice squad |url=https://dolphinswire.usatoday.com/2020/11/03/dolphins-cut-one-activate-wr-antonio-callaway-onto-practice-squad/ |website=USAToday.com |date=November 2, 2020 |access-date=November 26, 2020}}</ref> He was elevated to the active roster on November 14 for the team's week 10 game against the [[Los Angeles Chargers]], and reverted to the practice squad after the game.<ref>{{cite news |title=Kyle Van Noy Activated, Antonio Callaway Elevated to Active Roster |url=https://www.miamidolphins.com/news/kyle-van-noy-activated-antonio-callaway-elevated-to-active-roster |website=MiamiDolphins.com |date=November 14, 2020 |access-date=December 20, 2020}}</ref> Callaway was promoted to the active roster on November 18, 2020.<ref>{{cite news |author=Williams, Charean |title=Dolphins sign Antonio Callaway to 53-player roster |url=https://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2020/11/18/dolphins-sign-antonio-callaway-to-53-player-roster/ |website=NBCSports.com |date=November 18, 2020 |access-date=December 25, 2020}}</ref> The Dolphins waived Callaway on December 21, 2020.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Crabbs|first=Kyle|date=December 22, 2020|title=Miami Dolphins waive wide receiver Antonio Callaway|url=https://dolphinswire.usatoday.com/2020/12/22/miami-dolphins-waive-wide-receiver-antonio-callaway/|access-date=December 22, 2020|website=Dolphinswire}}</ref>

===Kansas City Chiefs===
On January 13, 2021, Callaway signed a reserve/futures contract with the [[Kansas City Chiefs]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Chiefs' Antonio Callaway: Heading to Kansas City |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/football/news/chiefs-antonio-callaway-heading-to-kansas-city/ |website=CBSSports.com |date=January 13, 2021 |access-date=February 17, 2021}}</ref> He was waived with an injury designation on August 17.<ref>{{cite web |title=WR Antonio Callaway among Chiefs' cuts in trimming roster to 85 |url=https://www.kshb.com/sports/wr-antonio-callaway-among-chiefs-cuts-in-trimming-roster-to-85 |website=KSHB.com|date=August 17, 2021 }}</ref> After going unclaimed on waivers, he was put on the Chiefs' injured reserve. He was released on August 26 after reaching an injury settlement with the Chiefs.

===Dallas Cowboys===
On November 11, 2022, the [[Dallas Cowboys]] hosted Callaway for a workout.<ref name="k943">{{cite web | last=Drummond | first=K.D. | title=Here's why Cowboys working out QB, WR ahead of Packers game is significant | website=Cowboys Wire|publisher=USA Today | date=2022-11-11 | url=https://cowboyswire.usatoday.com/lists/cowboys-workout-jacob-eason-antonio-callaway/ | access-date=2025-01-18}}</ref> He was signed to the team’s practice squad four days later.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2022/11/15/cowboys-to-add-antonio-callaway-to-practice-squad/amp/ | title=Cowboys to add Antonio Callaway to practice squad | date=November 16, 2022 | access-date=November 16, 2022 | archive-date=November 16, 2022 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221116030906/https://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2022/11/15/cowboys-to-add-antonio-callaway-to-practice-squad/amp/ | url-status=dead }}</ref> He signed a reserve/future contract on January 25, 2023.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.yardbarker.com/nfl/articles/amp/cowboys_sign_three_to_futures_contracts/s1_17039_38394352 | title=Cowboys Sign Three to Futures Contracts | date=February 27, 2023 }}</ref> He was released by Dallas on June 5, 2023, following his arrest.<ref>{{cite web|title=Cowboys BREAKING: Antonio Callaway Cut Following Arrest, New WR Signed|url=https://www.si.com/nfl/cowboys/news/dallas-cowboys-breaking-antonio-callaway-cut-following-arrest-new-tyron-johnson-signed|website=SI.com|date=June 5, 2023}}</ref>

==Legal issues==
On August 5, 2018, Callaway was issued a citation in Strongsville, Ohio for possession of marijuana and driving with a suspended license during a traffic stop at 3am.<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.news5cleveland.com/sports/browns/browns-rookie-receiver-callaway-cited-for-marijuana-possession-in-strongsville |title=Browns rookie receiver Callaway cited for marijuana possession in Strongsville |last=Cross |first=Ian |date=August 8, 2018 |work=News5Cleveland |access-date=October 4, 2018 |language=en-US}}</ref> The drug charges were dropped, and Callaway paid $911 for the license violation.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.usatoday.com/sports/nfl/arrests/ |title=NFL Player Arrests Database |last=Schrotenboer |first=Brent |website=[[USA Today]] |date=August 8, 2018 |access-date=August 3, 2019 |language=en-US}}</ref>

Callaway was arrested in Miami, Florida on June 4, 2023, for driving with a suspended license. His arrest led to his release from the Cowboys the next day.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/37801991/cowboys-release-wr-antonio-callaway-following-arrest|title=Cowboys release WR Antonio Callaway following arrest|last=Archer|first=Todd|date=June 5, 2023|work=ESPN|access-date=June 5, 2023}}</ref>

'''Antoine Wesley''' (born October 22, 1997) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[wide receiver]]. He played [[college football]] for the [[Texas Tech Red Raiders football|Texas Tech Red Raiders]].

==Early life==
Wesley attended [[Byron P. Steele II High School|Cibolo Steele]] in [[Cibolo, Texas]]. During his career he had 74 [[football catch|receptions]] for 1,192 yards and 15 [[touchdowns]]. He committed to [[Texas Tech University]] to play [[college football]].<ref>{{Cite news |date=May 14, 2015 |title=Recruiting: Did Texas Tech land its future pass-catch combination? |url=https://www.foxsports.com/stories/college-football/recruiting-did-texas-tech-land-its-future-pass-catch-combination |access-date=2025-01-01 |work=[[Fox Sports (United States)|Fox Sports]]}}</ref>

==College career==
Wesley had 10 receptions for 137 yards combined his first two years at Texas Tech.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Williams |first=Don |date=March 27, 2018 |title=Red Raiders need Antoine Wesley to emerge for inside receiver group |url=https://www.lubbockonline.com/news/20180327/red-raiders-need-antoine-wesley-to-emerge-for-inside-receiver-group |access-date=December 11, 2018 |work=[[Lubbock |access-date=December 11, 2018 |work=[[The Dallas Morning News]]}}</ref> As a junior in 2018, he was named an [[All-American]] after he had 88 receptions for 1,410 yards and nine ===Baltimore Ravens===
Wesley signed with the [[Baltimore Ravens]] as an undrafted free agent on May 3, 2019.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Brown, Clifton |date=May 3, 2019 |title=WR Jaylen Smith Among 17 Undrafted Free Agents Ravens Have Signed |url=https://www.baltimoreravens.com/news/wr-jaylen-smith-among-17-undrafted-free-agents-ravens-have-signed |website=BaltimoreRavens.com}}</ref> He was waived on August 31, 2019, and was signed to the [[practice squad]] the next day.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Brown, Clifton |date=September 1, 2019 |title=De'Lance Turner, Maurice Canady Among 10 Players Signed to Practice Squad |url=https://www.baltimoreravens.com/news/de-lance-turner-maurice-canady-among-10-players-signed-to-practice-squad |website=BaltimoreRavens.com}}</ref> He signed a reserve/future contract with the Ravens on January 13, 2020.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Brown, Clifton |date=January 13, 2020 |title=Ravens Sign Nine Players to Reserve/Future Contracts |url=https://www.baltimoreravens.com/news/ravens-sign-nine-players-to-reserve-future-contracts |website=BaltimoreRavens.com}}</ref>

On August 22, 2020, Wesley was placed on [[injured reserve]] with a shoulder injury.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Brown, Clifton |date=August 22, 2020 |title=Ravens Place Antoine Wesley on IR |url=https://www.baltimoreravens.com/news/ravens-place-antoine-wesley-on-ir |website=BaltimoreRavens.com}}</ref>

===Arizona Cardinals===
On May 21, 2021, Wesley signed with the [[Arizona Cardinals]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Cardinals sign wide receiver Antoine Wesley |url=https://www.azcardinals.com/news/cardinals-sign-wide-receiver-antoine-wesley |access-date=May 21, 2021 |website=AZCardinals.com |language=en-US}}</ref> He was named the Cardinals fifth wide receiver on the depth chart to begin the 2021 season. He scored his first career touchdown in Week 16 on a 24-yard pass from [[Kyler Murray]]. He finished the season with 19 catches for 208 yards and three touchdowns.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Antoine Wesley 2021 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/W/WeslAn01/gamelog/2021/ |access-date=2026-03-04 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

On September 1, 2022, Wesley was placed on injured reserve with a [[quadriceps]] tear.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Urban, Darren |date=September 1, 2022 |title=Cardinals Re-Sign Aaron Brewer; Place Antonio Hamilton On NFI |url=https://www.azcardinals.com/news/cardinals-re-signs-aaron-brewer-adds-devon-kennard-to-practice-squad |website=AZCardianls.com}}</ref>

===Las Vegas Raiders===
On August 30, 2023, Wesley was signed to the [[Las Vegas Raiders]] practice squad.<ref>{{Cite web |date=August 30, 2023 |title=Raiders announce practice squad additions |url=https://www.raiders.com/news/raiders-announce-2023-practice-squad-additions-nfl-roster-transactions |access-date=2025-05-28 |website=Raiders.com}}</ref> He was released on September 5, 2023.<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 5, 2023 |title=Raiders sign WR Keelan Cole Sr. to practice squad |url=https://www.raiders.com/news/raiders-sign-wr-keelan-cole-sr-to-practice-squad-nfl-2023-transactions-week-1 |access-date=2025-05-28 |website=Raiders.com}}</ref>

'''Antonio Gandy-Golden''' (born April 11, 1998) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[wide receiver]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Liberty Flames football|Liberty Flames]] and was selected by the [[Washington Football Team]] in the fourth round of the [[2020 NFL draft]]. Gandy-Golden retired from the NFL after two seasons in order to return to school.

== Early life==
Gandy-Golden attended [[Paulding County High School]] in [[Dallas, Georgia]], where he played [[wide receiver]] on the football team.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Antonio Gandy-Golden's High School Timeline |url=https://www.maxpreps.com/athlete/antonio-gandy-golden/YtgpWiRLEeS00gAmVebEWg/default.htm |access-date=October 9, 2019 |website=MaxPreps.com |language=en}}</ref> He was a 2-star recruit according to [[Rivals.com]]. Following high school, Gandy-Golden committed to [[Liberty Flames football|Liberty University]] over offers from [[Elon Phoenix football|Elon]], [[Mercer Bears football|Mercer]], [[Murray State Racers football|Murray State]], [[Kennesaw State Owls football|Kennesaw State]] and [[Samford Bulldogs football|Samford]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.aseaofred.com/2016-verbal-commit-wr-antonio-gandy-golden/|title=2016 Verbal Commit: WR Antonio Gandy-Golden|date=January 12, 2016}}</ref>

==College career==
As a freshman, Gandy-Golden recorded 315 receiving yards and three [[touchdown]] receptions.<ref name="College">{{Cite web |title=Antonio Gandy-Golden {{!}} Football {{!}} Liberty Flames |url=http://www.liberty.edu/flames/index.cfm?pid=36960&TeamID=9&RosterID=12074 |access-date=October 9, 2019 |website=www.liberty.edu}}</ref> In his sophomore season, he led the [[Big South Conference|Big South]] in receptions and receiving yards, also becoming Liberty's seventh 1,000-yard receiver in program history.<ref name="College" />

In his junior season, Gandy-Golden recorded 245 receiving yards against [[New Mexico Lobos football|New Mexico]], breaking the school's record. He was a part of Liberty's victory in the [[2019 Cure Bowl]], the school's first bowl game and his final college game. He finished his career at Liberty as the only player there to post three connective thousand yard receiving seasons. As a student, he pursued a major in [[graphic design]].<ref name="College" />

'''Antoine Duane Winfield Jr.''' (born August 16, 1998) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[Safety (gridiron football position)|safety]] for the [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Minnesota Golden Gophers football|Minnesota Golden Gophers]], earning [[unanimous All-American]] honors. Winfield was selected by the Buccaneers in the second round of the [[2020 NFL draft]].

==Early life==
Winfield Jr. attended [[Eden Prairie High School]] in [[Eden Prairie, Minnesota]] for his freshman year before he and his family moved to [[The Woodlands, Texas]] and attended [[The Woodlands High School]], where he was a three-year letterer and two-year starting safety, in addition to being the team's kick returner, playing alongside future NFL players [[Ethan Bonner]] and [[Patrick Carr (American football)|Patrick Carr]]. As a senior, he totaled 87 tackles, five forced fumbles, and one interception, and was named the [[Montgomery County, Texas|Montgomery County]] Player of the Year.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Mashek |first=Jim |date=December 26, 2015 |title=FOOTBALL: The Woodlands' Antoine Winfield, Jr. is The Courier's 2015 Player of the Year |url=https://www.chron.com/neighborhood/woodlands/sports/article/FOOTBALL-The-Woodlands-Antoine-Winfield-Jr-9878561.php |access-date=March 11, 2021 |website=Houston Chronicle}}</ref> Winfield was considered a two-star recruit by [[Rivals.com]], and accepted a scholarship from [[Minnesota Golden Gophers football|Minnesota]] over offers from [[Baylor Bears football|Baylor]], [[Eastern Michigan Eagles football|Eastern Michigan]], [[Houston Cougars football|Houston]], [[Lamar Cardinals football|Lamar]], [[Missouri Tigers football|Missouri]], [[USF Bulls football|South Florida]], [[Texas State Bobcats football|Texas State]], and [[Wyoming Cowboys football|Wyoming]], among others.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Christensen |first=Joe |date=December 13, 2015 |title=Antoine Winfield Jr. commits to Gophers |url=http://www.startribune.com/antoine-winfield-jr-commits-to-gophers/361742911/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160306074458/http://www.startribune.com/antoine-winfield-jr-commits-to-gophers/361742911/ |archive-date=March 6, 2016 |access-date=March 12, 2023 |website=Star Tribune}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Antoine Winfield, The Woodlands, Safety |url=https://247sports.com/Player/Antoine-Winfield-61713/high-school-107363/ |access-date=March 11, 2021 |website=247Sports |language=en-US}}</ref>

==College career==
As a true freshman at Minnesota in 2016, Winfield Jr. played in 12 games and made nine starts. During the season, he had 52 tackles, one [[interception]] and one fumble recovered for a [[touchdown]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Greder |first=Andy |date=October 6, 2016 |title=Gophers freshman safety Antoine Winfield Jr. was 'born for this' |url=https://www.twincities.com/2016/10/06/gophers-antoine-winfield-jr-vikings-penn-state-iowa-hawkeyes/ |access-date=March 11, 2021 |website=Twin Cities |language=en-US}}</ref> He played in the first four games in 2017 before suffering an injury that caused him to miss the rest of the season.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Greder |first=Andy |date=September 7, 2018 |title=Gophers' Antoine Winfield Jr. can do it all. Throughout [[training camp]], he competed to be a starting safety against veterans [[Mike Edwards (safety)|Mike Edwards]] and [[Jordan Whitehead]].<ref>{{cite web| title=Training Camp Buzz: Buccaneers rookie Antoine Winfield impressing every day| url=https://www.nfl.com/news/training-camp-buzz-buccaneers-rookie-antoine-winfield-impressing-every-day |access-date=January 22, 2025| website=NFL.com |date=August 23, 2020}}</ref> Head coach [[Bruce Arians]] named Winfield the starting strong safety to begin the regular season and paired him with free safety [[Jordan Whitehead]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Adams |first=Bailey |date=August 21, 2020 |title=Buccaneers’ safeties poised for a breakout year in 2020? |url=https://www.bucsnation.com/2020/8/21/21378209/are-the-buccaneers-safeties-poised-for-a-breakout-year-in-2020 |access-date=April 14, 2025 |website=Bucs Nation|publisher=SB Nation}}</ref><ref>{{cite web| title=Tampa Bay Buccaneers 2020 starting line up| url=https://bucswire.usatoday.com/gallery/bucs-starters-2020-nfl-depth-chart-roster-tom-brady-rob-gronkowski/ |access-date=January 22, 2025| website=NFL.com |date=September 3, 2020 |author=Luke Easterling}}</ref>

The Tampa Bay Buccaneers finished the [[2020 NFL season]] second in the [[NFC South]] with an 11–5 record to earn a Wildcard spot. On January 9, 2021, Winfield started in the first playoff game of his career and recorded six solo tackles during a 31–23 victory at the [[2020 Washington Football Team season|Washington Football Team]] in the [[2020–21 NFL playoffs#NFC: Tampa Bay Buccaneers 31, Washington Football Team 23|Wild Card Game]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Wild Card – Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Washington Football Team – January 9th, 2021 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202101090was.htm |access-date=March 11, 2021 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> On January 17, 2021, Winfield had six combined tackles (five solo) and forced a fumble by tight end [[Jared Cook]] that was recovered by [[Devin White]] as the Buccaneers earned a 30–20 victory at the [[2020 New Orleans Saints season|New Orleans Saints]] in the [[2020–21 NFL playoffs#NFC: Tampa Bay Buccaneers 30, New Orleans Saints 20|Divisional Round]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Divisional Round – Tampa Bay Buccaneers at New Orleans Saints – January 17th, 2021 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202101170nor.htm |access-date=January 20, 2021 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> During practice prior to the [[2020–21 NFL playoffs#NFC: Tampa Bay Buccaneers 31, Green Bay Packers 26|National Football Conference (NFC) Championship]] Winfield sustained an ankle injury and was subsequently inactive as the Buccaneers defeated the [[2020 Green Bay Packers season|Green Bay Packers]] 31–26.

====Super Bowl LV====
On February 7, 2021, Winfield returned from injury and started in [[Super Bowl LV]], recording six combined tackles (four solo) and intercepted a pass thrown by [[Patrick Mahomes]] to wide receiver [[Tyreek Hill]] as the Tampa Bay Buccaneers defeated the [[2020 Kansas City Chiefs season|Kansas City Chiefs]] 31–9 to earn Winfield his first [[Super Bowl ring]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Patra |first=Kevin |date=February 7, 2021 |title=What we learned from Buccaneers win over Chiefs in Super Bowl LV |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/what-we-learned-from-buccaneers-win-over-chiefs-in-super-bowl-lv |access-date=February 7, 2021 |website=NFL.com}}</ref>

===2021===
He entered training camp with the [[2021 Tampa Bay Buccaneers season|Buccaneers]] in 2021 slated as the ''de facto'' starting strong safety under defensive coordinator [[Todd Bowles]]. Head coach Bruce Arians retained Winfield and Jordan Whitehead as the starting safeties to begin the season. On October 3, 2021, Winfield made seven combined tackles (five solo), forced a fumble, made a pass deflection, and intercepted a pass thrown by [[Mac Jones]] to wide receiver [[Nelson Agholor]] before exiting at the end of the fourth quarter of a 19–17 victory at the [[2021 New England Patriots season|New England Patriots]] due to possibly suffering a [[concussion]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Easterling |first=Luke |date=October 4, 2021 |title=Latest injury updates on Carlton Davis III, Antoine Winfield Jr. |url=https://bucswire.usatoday.com/story/sports/nfl/buccaneers/2021/10/04/nfl-news-carlton-davis-antoine-winfield-jr-injury-updates-tampa-bay-buccaneers/79355209007/ |access-date=April 15, 2025 |website=Bucs Wire|publisher=USA Today}}</ref> He was confirmed to have suffered a concussion and would remain inactive for the next two games (Weeks 5–6) while in concussion protocol.<ref>{{cite web | last=Yarcho | first=James | title=Antoine Winfield Jr. returns to practice, Antonio Brown has sprained ankle | website=Bucs Nation|publisher=SB Nation | date=October 20, 2021 | url=https://www.bucsnation.com/2021/10/20/22736943/antoine-winfield-jr-returns-to-practice-antonio-brown-has-sprained-ankle-tampa-bay-buccaneers | access-date=April 19, 2026}}</ref> In Week 10, he set a season-high with 11 combined tackles (seven solo) and forced a fumble during a 19–29 loss at the [[2021 Washington Football Team season|Washington Football Team]]. He was inactive for another two games (Weeks 15–16) after sustaining a [[Lisfranc injury|lisfranc]] sprain.<ref>{{cite web| title=Lavonte David, Antoine Winfield Have Lisfranc Sprains |url=https://www.joebucsfan.com/2021/12/lavonte-david-antoine-winfield-have-lisfranc-sprains/-bay-buccaneers |access-date=January 22, 2025 |website=joebucsnation.com |date=December 22, 2021}}</ref> He finished the [[2021 NFL season]] with 88 combined tackles (62 solo), two sacks, six pass deflections, two interceptions, two forced fumbles, and three fumble recoveries in 13 games and starts.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Antoine Winfield 2021 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/W/WinfAn00/gamelog/2021/ |access-date=March 12, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> He received an overall grade of 89.1 from Pro Football Focus.<ref name="PFF"/>

[[File:WFT vs. Buccaneers (51686587730).jpg|thumb|right|225px|Winfield Jr. (right) playing against the Washington Football Team in 2021.]]
The [[2021 Tampa Bay Buccaneers season|Tampa Bay Buccaneers]] finished the 2021 NFL season with a 13–4 record and clinched a playoff berth atop the NFC South. On January 16, 2022, Winfield recorded five combined tackles (three solo) and a sack on [[Jalen Hurts]] during a 31–15 victory against the [[2021 Philadelphia Eagles season|Philadelphia Eagles]] in the [[2021–22 NFL playoffs#NFC: Tampa Bay Buccaneers 31, Philadelphia Eagles 15|Wild Card Game]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Wild Card – Philadelphia Eagles at Tampa Bay Buccaneers – January 16th, 2022 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202201160tam.htm |access-date=March 12, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> On January 23, 2022, Winfield recorded nine total tackles and a forced fumble, but gave up a key 44-yard reception to Rams wide receiver [[Cooper Kupp]] late in the fourth quarter which put Rams kicker [[Matt Gay]] in range to convert a game winning 30-yard field goal, as the Rams defeated the Buccaneers 30–27 to eliminate them from the playoffs during the [[2021–22 NFL playoffs#NFC: Los Angeles Rams 30, Tampa Bay Buccaneers 27|Divisional Round]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Divisional Round – Los Angeles Rams at Tampa Bay Buccaneers – January 23rd, 2022 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202201230tam.htm |access-date=March 12, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

On January 26, 2022, Winfield earned his first career [[Pro Bowl]] selection after being named as an injury replacement for [[Seattle Seahawks]] safety [[Quandre Diggs]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Smith |first=Scott |date=February 4, 2022 |title=Pro Bowl S Antoine Winfield, Jr.: First Two Seasons Were Surreal |url=https://www.buccaneers.com/news/bucs-pro-bowl-safety-antoine-winfield-jr-2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220218210109/https://www.buccaneers.com/news/bucs-pro-bowl-safety-antoine-winfield-jr-2022 |archive-date=February 18, 2022 |access-date=August 17, 2022 |website=www.buccaneers.com |language=en-US}}</ref> He was ranked 75th by his fellow players on the [[NFL Top 100 Players of 2022]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=2022 NFL Top 100 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/awards/2022-nfl-top-100.htm |access-date=March 12, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

===2022===
On March 30, 2022, the [[2022 Tampa Bay Buccaneers season|Tampa Bay Buccaneers]] promoted defensive coordinator [[Todd Bowles]] to head coach after [[Bruce Arians]] retired and shifted to a senior football consultant role.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Smith |first=Scott |date=March 31, 2022 |title=Bruce Arians Steps Into New Role, Todd Bowles Taking Over as Bucs' Head Coach |url=https://www.buccaneers.com/news/bucs-bruce-arians-new-role-todd-bowles-named-head-coach |access-date=March 31, 2022 |website=Tampa Bay Bucccaneers}}</ref> He continued to retain Winfield as the starting strong safety and paired him with Mike Edwards, following the departure of Jordan Whitehead.

On September 11, 2022, Winfield started in the Tampa Bay Buccaneers' season-opener at the [[2022 Dallas Cowboys season|Dallas Cowboys]] and made six combined tackles (five solo), one pass deflection, and intercepted a pass thrown by [[Dak Prescott]] to wide receiver [[Noah Brown (American football)|Noah Brown]] during a 19–3 victory. On October 23, 2022, Winfield made two solo tackles before exiting during the third quarter of a 3–21 loss at the [[2022 Carolina Panthers season|Carolina Panthers]] to be evaluated for a possible concussion after colliding with running back [[Raheem Blackshear]] while tackling him for a four–yard loss. He was confirmed to have suffered a concussion and remained inactive for the next two games (Weeks 8–9). He injured his ankle and was subsequently sidelined for another two games (Weeks 13–14). In Week 14, Winfield set a new season-high with 13 combined tackles (ten solo) as the Buccaneers 17–30 lost at the [[2022 Atlanta Falcons season|Atlanta Falcons]]. He completed the [[2022 NFL season]] with 80 combined tackles (64 solo), a career-high four sacks, one interception, three passes defended, and one forced fumble in 13 games and 13 starts.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Antoine Winfield Jr. 2022 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/W/WinfAn00/gamelog/2022/ |access-date=July 17, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref> He finished the season with an overall grade of 78.1 from Pro Football Focus in 2022.

===2023===
He returned to training camp with the [[2023 Tampa Bay Buccaneers season|Tampa Bay Buccaneers]] slated as the ''de facto'' starting free safety following the departure of Mike Edwards. Head coach Todd Bowles named Winfield a starting safety to begin the season and paired him with [[Ryan Neal]].

In Week 10, Winfield had six combined tackles (three solo), one pass deflection, and intercepted a pass by [[Will Levis]] to wide receiver [[DeAndre Hopkins]] during a 20–6 victory against the [[2023 Tennessee Titans season|Tennessee Titans]]. On November 19, 2023, Winfield set a career-high with 16 combined tackles (ten solo) during a 27–14 loss at the [[2023 San Francisco 49ers season|San Francisco 49ers]]. On December 3, 2023, Winfield made eight combined tackles (six solo), set a career-high with three pass deflections, made one sack, and secured a 21–18 win over the [[2023 Carolina Panthers season|Carolina Panthers]] by intercepting a pass by [[Bryce Young]] to wide receiver [[Adam Thielen]] with only 2:21 remaining in the fourth quarter. His performance earned him NFC Defensive Player of the Week.<ref>{{cite web|title=Bengals QB Jake Browning, 49ers WR Deebo Samuel highlight Players of the Week|url=https://www.nfl.com/news/bengals-qb-jake-browning-49ers-wr-deebo-samuel-highlight-players-of-the-week|author=Gordon, Grant|website=NFL.com|date=December 6, 2023}}</ref> In Week 16, he had three solo tackles, one pass deflection, a sack, and set a new career-high with his third interception of the season on a pass by [[Trevor Lawrence]] to tight end [[Evan Engram]] during a 30–12 win against the [[2023 Jacksonville Jaguars season|Jacksonville Jaguars]]. In Week 18, he recorded five combined tackles (four solo), made one sack, and had a touchdown-saving forced fumble in a 9–0 win over the Carolina Panthers to earn his second Player of the Week award of the season.<ref>{{cite web|title=Texans QB C.J. Stroud, Packers QB Jordan Love highlight Players of the Week|url=https://www.nfl.com/news/texans-quarterback-c-j-stroud-packers-quarterback-jordan-love-highlight-players-|author=Gordon, Grant|website=NFL.com|date=January 10, 2024}}</ref> He started all 16 games during the [[2023 NFL season]] and finished with a career-high 122 combined tackles (76 solo), set a career-high with six sacks, set a new career-high with three interceptions, made 12 pass deflections, had six forced fumbles, and four fumble recoveries.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Antoine Winfield Jr. 2023 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/W/WinfAn00/gamelog/2023/ |access-date=December 30, 2024 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> He earned first team All-Pro honors for the first time.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2023 NFL All-Pros |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2023/allpro.htm |access-date=2026-04-19 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> He was the highest graded safety by Pro Football Focus in 2023 with an overall grade of 90.7.<ref>{{cite web |last=Buday |first=Zoltán  |date=June 3, 2024 |title=PFF Safety Rankings: Top 32 ahead of the 2024 NFL season |url=https://www.pff.com/news/nfl-safety-rankings-top-32-2024-nfl-season |access-date=January 26, 2025 |website=pff.com}}</ref> He was ranked 46th by his fellow players on the [[NFL Top 100 Players of 2024]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=2024 NFL Top 100 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/awards/2024-nfl-top-100.htm |access-date=2026-04-19 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

===2024===
On March 5, 2024, the [[2024 Tampa Bay Buccaneers season|Tampa Bay Buccaneers]] placed the franchise tag on Winfield that was an offer of one–year, $17.12 million.<ref>{{cite web|title=Bucs Place Franchise Tag on All-Pro Safety Antoine Winfield Jr.|url=https://www.buccaneers.com/news/bucs-place-franchise-tag-all-pro-safety-antoine-winfield-jr|author=Smith, Scott|website=Buccaneers.com|date=March 5, 2024}}</ref><ref name="Spotrac"/> On May 13, 2024, the Tampa Bay Buccaneers signed Winfield to a four–year, $84.10 million contract extension that includes $45 million guaranteed upon signing and an initial signing bonus of $20 million, making him the highest paid [[defensive back]] in league history.<ref>{{cite web | last=Smith | first=Scott | title=Franchise Player! Antoine Winfield Jr., Bucs Agree to Four-Year Deal | website=Buccaneers.com| date=May 14, 2024 | url=https://www.buccaneers.com/news/franchise-player-antoine-winfield-jr-bucs-four-year-deal-2024 | access-date=April 19, 2026}}</ref><ref name="Spotrac"/>

He entered [[training camp]] slated to remain as the Buccaneers' ''de facto'' starting free safety. Head coach Todd Bowles chose named him the starting free safety to begin the season and paired him with strong safety [[Jordan Whitehead]].<ref>{{cite web| title=Bucs' Release Week One Depth Chart: Jalen McMillan in Third WR Spot| url=https://www.buccaneers.com/news/bucs-release-week-one-depth-chart-jalen-mcmillan-third-wr-spot |access-date=January 24, 2025 |website=Buccaneers.com |date=September 6, 2024 |author=Scott Smith}}</ref>

On September 8, 2024, Winfield started in the Buccaneers' home-opener against the [[2024 Washington Commanders season|Washington Commanders]] and had seven combined tackles (four solo) before exiting at the end of the fourth quarter of their 37–20 victory after injuring his foot. It was confirmed that Winfield had injured his ankle and remained inactive for the next four games (Weeks 2–5).<ref>{{cite web| title=Buccaneers' All-Pro Safety Antoine Winfield Suffers Injury vs. Commanders| url=https://athlonsports.com/nfl/bucs-country/tampa-bay-buccaneers-week-1-washington-commanders--winfield-jr-injury |access-date=January 24, 2025 |website=Buccaneers.com |date=September 9, 2024 |author=Scott Smith}}</ref> On October 13, 2024, Winfield returned from his injury and made four solo tackles while also scoring his first career touchdown when [[Tykee Smith]] and [[Zyon McCollum]] forced a fumble by wide receiver [[Chris Olave]], which led to a fumble recovery by Winfield that he returned 58–yards return by Winfield during a 51–27 victory at the [[2024 New Orleans Saints season|New Orleans Saints]].<ref>{{cite web| title=Tampa Bay Buccaneers at New Orleans Saints - October 13th, 2024| url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202410130nor.htm |access-date=January 24, 2025 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref> In Week 9, he collected a season-high 12 combined tackles (five solo) during a 30–24 loss at the [[2024 Kansas City Chiefs season|Kansas City Chiefs]]. After injuring his ankle, Winfield would subsequently miss the last four games (Weeks 15–18) of the [[2024 NFL season]]. He ended the season with a total of 60 combined tackles (34 solo), three pass deflections, two sacks, one fumble recovery, and a touchdown in nine games and nine starts.<ref>{{cite web| title=Pro-Football-Reference: Antoine Winfield Jr stats (2024)| url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/W/WinfAn00.htm |access-date=January 24, 2025 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref> He received an overall grade of 56.8 from [[Pro Football Focus]], which ranked 126th among 171 qualifying safeties in 2024.<ref name="PFF">{{cite web| title=Pro Football Focus: Antoine Winfield Jr.| url=https://www.pff.com/nfl/players/antoine-winfield/42475| access-date=April 15, 2025| website=PFF.com}}</ref>

===2025===
In the 2025 season, Winfield Jr. had 93 total tackles (53 solo), one sack, two interceptions, eight passes defended, one forced fumble, and one fumble recovery.<ref>{{cite web | title=Antoine Winfield Jr. 2025 Stats per Game | website=ESPN.com | url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/player/gamelog/_/id/4034790/type/nfl/year/2025 | access-date=April 19, 2026}}</ref> He earned Pro Bowl honors for the second time in his career.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2025 NFL Pro Bowlers |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2025/probowl.htm |access-date=2026-04-19 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

'''Antonio Gibson''' (born June 23, 1998) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[running back]] and [[kickoff returner]]. He played [[college football]] at [[East Central Community College]] in Mississippi for two years prior to transferring to [[Memphis Tigers football|Memphis]] in 2018. As a [[return specialist]] and [[wide receiver]] with Memphis, Gibson was named [[American Athletic Conference]] (AAC) special teams player of the year in 2019 and received conference honors for both positions. He entered the [[2020 NFL draft]] as a running back, where he was selected by the [[Washington Football Team]] in the third round and played four seasons.

==Early life==
Gibson attended [[Eagle's Landing High School]] in [[McDonough, Georgia]], playing for their [[high school football|football]], basketball, and track teams. As a senior, he was named the ''[[Henry Daily Herald]]''{{'s}} offensive player of the year.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Torres |first=Maria |date=December 23, 2015 |title=Offensive Player of the Year: Antonio Gibson Sr., WR/ATH, Eagle’s Landing |url=https://www.henryherald.com/sports/offensive-player-of-the-year-antonio-gibson-sr-wr-ath-eagle-s-landing/article_8d2f605b-fc4e-5857-b299-ae2d4dbc0c9d.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200425152513/https://www.henryherald.com/sports/offensive-player-of-the-year-antonio-gibson-sr-wr-ath-eagle-s-landing/article_8d2f605b-fc4e-5857-b299-ae2d4dbc0c9d.html |archive-date=April 25, 2020 |access-date=April 19, 2020 |website=Henry Herald}}</ref>

==College career==
Gibson enrolled at [[East Central Community College]] in 2016, playing football for them prior to transferring to the [[University of Memphis]] in 2018.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Barnes |first=Evan |date=October 10, 2019 |title=Memphis' Antonio Gibson motivated by former high school coach's memory |url=https://www.commercialappeal.com/story/sports/college/memphis-tigers/2019/10/10/memphis-football-antonio-gibson-joe-teknipp/3895597002/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200425055759/https://www.commercialappeal.com/story/sports/college/memphis-tigers/2019/10/10/memphis-football-antonio-gibson-joe-teknipp/3895597002/ |archive-date=April 25, 2020 |access-date=March 12, 2020 |website=The Commercial Appeal}}</ref> In his two years at East Central, he had 50 receptions for 871 receiving yards with 13 touchdowns, 27 kick returns, 554 kick-return yards and 249 rushing yards. He played wide receiver and running back at Memphis.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Jordan |first=Jonah |date=January 27, 2020 |title=Running back designation only a 'label' for Antonio Gibson |url=https://dailymemphian.com/article/10291/running-back-designation-only-a-label-for-antonio-gibson |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200504134852/https://dailymemphian.com/article/10291/running-back-designation-only-a-label-for-antonio-gibson |archive-date=May 4, 2020 |access-date=March 12, 2020 |website=The Daily Memphian}}</ref>

In his two years, he had 44 receptions for 834 yards with 10 touchdowns, 369 rushing yards and four touchdowns and 647 return yards and a touchdown.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Goodman |first=Darius |date=January 2, 2020 |title=Antonio Gibson's rise to fame at Memphis was a long time coming |url=https://www.henryherald.com/sports/antonio-gibsons-rise-to-fame-at-memphis-was-a-long-time-coming/article_57a6c0b0-2d63-11ea-96b1-af9cd9531d7d.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200514075816/https://www.henryherald.com/sports/antonio-gibsons-rise-to-fame-at-memphis-was-a-long-time-coming/article_57a6c0b0-2d63-11ea-96b1-af9cd9531d7d.html |archive-date=May 14, 2020 |access-date=October 8, 2020 |website=Henry Herald}}</ref> In 2019, he was named the [[AAC Special Teams Player of the Year|American Athletic Conference (AAC) Special Teams Player of the Year]] and made first-team all-AAC as a [[return specialist]] and second-team as a wide receiver, becoming only the fourth player in conference history to receive such an honor at two positions.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Antonio Gibson |url=https://gotigersgo.com/sports/football/roster/antonio-gibson/8410 |access-date=September 8, 2020 |website=gotigersgo.com}}</ref> He was invited to the [[2020 Senior Bowl]] as a [[running back]], where he recorded 68 rushing yards on 11 carries.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Fowler |first=Christian |date=January 29, 2020 |title=Antonio Gibson talks Senior Bowl, NFL Draft and breakout season |url=https://247sports.com/college/memphis/Article/Antonio-Gibson-talks-Senior-Bowl-NFL-Draft-and-breakout-season-142875816/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201029201115/https://247sports.com/college/memphis/Article/Antonio-Gibson-talks-Senior-Bowl-NFL-Draft-and-breakout-season-142875816/ |archive-date=October 29, 2020 |access-date=September 10, 2020 |website=247 Sports}}</ref>

In Week 3 of the 2021 season, Gibson recorded a 73–yard touchdown reception against the [[Buffalo Bills]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Werner |first=Barry |date=September 26, 2021 |title=Antonio Gibson takes screen pass 73 yards for touchdown |url=https://touchdownwire.usatoday.com/2021/09/26/washington-football-team-antonio-gibson-takes-screen-pass-73-yards-for-touchdown-buffalo-bills/ |access-date=September 27, 2021 |website=Touchdown Wire |publisher=USA Today}}</ref> The play was the second-longest touchdown reception by a Washington running back in franchise history.<ref>{{cite tweet|user=Wash_PR |title=That Antonio Gibson 73-yard receiving TD is the second-longest by a Washington RB in franchise history. RB Matt Jones had a 78-yard TD reception in 2015. |number=1442188623642648580 |access-date=October 3, 2021 |date=September 26, 2021}}</ref> The next week, he recorded 63 yards and one touchdown in the win over the [[Atlanta Falcons]], which brought him over 1,000 career rushing yards.<ref>{{Cite web |date=October 4, 2021 |title=Washington-Falcons Monday Stats Pack |url=https://www.commanders.com/news/washington-falcons-monday-stats-pack |access-date=February 2, 2022 |website=Washington Commanders}}</ref> This made Gibson the third Washington player in the franchise's history to attain 1,000 rushing yards within his first two seasons since running back [[Alfred Morris (American football)|Alfred Morris]] and quarterback [[Robert Griffin III]]. On ''[[Monday Night Football]]'' against the [[Seattle Seahawks]], he recorded 111 yards over 29 carries in the Week 12 win which was his first 100-plus rushing yard game of the season.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Lambert |first=Ivan |date=November 30, 2021 |title=Fuller interception saves Washington |url=https://washingtonfootballwire.usatoday.com/2021/11/30/kendall-fuller-interception-saves-the-washington-football-team/ |access-date=December 2, 2021 |work=Washington Football Wire|publisher=USA Today}}</ref> On December 31, 2021, he was placed on the team's COVID-19 reserve list and was forced to sit out of the Week 17 game against the [[Philadelphia Eagles]].<ref>{{cite web|work=ESPN.com|url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/32968932/washington-football-team-adds-antonio-gibson-ereck-flowers-reserve-covid-19-list|title=Washington Football Team adds Antonio Gibson, Ereck Flowers to reserve/COVID-19 list|date=December 31, 2021|first=John|last=Keim|accessdate=January 8, 2022}}</ref> He finished the 2021 season with 258 carries for 1,037 yards and seven touchdowns to go with 42 receptions for 294 yards and three touchdowns.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Antonio Gibson 2021 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/G/GibsAn00/gamelog/2021/ |access-date=2026-05-02 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> He was placed back on active roster on January 5, 2022.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.nbcsports.com/washington/football-team/washington-activates-antonio-gibson-ereck-flowers-reservecovid-19-list|work=NBCSports.com|title=Washington activates Gibson, Flowers from reserve/COVID-19 list|date=January 5, 2022|accessdate=January 8, 2022|first=Ethan|last=Cadeaux}}</ref>

====2022====
[[File:Antonio Gibson TD Packers-Commanders OCT2022.jpg|thumb|Gibson catching a touchdown against the [[Green Bay Packers]] in [[2022 Washington Football Team season|2022]]]]
In the 2022 preseason, Gibson was announced as the team's new kick returner while losing his starting position to rookie running back [[Brian Robinson Jr.]]<ref>{{cite news |work=NBCSports.com|url=https://www.nbcsports.com/washington/commanders/ron-rivera-thinks-antonio-gibson-will-be-commanders-top-kick-returner|title=Rivera thinks Gibson will be Commanders’ top kick returner|date=August 25, 2022|accessdate=November 16, 2022|first=Bijan|last=Todd}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|work=SI.com|url=https://www.si.com/nfl/commanders/news/washington-antonio-gibson-brian-robinson-depth-chart-running-back-training-camp|title=Antonio Gibson Losing Starting Job with Washington Commanders?|first=Cole|last=Thompson|date=August 16, 2022|accessdate=November 16, 2022}}</ref> Following Robinson Jr. being shot in an armed robbery, Gibson returned as the team's starting running back in the beginning of the 2022 season. In the Week 7 win over the [[Green Bay Packers]], Gibson recorded 59 rushing yards, three receptions, 18 receiving yards, and one receiving touchdown.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.commanders.com/news/numbers-to-know-from-washington-s-win-over-green-bay|work=Commanders.com|title=Numbers to know from Washington's win over Green Bay|date=October 24, 2022|first=Hannah|last=Lichtenstein|accessdate=November 16, 2022}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=October 24, 2022 |title=Commanders-Packers Stats & Snaps |url=https://www.commanders.com/news/commanders-packers-stats-snaps |access-date=November 16, 2022 |website=Commanders.com}}</ref> The touchdown was the franchise's 3,000 in their history, with the ball being displayed in the [[Pro Football Hall of Fame]].<ref>{{cite news|work=NBCSports.com|url=https://www.nbcsports.com/washington/commanders/taylor-heinicke-antonio-gibson-touchdown-ball-headed-pro-football-hall-fame|title=Heinicke-Gibson TD ball headed to Pro Football Hall of Fame|date=October 28, 2022|accessdate=November 16, 2022|first=Bijan|last=Todd}}</ref> On January 5, 2023, he was placed on [[injured reserve]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.commanders.com/news/commanders-place-antonio-gibson-on-ir-sign-jaret-patterson-from-practice-squad|work=Commanders.com|title=Commanders place Antonio Gibson on IR, sign Jaret Patterson from practice squad|date=January 5, 2023|accessdate=January 5, 2023|first=Zach|last=Selby}}</ref> He finished the season with 546 rushing yards and three touchdowns, along with 46 catches for 353 yards and two touchdowns.<ref name="b474">{{cite web | title=Antonio Gibson 2022 Game Log | website=[[Pro Football Reference]]| url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/G/GibsAn00/gamelog/2022/ | access-date=2024-10-02}}</ref>

'''Antoine Brooks Jr.''' (born October 28, 1997) is an American professional [[gridiron football|football]] [[Safety (gridiron football position)|safety]] for the [[Saskatchewan Roughriders]] of the [[Canadian Football League]] (CFL). He played [[college football]] at [[Maryland Terrapins football|Maryland]] and was selected by the [[Pittsburgh Steelers]] in the sixth round of the [[2020 NFL draft]].

==Early life==
Brooks grew up in [[Lanham, Maryland]], and attended [[DuVal High School]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.latimes.com/ph-cc-sp-terps-antoine-brooks-0203-story.html|title=Maryland National Signing Day 2016: Antoine Brooks|work=[[Los Angeles Times]]|date=February 3, 2016|access-date=April 6, 2020}}{{dead link|date=June 2021|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref> He was a starting [[defensive back]] and [[quarterback]] for the Tigers. As a junior, he was named first-team All-Metro by ''[[The Washington Post]]'' and
first-team All-State at defensive back.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.capitalgazette.com/sports/high-school/ph-ac-cs-all-state-football-10516-20160104-story.html|title=2015 Maryland high school All-State football team|work=[[Capital Gazette]]|date=January 4, 2016|access-date=April 6, 2020}}</ref> Midway through his senior season Brooks suffered a compound fracture on his ankle and a broken wrist while throwing a pass against [[Dr. Henry A. Wise Jr. High School|Wise High School]], requiring five hours of surgery to repair and putting his football career in doubt.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fox5dc.com/sports/star-md-prep-football-player-antoine-brooks-recovering-after-suffering-serious-injuries|title=Star Md. prep football player Antoine Brooks recovering after suffering serious injuries|first=Scott|last=Smith|work=Fox5DC.com|date=October 14, 2015|access-date=April 6, 2020}}</ref> He was still named second-team All-Metro, first-team All-State and the [[Prince George's County, Maryland|Prince George's County]] 4A Offensive Player of the Year despite missing half of the season.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/news/recruiting-insider/wp/2016/02/02/injured-duval-football-star-antoine-brooks-commits-to-maryland-after-late-offer/|title=Injured DuVal football star Antoine Brooks commits to Maryland after late offer|first=Mark|last=Giannotto|newspaper=[[The Washington Post]]|date=February 2, 2016|access-date=April 6, 2020}}</ref> Although he originally had over 15 scholarship offers, much of his recruiting interest faded after his injury and he initially committed to play [[college football]] at Buffalo. Brooks committed to play at Maryland a few days before [[National Signing Day]] after a late push from coach [[D. J. Durkin]] over offers from Pitt, Indiana, Hawaii, Buffalo, Army, Old Dominion and Charlotte.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.testudotimes.com/2016/8/18/12528614/maryland-football-antoine-brooks-freshman-injury|title=After a grisly injury, freshman Antoine Brooks is ready to contribute for Maryland football|first=Ryan|last=Connors|website=TestudoTimes.com|publisher=[[SB Nation]]|date=August 18, 2016|access-date=April 6, 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.testudotimes.com/maryland-terrapins-football-recruiting/2016/2/1/10889170/antoine-brooks-terps-commits-linebacker-2016|title=Antoine Brooks commits to Maryland: Terps land local linebacker|first=Alex|last=Kirshner|website=TestudoTimes.com|publisher=[[SB Nation]]|date=February 1, 2016|access-date=April 6, 2020}}</ref>

==College career==
Brooks played in six games, mostly on [[special teams]], during his freshman season before being suspended for the rest of the season.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nbcsports.com/washington/maryland-terps/two-maryland-football-players-charged-in-bb-gun-incident|title=Two Maryland football players charged in BB gun incident|website=[[NBC Sports Washington]]|date=November 16, 2016|access-date=April 6, 2020}}</ref> He became the Terrapins' primary nickel back as a sophomore and finished second on the team with 77 tackles and led all defensive backs in the [[Big Ten Conference]] with 9.5 tackles for loss along with one sack, two [[interception]]s, three pass breakups and a forced fumble.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.baltimoresun.com/sports/terps/bs-sp-antoine-brooks-maryland-football-1021-story.html|title=Halfway through season, Antoine Brooks Jr. has been a hit as Maryland's nickel back|work=[[The Baltimore Sun]]|date=October 20, 2017|access-date=April 6, 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.testudotimes.com/maryland-terps-football/2019/7/29/8934430/defensive-backs-week-antoine-brooks-profile-stats-bio|title=Antoine Brooks Jr. will lead Maryland football's defense at a new position|first=Justin|last=Fitzgerald|website=TestudoTimes.com|publisher=[[SB Nation]]|date=July 29, 2019|access-date=April 6, 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/news/terrapins-insider/wp/2018/09/07/for-antoine-brooks-jr-his-family-and-the-terps-smiles-tears-joy-a-lot-of-mixed-emotions/|title=For Antoine Brooks Jr., his family and the Terps, 'smiles, tears, joy, a lot of mixed emotions'|newspaper=The Washington Post|date=September 7, 2018|access-date=April 6, 2020}}</ref> As a junior, Brooks was Maryland's third leading tackler with 68 and led the team with 9.5 tackles for loss with 2.5 sacks, three passes defended and an interception and was named second-team All-Big Ten by the league's coaches.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.baltimoresun.com/sports/terps/bs-sp-maryland-football-antoine-brooks-20191019-k35mgecl5rcnnja2izf6llt7f4-story.html|title=No quit in Maryland safety Antoine Brooks Jr. four years ===Los Angeles Rams===
On September 4, 2021, Brooks was signed to the [[Los Angeles Rams]] practice squad. He was promoted to the active roster on November 9.<ref>{{Cite web |last=DaSilva |first=Cameron |date=November 10, 2021 |title=Rams sign DB Antoine Brooks Jr. to roster, bring back Jonah Williams on practice squad |url=https://theramswire.usatoday.com/2021/11/10/rams-roster-moves-antoine-brooks-jonah-williams/ |access-date=2023-03-25 |website=TheRamsWire |publisher=USA Today}}</ref> He was waived on January 29, 2022, and re-signed to the practice squad. Brooks won [[Super Bowl LVI]] when the Rams defeated the [[Cincinnati Bengals]].<ref>{{cite web|title= LA Rams defeat Cincinnati Bengals to win Super Bowl 2022|url=https://nypost.com/2022/02/13/la-rams-defeat-cincinnati-bengals-to-win-super-bowl-2022/|author=Schwartz, Paul|website=nypost.com|date=February 13, 2021}}</ref>

On February 15, 2022, Brooks signed a reserve/future contract with the Rams.<ref>{{cite web|title=Rams Sign 12 Players to a Reserve/Future Contract|url=https://www.si.com/nfl/rams/news/rams-super-bowl-lvi-sign-12-players-reserve-future-contract-nfl-offseason|author=Cothrel, Nicholas|website=sportsillustrated.com|date=February 15, 2022}}</ref> He was waived on May 4.

=== Seattle Sea Dragons ===
On November 17, 2022, Brooks was drafted by the [[Seattle Sea Dragons]] of the [[XFL (2020)|XFL]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-11-18 |title=Rosters for all eight XFL teams: Full draft results and where Vic Beasley, Martavis Bryant landed |url=https://www.espn.com/xfl/story/_/id/35053464/xfl-draft-results-2023-full-rosters-eight-teams-vic-beasley-martavis-bryant-picks |access-date=2022-12-30 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}}</ref> The Sea Dragons folded when the XFL and [[United States Football League (2022)|United States Football League]] merged to create the [[United Football League (2024)|United Football League]] (UFL).<ref>{{Cite web |last=Seifert |first=Kevin |date=January 1, 2024 |title=Newly formed United Football League sets 8 markets, tabs coaches |url=https://www.espn.com/xfl/story/_/id/39222541/newly-formed-united-football-league-sets-8-markets-tabs-coaches |access-date=January 15, 2024 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref>

=== Memphis Showboats ===
On January 15, 2024, Brooks was selected by the [[Memphis Showboats (2022)|Memphis Showboats]] in the 12th round of the Super Draft portion of the [[2024 UFL dispersal draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Rachuk |first=Stephan |date=2024-01-15 |title=2024 United Football League (UFL) Super Draft Tracker |url=https://pfnewsroom.com/news/2024-united-football-league-ufl-super-draft-tracker/ |access-date=2024-01-15 |website=Pro Football Newsroom |language=en-US}}</ref> He signed with the team on January 30.<ref>{{Cite news |title=UFL Player Transactions - Tuesday January 30, 2024. |url=https://uflboard.com/news/ufl-player-transactions-tuesday-january-30-2024/ |website=UFLBoard.com |date=January 30, 2024 |access-date=January 31, 2024}}</ref> Brooks was released on March 10.<ref>{{Cite news |title=UFL Teams Set their Training Camp Rosters to 58 |url=https://uflboard.com/news/ufl-teams-set-their-training-camp-rosters-to-58/ |website=UFLBoard.com |date=March 10, 2024 |access-date=March 10, 2024}}</ref>

=== Saskatchewan Roughriders ===
On April 11, 2024, Brooks signed with the [[Saskatchewan Roughriders]] of the [[Canadian Football League]] (CFL).<ref>{{Cite web |title=Transactions - Football Player Trades and Signings |url=https://www.cfl.ca/transactions/ |access-date=2024-04-12 |website=CFL.ca |language=en}}</ref>

'''Antoine Green''' (born November 15, 1999) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[wide receiver]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[North Carolina Tar Heels football|North Carolina Tar Heels]].

==College career==
As a [[freshman]] at [[North Carolina Tar Heels football|North Carolina]] in [[2018 North Carolina Tar Heels football team|2018]], Green appeared in five games at wide receiver and on special teams, and posted four receptions for 45 yards. On October 20, 2018, he suffered a season-ending leg injury in an overtime loss to [[2018 Syracuse Orange football team|Syracuse]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Alexander |first=Jonathan M. |date=October 23, 2018 |title=After gruesome injury, UNC freshman WR Antoine Green is doing well, says Larry Fedora |url=https://www.newsobserver.com/sports/article220487415.html |access-date=April 29, 2023 |newspaper=[[The News & Observer]]}}</ref> As a [[sophomore]] in [[2019 North Carolina Tar Heels football team|2019]], he appeared in 10 games and made two starts at wide receiver, posting eight receptions for 217 yards and two touchdowns. As a [[Junior (education year)|junior]] in [[2020 North Carolina Tar Heels football team|2020]], Green appeared in 11 games, and made one start at wide receiver and on special teams.<ref name="Bio">{{cite web|url=https://goheels.com/sports/football/roster/antoine-green/23330 |title=Antoine Green Bio |website=goheels.com |access-date=April 29, 2023}}</ref>

As a [[Senior (education)|senior]] in [[2021 North Carolina Tar Heels football team|2021]], he started all 13 games at wide receiver, and ranked second on the team in receptions (31), receiving yards (612) and receiving touchdowns (5). He ranked second in the [[Atlantic Coast Conference]] (ACC), and 12th nationally, averaging 19.7 yards per reception.<ref name="Bio"/>

He suffered a collarbone injury in a preseason scrimmage and missed the first three games of the season.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://tarheelswire.usatoday.com/2022/11/21/unc-wide-receiver-antoine-green-back-at-practice-this-week/ |title=UNC wide receiver Antoine Green back at practice this week |newspaper=[[USA Today]] |first=Alec |last=Laslez |date=November 21, 2022 |access-date=April 29, 2023}}</ref> As a fifth-year senior in [[2022 North Carolina Tar Heels football team|2022]], he appeared in nine games, and made eight starts at wide receiver, and ranked second on the team in receptions (43), yards receiving (798), receiving touchdowns (7) and receiving yards per game (88.67).<ref name="Bio"/> Following the season he was named third-team [[2022 Atlantic Coast Conference football season#All Conference Teams|All-ACC]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://theacc.com/news/2022/11/29/athlete-awards-clemson-leads-with-12-selection-to-all-acc-football-teams.aspx |title=Clemson Leads With 12 Selection to All-ACC Football Teams |website=theacc.com |publisher=[[Atlantic Coast Conference]] |date=November 30, 2022 |access-date=April 29, 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.detroitlions.com/news/lions-draft-wide-receiver-antoine-green |title=Lions draft wide receiver Antoine Green |website=detroitlions.com |first=Tim |last=Twentyman |date=April 29, 2023 |access-date=April 29, 2023}}</ref>
